##  Collaborations / Collections 
**Project to digitize the memory of Lebanese and Syrian immigration to Latin America**
The project aims at digitizing, among others, newspapers, magazines, old books, photographs, and documents produced by the Lebanese and Syrian communities, specifically in Latin America since the 19th century, during the great immigration wave. USEK’s pioneering role consists of starting to form studios to digitize the relevant material to be found in the region and store it within USEK’s digital library in Lebanon, thereby making research easier for scholars and other stakeholders. 
Two agreements have been signed so far with digital studios in two countries:
**Argentina** – 2016 Agreement
USEK –  _Fundación Ninawa Daher_ (Ninawa Daher Foundation), Buenos Aires. 
Founder and President: Alicia Daher. 
([http://www.diariosiriolibanes.com.ar/Sociedad/Instituciones/Proyecto-de-conservaci%C3%B3n-del-patrimonio-Liban%C3%A9s](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.diariosiriolibanes.com.ar%2FSociedad%2FInstituciones%2FProyecto-de-conservaci%25C3%25B3n-del-patrimonio-Liban%25C3%25A9s&data=04%7C01%7Cjenniferberry%40usek.edu.lb%7C556fc5ace16f4547a34508d9f21f6a2a%7C06d0a2c459b94cf8a36a9190f22cd1f6%7C0%7C0%7C637807039002024294%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000&sdata=52q29juXM%2BeV6bBDF9OnyRz%2Fe0YuSwUMUKotIqY7cms%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: http://www.diariosiriolibanes.com.ar/Sociedad/Instituciones/Proyecto-de-conservaci%C3%B3n-del-patrimonio-Liban%C3%A9s. Click or tap if you trust this link.")) 
**Brazil** – 2018 Agreement 
USEK – [_Câmara de Comércio Árabe-Brasileira_ (Arab-Brazilian Chamber of Commerce)](https://www.ccab.org.br/)
Former president: Rubens Hannun. Current president: Brazilian diplomat Osmar Chohfi
CCAB Cultural Sector: Silvia Antibas, director. Heloisa Abreu Dib Julien, coordinator. Mirna Adel Nasser, digitization.
[https://anba.com.br/en/project-immigration-set-launch-arab-chamber/](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fanba.com.br%2Fen%2Fproject-immigration-set-launch-arab-chamber%2F&data=04%7C01%7Cjenniferberry%40usek.edu.lb%7C556fc5ace16f4547a34508d9f21f6a2a%7C06d0a2c459b94cf8a36a9190f22cd1f6%7C0%7C0%7C637807039002024294%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000&sdata=OvAqFnF%2Bf4jQErBIC3f%2BRcnzX460XlrrrQ7GLFWTp%2BI%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://anba.com.br/en/project-immigration-set-launch-arab-chamber/. Click or tap if you trust this link.")
[https://anba.com.br/projeto-sobre-imigracao-sera-lancado-na-camara-arabe/](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fanba.com.br%2Fprojeto-sobre-imigracao-sera-lancado-na-camara-arabe%2F&data=04%7C01%7Cjenniferberry%40usek.edu.lb%7C556fc5ace16f4547a34508d9f21f6a2a%7C06d0a2c459b94cf8a36a9190f22cd1f6%7C0%7C0%7C637807039002024294%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000&sdata=Y5v7Dwy4AC6kyBAjQCQ%2F6PuKhedsFvwjEiuFfnUvsr0%3D&reserved=0 "Original URL: https://anba.com.br/projeto-sobre-imigracao-sera-lancado-na-camara-arabe/. Click or tap if you trust this link.")
Working in coordination with USEK’s Library and Latin American Studies and Cultures Center (CECAL) , the three partners and their teams are undertaking research on collections (at the level of institutions, libraries, private individuals, etc.) to locate magazines, newspapers, and other publications in Arabic, Spanish, and Portuguese in Latin American countries with the purpose of rebuilding and preserving these collections in immigration memory. 
The first newspaper established by Lebanese immigrants in Latin America was _Al-Fayha_ , published in 1894 in Campinas, São Paulo and owned by Salim Balech. Historian Philippe Hitti estimates at 166 the number of Arabic-language newspapers and magazines published in Latin America in 1950 (95 in Brazil, 58 in Argentina, 8 in Chile, 3 in Cuba, and one in Uruguay). 
In addition to our digitization studios in two countries, we are conducting research on collections in other Latin American countries. The digitized collections are available in the library catalog.
**The below table lists the Institutions, Libraries, and individuals etc. that have authorized us to digitize their own collections or the collections of Lebanese and Syrian emigrants dating back to the 19th Century onward.**

# USEK Robotics
USEK Robotics spans a series of multidisciplinary labs which pursue innovative research in human-robot interaction, human-robot collaboration, assistive technology, long-term automation, and robot ethics. 
##### Join USEK Robotics and embark on a journey for designing the robots of tomorrow.
Send us an email to know more
![USEK](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/files/20230812_11-57-44_usek-pepper-standing-001.png)
## Human-Robot Interaction
_Want to design a Socially Interactive Robot?_
At the Human-Robot Interaction Lab of USEK Robotics, we focus on building behavioural modals for **socially interactive robots** which are meant to interact with humans in various contexts such as education, assistive technology, healthcare and entertainment.   
The research areas include **Human-Robot Interaction** (HRI), **Artificial Intelligence** (AI) and **Ethics** in the (social) robotics field.
![USEK](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/files/20231028_13-08-31_go1-3dlidar.png)
## Robot Long-term Autonomy
_How about designing autonomous robots?_
At **USEK Robotics** we investigate new methods for enabling **autonomy of mobile robots** (e.g., quadrupeds). The focus is on improving the robot's abilities by augmenting it with Lidars and robotic arms to perform service tasks ranging from **manipulating objects** (e.g., grasping), **navigating** the environment and **collaborating with humans** when deployed in the wild (e.g., patrol inspections, 3D mapping, and material transportation).   
Students will be exposed to various research areas covering **artificial intelligence, computer vision, machine learning** and other.
## Wanna know more about Robotics and AI?
Are you an undergraduate or graduate student in the fields of Computer/Electrical/Biomedical Engineering or Computer Science with a very good academic record? Are you interested in the robotics and artificial intelligence fields? 
Send us an email to know more
![USEK](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/files/20231028_20-28-54_ai-001.png)
## Our Robots
Humanoids and Quadruped Robots
![](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/files/20231028_12-14-03_pepper-003.png)
### Pepper Robot
Pepper is a social humanoid robot which is optimized for human interactions. It has many capabilities to allow engaging and interacting with people through speech and its tablet screen.   
The Pepper robot will be used by our students to investigate the social skills needed for designing interactive human-robot applications meant for various settings such as education, healthcare and entertainment.
![](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/files/20231028_11-53-05_furhat-face.jpg)
### Furhat Robot
The Furhat Robot (designed by Furhat Robotics) utilizes the latest advancements in technology and computer vision. It has a customizable appearance and life-like expressiveness to allow a wide range of research and development opportunities.   
The capabilities of the Furhat robot will be exploited by our students to design new social skills and allow Furhat to interact smoothly with people.
![](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/files/20231028_13-15-02_go1-2dlidar.png)
### Go1 Quadruped Robot
Go1 is a quadruped robot used for research and development of autonomous systems. It has a super sensory system (including depth cameras and hypersonic sensors) along with powerful on-board AI capabilities.   
The Go1 robot can be equipped with 2D/3D/4D lidars and a robotic arm to allow students explore and investigate new ways of interacting and collaborating with robots (e.g., manipulating objects, navigating and exploring the environment). 
![](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/files/20231028_13-38-54_aliengo-with-arm.jpg)
### AlienGo Quadruped Robot
AlienGo is a quadruped industrial robot used for research and development of autonomous systems. It has a long endurance (compared to Go1) as well as a super sensory system (including depth cameras and hypersonic sensors) and powerful on-board AI capabilities. Further, AlienGo has strong multi-terrain adaptability which allows it to operate stably on rugged environment (e.g., gravel and grassland).   
The AlienGo robot can also be equipped with 2D/3D/4D lidars and an advanced Z1 robotic arm to allow students explore and investigate new ways of interacting and collaborating with robots (e.g., manipulating objects, navigating and exploring the environment).

## [Chessmen and Checkmate: Playing with Fate](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Chessmen-and-Checkmate-Playing-with-Fate)
by Elham Abdallah on April 11th, 2025 | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Chessmen-and-Checkmate-Playing-with-Fate#comments)  

![](https://d2jv02qf7xgjwx.cloudfront.net/accounts/148280/images/1.JPG)
This exquisite chess set, known as the **Lewis Chessmen** , is a replica from the British Library. The original pieces, discovered in 1831 on the Isle of Lewis in Scotland, were believed to have been carved in Trondheim, Norway, between 1150 and 1200. Made from walrus ivory and whale tooth, _luxury materials at the time_ , their detailed carvings reflect Norwegian artistic traditions. Today, the chessmen are famous for their expressive faces and roles, **kings** , **queens** , **bishops** , **knights** , and **warders** , each evoking a frozen moment of strategic tension.
In reflecting on the meaning embedded in these chess pieces, we were reminded of another work shaped by strategy and suspense: **Checkmate,** a painting by Friedrich Moritz August Retzsch. 
![](https://d2jv02qf7xgjwx.cloudfront.net/accounts/148280/images/checkmate-painting.jpg)
The painting portrays a dramatic chess match between a **man** and **satan**. At first glance, **satan appears to be winning** and the **man looks defeated** , but closer analysis reveals that **a winning move still exists**. This interpretation transforms the painting into a metaphor not only for perception and critical thinking, but for the larger **game of life and death**.
By displaying the Lewis Chessmen to mirror the composition in Checkmate, we reflect on how both artifacts, _one a historical object_ , the _other a conceptual artwork_ , explore enduring themes of strategy, conflict, uncertainty, and the possibility of redemption. Each reminds us that even in the darkest moments, the next move might change everything.
**References:**
Phago, P. (2023). _Decoding “Checkmate”, and how it relates to life_. <https://pratikphago.medium.com/decoding-checkmate-and-how-it-relates-to-life-90fa4b93d853>
_The Queen's Gambit: how the Lewis Chessmen won the world over, British Museum_. Retrieved Feb 19, 2025, from <https://www.britishmuseum.org/blog/queens-gambit-how-lewis-chessmen-won-world-over>

## ["Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers)
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.

## [The USEK Library Partners with the British Library to Digitize Endangered Historical Newspapers in the Middle East (1895-1950)](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library)
by Elham Abdallah on March 13th, 2023 in [Archives](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200095), [British Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225150), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Digitization](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225155), [EAP1434](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225149), [Endangered Archives Programme](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225151), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [History](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144974), [Identity Crisis](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225153), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Metadata](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225156), [Middle Eastern Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=202255), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

## [فارس خيرالله اسطفان](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/95602)
by Carlos Younes on April 13th, 2022 | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/95602#comments)  

في زمن الألام والقيامة نستذكر صديق المكتبة العامة في جامعة الروح القدس – الكسليك، إبن بلدة غوسطا المرحوم فارس خيرالله اسطفان الذي غادرنا الى بيت الأب السماوي في 6 نيسان 2022.
في مثل هذا اليوم من العام 2020 وهب المرحوم فارس اسطفان أرشيف جريدة الهدى النيويوركية الى المكتبة العامة في جامعة الروح القدس – الكسليك، ليكون هذا الأرشيف بمتناول الباحثين والطلاب في دراساتهم البحثية.
مع الاشارة الى أن جريدة الهدى هي من أعرق الصحف المهجرية الناطقة باللغة العربية، وقد لعبت دوراً هامأ في دنيا الإغتراب، وكانت الصوت الحر للبنان واللبنانيين في المهجر خاصة في زمن الحرب العالمية الأولى والمجاعة.
بعد ان انتقال ملكيتها في أوائل السبعينات الى فارس اسطفان تحول دار " الهدى" الى ملتقى التف حواليه كل من أحب وخاف على الوطن الجريح، خاصة خلال الحرب الأهلية التي عصفت بلبنان واللبنانيين، فظلت الصوت اللبناني الصارخ للمغتربين والمنتشرين الى جانب جريدة Lebanese American Journal التي تصدر باللغة الأنكليزية.
مع غياب فارس اسطفان في غوسطا غابت صورة لبنان بشجاعته ووطنيته وكرمه ونبله، وغاب فارس الاغتراب والموقف والشهامة والأخلاق، لكن ذكراه ستبقى خالدة من خلال الدراسات والأبحاث التي ستستند الى أرشيفه المحفوط بعناية في مكتبة جامعة الروح القدس - الكسليك.

## [Partnership between USEK Library and Moise Khayrallah Center: Arabic OCR](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR)
by Elham Abdallah on April 4th, 2022 in [Diaspora](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213563), [Latin America](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213562), [Lebanese Immigrants](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213564), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/ARABIC_OCR_LIBRARY1__002_.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce its cooperation with Moise Khayrallah Center in USA aimed at implementing the Arabic OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology to the digital periodicals from the Latin American collection housed at the USEK Library. These periodicals were written in Arabic and published in Latin America by Lebanese immigrants, dating back to the 19th century, era of the great immigration wave, onwards.
This partnership is part of the arabicarchives.org project initiated by Khayrallah Center, which collects the early Arab immigrants’ archives that have left remarkable legacy in North and South America. These records were not accessible because they were dispersed and stored in disparate locations, and hence not digitally searchable. Consequently, the Center has created a completely searchable database of these publications by developing Arabic OCR technology to render the digitized images of these history pages into searchable text. 
The objectives of this collaboration are to contribute to scholarly research, explore a heritage that spans years and tells the stories of Lebanese/Arab pioneers, and expand non-English content on the web. 
Accordingly, our digital periodicals from the Latin American collection will be fully searchable, allowing users to easily search their content by keyword. 
_“We at USEK Library, entrusted with this legacy, are proud to join this remarkable initiative, to bring our treasures and efforts in support of the expertise of Khayrallah Center to achieve this worthy goal”_ , said Fr. Joseph Moukarzel, USEK Library Director.
_“Joining this partnership allows us to share our collection with scholars, researchers and public worldwide, a step forward in keeping with our commitment to discoverability and to the growth of our renowned collections”_ , added Fr. Moukarzel.
_“_ _The Khayrallah Center is delighted and privileged to collaborate with USEK Library, one of the premiere archives in the world for Lebanese history. This partnership will add a treasure trove of periodicals to our Arabic database and give researchers and the general public unprecedented access to a wealth of historical literature about Lebanese migration to South America. We regard this as the first step in a very important partnership between NC State University and USEK."_ stated Dr. Akram Khater, Director of Moise Khayrallah Center.

## [The Book of the Psalms of David, King and Prophet, 1610](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610)
by Joseph Moukarzel on May 22nd, 2021 in [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Maronite](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200349), [Ottoman Empire](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200100), [Psalms](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201294), [Special Collections](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200094) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610#comments)  

![alt="Book of Psalms"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/281549/images/May_post6.png)
**The Book of the Psalms of David, King and Prophet, 1610**
_**[Ktobo d-mazmouré d-David malko wa-nbiyo]**_
The  _Book of Psalms_ was printed in the monastery of Saint Anthony of Qozhaya in 1610. Since it is the first book ever printed in the Eastern part of the Ottoman Empire, it is considered as one of the most distinguished works in the history of typography.
In 1485, the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II issued a decree banning all forms of printing in the Empire, and this prohibition was reinforced by Sultan Selim I in 1515. The supposed purpose was to safeguard the contents of Islamic religious books from being modified in the process of printing. However, some researchers believe that the real motivation was to control the work of calligraphers and painters, and to ensure that Istanbul benefited financially. This ban remained in force until the establishment of the first Ottoman printing press in Istanbul in 1727 which printed only in Arabic and Turkish.
The Christian minorities living in the eastern part of the Ottoman Empire were unaware of the printing process during the majority of the 16th century. The first published work seen by the Maronites was a book on Christian catechism in Garshuni, printed in Rome in 1580. In this same year, it was brought to Mount Lebanon by the papal legate Giovanni Battista Eliano, who distributed it to the members of the Synod of Qanoubine. Eliano also distributed another book he translated himself from Latin into Arabic (printed in Garshuni, 1580). It was entitled  _Creed of the Catholic Faith_ , approved by the Council of Trent, and known as the  _Creed of Pope Pius IV_.
However, this development of typography was not paralleled in the Middle East. Although Stefano Evodio Assemani recorded in the catalogue of the Bilblioteca Medicea Laurenziana (Florence - Italy), that the  _Book of Psalms_ was printed in the Qozhaya monastery in 1585, this statement remains questionable, since there is no physical evidence of the existence of this edition in any library. Furthermore, the papal legate Girolamo Dandini noted, during his apostolical visit to the Maronites in 1596, that there were no printing presses in the region. Therefore, it can be concluded that the first book in the eastern part of the Ottoman Empire was this Syriac-Garshuni  _Book of Psalms,_ printed at Qozhaya monastery in 1610.
Researchers tend to believe, without any reliable sources, that Sarkis, ater named Archbishop of Damascus, purchased printing tools from a city in Italy and carried them back to Mount Lebanon after the election of Patriarch Makhlouf (circa 1609). It is important to mention that since printing presses at that time were made of wood, and required great dexterity and expertise, the printing of the  _Book of Psalms_ was not completed before November 10th, 1610, as is written in the colophon at the end of the book. However, the fact that this book was the only one printed at that time raises many questions such as: why other books were not printed, what happened to the printing press or even if the printing press was dismantled. The relevant historical sources do not delve into this topic at all, and most of them actually ignore the existence of this printing press. For these reasons, we wonder whether the  _Book of Psalms_ was only printed in a limited number of copies before the printing press was dismantled.
The  _Book of Psalms_ is made up of 268 pages and uses Syriac letters for pagination (except for the first eight pages which were not paginated). The psalm verses are not numbered but divided into groups of five, with a number placed in the margin to mark each of these groups.
We still do not know exactly how many copies were printed and distributed. All we can confirm is that a German traveler bought one copy in Tripoli in 1611. Currently we have tracked six copies in various public and private libraries: National Library of France, the Saint Geneviève Library in Paris, the Staatsbibliothek in Nürnberg (Germany), the Herzog August Bibliothek, in Wolfenbüttel (Germany), the Saint Joseph University Library in Beirut and lastly the Holy Spirit University Library of Kaslik (Lebanon).

## [Map of Beirut (Beyrouth), 1922](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Map-of-Beirut-1922)
by Carlos Younes on April 19th, 2021 in [Beirut](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200344), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Map-of-Beirut-1922#comments)  

![alt="map of beirut 1922"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Map_Beyrouth_1922.jpg)
The map of Beirut was drawn by the cadastral office of the French Army of the Levant in February 1922, at a scale of 1/10,000.
Highlighted in red are residences, institutions and populated areas at the time, in addition to bridges and street names, the tramway line, the hippodrome, and agricultural lands the majority of which were planted with vineyards, berries and cactus.
We also see on the map some landmarks that no longer exist, namely:
**Place des Canons:** Currently known as the Martyrs’ Square, it was called at the time as the Cannons’ Square, in reference to the cannons that were installed therein to protect Beirut against naval invasions.
During World War I, Jamal Pasha executed death sentences in the square for an elite of Lebanese and Syrian intellectuals, and since then it was known as the Martyrs’ Square. In 1937, May 6 was declared as the Martyrs’ Day in honor of their memory and to pay tribute to their pure souls.
**The Petit Serail:** It was called the _Petit Serail_ (literally the ‘small serail’) to distinguish it from the Grand Serail; it was built on the northern side of the Cannons’ Square (now opposite the _Le Gray_ Hotel), and it was inaugurated in 1884 as the seat of the governor of Beirut, then the seat of the French rulers, and finally the seat of the Presidency of the Republic.
The most powerful image in the memory of the Lebanese is the one that represents the demonstrators on the morning of November 22, 1943, climbing the roof of the Serail to raise the new Lebanese flag before the return of President Bechara El-Khoury along with the men of independence to the _Petit Serail_ after being arrested in the citadel of Rashaya.
In order to expand the Martyrs' Square, the Grand Serail was demolished in 1950.

## [Letter from the heirs of Emir Fares Chehab : Titanic victim](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab)
by Carlos Younes on April 14th, 2021 in [Emir Fares Chehab](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201996), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Titanic Sank](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201994), [Titanic Victim](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201995) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/titanic.png)
**Storied @ USEK Library**
On the 109th anniversary of the sinking of the Titanic, there are still many conflicting opinions about the exact number of Lebanese victims who drowned on that tragic day in April 1912.
Some say that the official number of Lebanese victims is 85, while others claim that the number is considerably higher and can be up to 125, or maybe even more. This discrepancy in numbers is because the nationality of the victims is missing, and many names were incorrectly registered. 
The Lebanese who sailed on the “unsinkable ship” are mostly third-class passengers, who were attempting to flee persecution and poverty in their home country, and dream of a better tomorrow in the country of freedom. They were originally from: Bint Jbeil, Tebnine, Sereel, Kfarmechki, Beirut, Kfaraabida, Zgharta, Kfardlaqos, Tripoli, ‘Ibrin, Hardine (the village that lost 11 of its residents), Kfarzghab, Fghal, Choueir, Al-Hakur, Toula, Bkassine, Hadath, Zahle, Tahoum, and Al-Faqha .
During our search in the Ottoman archives in Istanbul, and among the documents related to the Titanic, we found a letter signed by the heirs of Prince Fares Chehab, one of the ship’s victims from the village of Hadath. The heirs include his wife Hind Chehab, his mother Marwa Chehab, and his sister Helen Chehab; they addressed the letter to the Emergency Committee on June 11, 1912, through the Turkish Consul in London, to claim compensation following the death of their devisor on the Titanic.
It is said about Prince Fares Chehab that while the ship was sinking, he quietly grabbed his _oud_ and played a song "Be strong, young fellowmen. It is a shame to die without _dabke_ and songs”.
في الذكرى التاسعة بعد المئة لغرق سفينة التايتانيك، لا تزال الآراء متضاربة حول العدد الفعلي للضحايا اللبنانيين الذين قضوا غرقًا في ذلك اليوم المشؤوم من شهر نيسان 1912.
يذكر البعض أنَّ العدد الرسمي للضحايا اللبنانيين هو 85 شخصًا، فيما يذكر البعض الآخر إنَّ الرقم أعلى وقد يصل إلى 125 شخصًا وربما أكثر. ويعود هذا التفاوت في الأرقام إلى عدم ذكر جنسيات الضحايا والأخطاء المرتكبة خلال إجراءات التسجيل لكثير من الأسماء.
كانت غالبيّة اللبنانيين الذين أبحروا في السفينة التي "لا تغرق ولا تحرق" من ركاب الدرجة الثالثة، هربًا من الاضطهاد والفقر في بلدهم الأم وحلماً بغدٍ أفضل في بلد الحرية. وهم من بلدات: بنت جبيل، تبنين، سرعل، كفرمشكي، بيروت، كفرعبيدا، زغرتا، كفردلاقوس، طرابلس، عبرين، حردين (القرية التي خسرت 11 من أبنائها)، كفرصغاب، فغال، الشوير، الحاكور، تولا، بكاسين، الحدث، زحلة، تحوم، والفاكهة.
خلال بحثنا في الأرشيف العثماني في اسطنبول، ومن ضمن الوثائق المتعلقة بسفينة التايتانك، عثرنا على رسالة موقّعة من ورثة الأمير فارس شهاب، أحد ضحايا السفينة من قرية الحدث، وهم زوجته هند شهاب، ووالدته مروه شهاب، وشقيقته هيلين شهاب، موجهة إلى لجنة الطوارئ بتاريخ 11 حزيران 1912، من خلال القنصل التركي في لندن، طالبين التعويض عليهم جراء وفاة مورثهم في باخرة التايتانيك.
ويُروى عن الأمير فارس شهاب أنه أثناء غرق السفينة، أخذ عوده بكل رباطة جأش وعزف عليه أغنية "شدّوا الهمة يا شباب، عيب نموت بدون دبكة وأغاني".

## [USEK Library Services : COVID-19 Experience](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/usek-library-services-covid19-experience)
by Elham Abdallah on March 23rd, 2021 in [COVID-19](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201293), [Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144980), [Library Services](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201292) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/usek-library-services-covid19-experience#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/salle.jpg)
In early March 2020, COVID-19 blindsided academic institutions all over the world. With little time to plan, we suspended our library facilities for the safety of our users and employees and moved to **remote services** only. Due dates for all outstanding printed material were extended indefinitely and overdue fines waived.
Thankfully, our **electronic resources** , **research tools** , **off-campus access service** and **website** have served us well during this transition. For **print-only materials** or library holdings, we created two new services for our users:![alt="photos of drive thru and drop box"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/drive_drob.png)
**Drive-thru Service :** whereUSEK members can request any book online via the Library Catalog and pick it up from the University’s main gate. 
**Chapter Scanning Service :** As the US Fair Use & Emergency Remote Teaching and Research copyright law does not apply in the context of the Lebanese copyright law, we created the Scanning Chapter Service for our students, scanning chapters or sections of material and sending them to the user via email or Article Exchange.
![alt="photo of a scanner"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/scan.jpg)Within weeks of closure, the Library managed to roll out **Remote Research Help Services** including**WhatsApp calls, online chat** with extended hours, **online research consultations**(one-on-one appointments),**online training sessions**(RefWorks, APA, Electronic Resources access, etc.),**e-conferences** through Microsoft Teams, etc. and **research webinars** organized by database providers.
Recognizing the need to stay connected to our users, our reference librarians have been coming up with daily **tricks** and **tips** , **handouts** , and **tutorials** for the community, posting them on social media and sending them by email. They have produced **research guides** to provide targeted information on specific topics and tools to help users in their research process. They also created a new webpage on the library website for a list of free **Covid-19 library resources**.![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/ask_us.jpg)
Our **Document Delivery Service** has been an added value during this period. It allows us to order articles and chapters that are not available in the library collection through our partners in Lebanon and abroad at zero cost. This service is the result of USEK Library efforts to facilitate the development of collaborations with national and international consortia and organizations. 
The USEK Library was the first Academic Library in Lebanon to resume its activities on campus [in a phased manner](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/usek-library-lockdown-exit-strategy/resuming-activities-phases) with effect from May 2020. It has implemented robust **safety measures** to prevent the spread of COVID-19 on its premises. All measures taken for the phased activity were based on the WHO recommendations and the "[COVID-19 and the Global Library Field](https://www.ifla.org/covid-19-and-libraries)" published by IFLA and were announced to users through the following libguide: [https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/usek-library-lockdown-exit-strategy/lockdown-exit-strategy](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/usek-library-lockdown-exit-strategy/lockdown-exit-strategy)
**USEK Library Roadmap**
As it is too early to predict the end of COVID-19, we have drawn a strategic roadmap to allow us to continue our library services under the “new normal” and explore all the opportunities and possibilities for developing even better services for our users. 
We are starting with the following:
• Moodle Learning System
  * Integrating USEK Library Catalog with Moodle
  * Embedding a Librarian into Moodle Course
  * Creating a library information block


• Creating additional subject research guides 
• Creating a YouTube channel for Library orientation sessions, workshops, training, and tutorials
• E-course reserve, etc.

## [The Maronite Evangeliary, 1673](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/maronite-evangeliary-1673)
by Essine Gemayel on March 18th, 2021 in [Evangeliary](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201291), [Manuscripts](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200093), [Maronite](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200349) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/maronite-evangeliary-1673#comments)  

![alt="photos from the maronite gospel"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/collage_with_cross-reused.png)
Did you know that the USEK Library holds thousands of [significant manuscripts, incunables and rare books](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/special-collections)? Its [Conservation and Restoration Center](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/crc)[ ](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/crc)oversees the preservation of these priceless heritage collections.
Today, we are featuring one of the most remarkable manuscripts of the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM): 
**_, 1673_**
**_[Qira’at min Al-ānjīl Al -Araba‘a, 1673_ _]_**
The Maronite Evangeliary, written in Aleppo (Syria) contains a Syriac-Garshuni Gospel of the 17th century (1673, 354 ff, 33 x 23 x 10 cm), including a text in two columns (23 lines per column). The Gospels are divided according to the days and feasts of the Maronite liturgical year.
This manuscript was copied and illuminated by the hand of Deacon Rizk – son of Pierre from the Marc family, the student of Bishop Gibrael (f.351v) – following the request of Bishop Gibrael Al Blouzani for the Monastery of Our Lady of Tamich, Lebanon. 
Three miniatures representing the evangelists St. Mark, St. Luke and St. John illuminate this manuscript, and several portals mounted with a cross embellish the beginning of each Gospel.
Throughout the pages, we find several details, filled with decorative Syriac letters, creating sometimes the shape of a cross. 
This manuscript still retains its original full-leather binding.
For more details about the restoration of this manuscript, visit the following page: [https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/crc/step-by-step](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/crc/step-by-step)

#  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/new-students#welcome-to-the-holy-spirit-university-of-kaslik) Welcome to the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik ![🎓](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/_assets/svg/twemoji/1f393.svg)
#  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/new-students#steps-to-follow) Steps to follow 
To facilitate your enrollment at USEK, please follow the following steps:
  

##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/new-students#step-1-activation) ● Step 1: Activation
If you haven’t confirmed your choice yet, please do it no later than **Monday, August 18, 2025**. (kindly check the acceptance email received from the Admission Office)
##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/new-students#step-2-first-payment) ● Step 2: first payment
Starting **Monday, August 4, 2025** , you can **settle the first payment** , amounting to **1,000$ fresh USD** _(including 200 USD in registration fees)._ The first payment must be made at least 48 hours before the orientation session(s).
No payments are accepted on campus. You can use one of the following payment methods:
  * At one of the following **banks** ![🏦](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/_assets/svg/twemoji/1f3e6.svg): **BOB | Byblos | AUDI | BLOM**
  * At any **OMT/BOB Finance** branch or through the **OMT Pay** App.
  * Via the **USEK Online Payment** method on **[MyUSEK](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/)**


> ####  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/new-students#deadlines) Deadlines ![⏳](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/_assets/svg/twemoji/23f3.svg)
> Please bear in mind the following deadlines:  
>  a) `First Payment Settlement`: 2 days prior to the registration period  
>  b) `Registration period`: registration will take place during the orientation session (August 20,21)

* * *
Smart Boards User Guide
* * *
#  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#ideahub-smartboard-connection-projection-guide) 📘 Ideahub Smartboard Connection & Projection Guide
##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#eligibility) 👤 Eligibility
User Type | Connection Methods  
---|---  
Students | Wired HDMI only  
Faculty & Staff | Wired HDMI, Type-C and Wireless (IdeaShare App)  
> Type-C cable to get from the school administration.
* * *
> 🔘 **Before You Begin:**  
>  Make sure the **IdeaHub is powered on** by pressing the **button located at the bottom-right of the smartboard frame**.
> 🔘 **After each use:**  
>  Ensure the **smart pen is properly returned to its magnetic holder** (usually located on the **right and left edge**) after use, to avoid loss or damage.
#  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#projection-methods) 🔧 **Projection Methods**
##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#option-1-wired-hdmi-connection-all-users) 🧷 Option 1: Wired HDMI Connection (All Users)
  * Plug an HDMI cable from your device into the smartboard.
  * Your screen should instantly project.


##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#option-2-wireless-via-ideashare-app-faculty-staff-only) 📡 Option 2: Wireless via IdeaShare App (Faculty & Staff Only)
📲 **Connect your device to the Smartboard Network**
  * On your laptop or mobile:
    * Click the `Wi-Fi` icon.
    * Select the `Smartboard` SSID.
    * Enter your USEK username and password when prompted.


###  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#part-1-device-pairing) Part 1: Device Pairing
  1. ✅ **Ensure the Smartboard Wi-Fi is Connected**
     * Look for the Wi-Fi icon in the top-right corner of the Smartboard.  
![img_5747_2.jpeg](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/applications/smartboard/img_5747_2.jpeg)
     * If not connected, connect to SSID **SmartBoards**.  
![img_5751.jpg](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/applications/smartboard/img_5751.jpg)
     * If prompted to enter credentials, contact the User Support Desk at **it.support@usek.edu.lb** , or visit **C007**.
  2. Download the [IdeaShare App](https://www.huaweicloud.com/intl/en-us/product/ideashare.html).
  3. Choose the version matching your device (Windows, macOS, iOS, Android).
  4. Open the app.
  5. Enter the 6-digit projection code, found:  
![ideashare_app.png](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/applications/smartboard/ideashare_app.png)
     * Next to the Wi-Fi icon (top-right), or
     * In the center of the screen under “Projection Code” (e.g., **XNPX-GBNB**).  
![img_5754.jpg](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/applications/smartboard/img_5754.jpg)


####  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#optional-cast-without-audio) 🔇 Optional: Cast Without Audio
  * Inside the IdeaShare app: 
    * Go to **Settings**.
    * Uncheck **"Cast Audio"** if you prefer to mute the sound coming from the screen during projection.
    * Click **Share** to begin screen projection and **Stop Share** to end it.


* * *
###  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#part-2-after-pairing) 🧩 Part 2: After Pairing
####  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#navigate-to-the-smartboard-main-interface) 🧭 **Navigate to the Smartboard Main Interface**
Once paired, the smartboard will display several options:
  * **Whiteboard** – For drawing and annotation.
  * **Projection** – For screen sharing.  
![img_5745.jpeg](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/applications/smartboard/img_5745.jpeg)


> 🖊️ When using **Projection mode** , if you click on **Annotate** , you can draw on the screen.  
>  Once you're done annotating, tap **Back to Wireless Projection** to continue with your shared screen.
####  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#interactive-screen-features) ✋ **Interactive Screen Features**
🔄 Enable Touch Control on Smartboard
  * Tap the screen on the smartboard.
  * A left-arrow icon appears (bottom-right).
  * Tap the arrow, then select **“Reverse Control”** to enable interaction via the smartboard.  
![img_5759.jpg](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/applications/smartboard/img_5759.jpg)


🔁 Revert Control Back to Your Device
  * Tap the arrow again → a red circle appears, indicating control has returned to your device.  
![img_5755.jpg](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/applications/smartboard/img_5755.jpg)


* * *
#  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#system-controls-additional-features) System Controls & Additional Features
  1. 🔘 **Turning the Smartboard On or Off**
     * Tap the bottom-right corner.
     * Tap the **Power** icon.
     * Select **"Shutdown"** to power off.
  2. 📂 **On-Screen Tools & Apps**
Tap the 9-dot icon on the left or right edge to access:
     * **Home** – Return to home screen.
     * **Microphone** – Toggle on/off (blue = active).
     * **Camera** – Toggle on/off (blue = active). 
       * ⚠️ **Note:** When using the camera for meetings, ensure the physical camera at the **top-center of the smartboard** is manually switched **on** (it can be physically closed or opened).
     * **Annotate** – Write or draw on the screen.
     * **Split Windows** – Divide screen into two.
     * **Windows Mode** – Access built-in Windows environment.
####  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#to-exit-windows-mode) 🔚 To Exit Windows Mode:
     * Tap the **Windows** icon (bottom-left).
     * Click **"Shutdown"** to exit Windows and return to main screen.


* * *
###  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#%EF%B8%8F-troubleshooting-support) 🛠️ Troubleshooting & Support
If the smartboard is unresponsive, or issues arise, **contact the User Support Desk immediately.**
* * *
##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/eits/smartboard#additional-requirements) 💼 Additional Requirements
> 1.**Microsoft Teams** must be signed in using the smartboard’s dedicated account and not your personal USEK credentials.  
>  2.If you are using the **wired screen sharing method** or **no screen sharing method at all** ,  
>  **do not sign into Office 365 or other services with your credentials** , as they may be saved on the system.

* * *
Change your Password
Steps on how to change your password on and off campus
* * *
#  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/change-password#how-to-change-your-password) How to change your password
Passwords are a way to authenticate a user against a system account. It should be strong, secure, and frequently changed. This guide will teach you how to change your USEK account password while making sure you this is a `strong` password.
##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/change-password#create-a-new-password) Create a new password
> **For a better guide and understaning about generating a strong password, please visit[this page](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/generate-passwords)**
For the best security practices, please make sure that your password meets the minimum complexity requirements:
  * Does Not contain the user's 'account name' : first Name, Last Name or ID.
  * Be `ten to fifteen` (10 to 15) characters in length.
  * Contains at least one character from at least three of four sets of characters: 
    * `Capital letters`: A through Z
    * `Small letters`: a through z
    * `Numbers`: 0 through 9
    * `Symbols`: ! _ # $ % ^ & \ *


##  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/change-password#change-your-passowrd) Change your passowrd
###  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/change-password#h-1-to-change-your-password-when-off-campus-from-outside-usek) 1. **To change your password when off-campus (from outside USEK)**
####  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/change-password#using-outlook-online) Using Outlook Online
  * Login to [Outlook online](https://outlook.office365.com) with your current USEK credentials.


  * If you're using Google Chrome on your mobile, you need to select "Request Desktop Site" browser option (by clicking on the three dots ..., bottom right).
  * If you are using Safari Browser on Your IPhone Just Click on the double A icon then click on "Request Desktop Website"  
![whatsapp_image_2023-12-04_at_11.59.51_f612f5f8.jpg](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/whatsapp_image_2023-12-04_at_11.59.51_f612f5f8.jpg)


  * Go to your name tag at the top right of the page and click on it, then click on **View account**


![resetpass1.png](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/service-desk/change-password/resetpass1.png)
  * Click on **Change password**


![resetpass2.png](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/service-desk/change-password/resetpass2.png)
  * Follow the on-screen instructions (you need to enter your current/old password, then input your new password, and confirm it)


###  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/change-password#h-2-to-change-your-password-when-on-campus-from-inside-usek) 2. **To change your password when on-campus (from inside USEK)**
####  [¶](https://wiki.usek.edu.lb/en/service-desk/faq/change-password#using-a-computer) Using a computer
> **USEK Staff and Faculty** : Make sure you are on your domain joined **office computer** before proceeding  
>  **Students** : You need to be connected via [citrix](https://vdi.usek.edu.lb/Desktop/) in order to proceed
  * Press `Ctrl` + `Alt` + `Delete` on your keyboard
  * Click on `Change a password`, and follow the on-screen instructions (you need to enter your current/old password, then input your new password, and confirm it)

You can pass by the service desk office on campus during working hours for a password reset assistance, or
  * by sending an email to it.servicedesk@usek.edu.lb

##  Advancement Office 
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) Advancement Office mission is to serve USEK’s educational mission and strategic goals through partnership and fundraising programs from diverse donors including alumni. Our advancement team shall observe the highest standards of personal and professional conduct.   
  
Therefore, by coordinating closely with alumni relations, securing private financial support, spreading awareness about the institution, and promoting its planned projects, the USEK Advancement Office aims to increase the philanthropic support to allow the university to invest more in financial aid, new education programs, and facilities.  
  
The USEK Advancement Office hopes and vision are supported by the university board of trustees and the Holy Spirit University Foundation members, but it only can be realized by your contributions, so that together we can embark on supporting USEK’s vision and the Lebanese education system.  
  

### Mission
The Advancement Office seeks to serve USEK’s educational and community mission through fundraising programs from existing and potential donors locally and around the globe. Our services shall adhere to accepted professional and ethical standards while maintaining the values of USEK.  
  

### Vision
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik Advancement Office will support the university and its constituents in being among the leading Higher Education institutes in Lebanon and MENA region, as well as meeting international educational standards and helping its students embark on their journey, all by maintaining its core values.

##  Director’s Word 
Greetings,   
As the newly appointed director of the Alumni Relations Office and the Advancement Office at USEK, it is an honor to serve our vibrant community.   
  
Together, we embark on a journey of fostering connections, celebrating accomplishments, and advancing the legacy of our esteemed institution. The bond between alumni and our alma mater is a testament to the enduring spirit that defines USEK.  
  
As an alumna myself, I realize the importance of strengthening ties with our graduates worldwide, driving initiatives and collaborations that propel our university to new heights. I am excited about the transformative impact we can achieve together.  
  
This platform will serve as a hub for updates, events, and opportunities to reconnect. I encourage you to explore, engage in, and be an active part of the USEK family. Your support is instrumental in shaping the future of our alma mater.  
  
Thank you for entrusting me with this responsibility. Here’s to a future filled with shared successes and continued growth.  
  
**Cosette A. El Kamar**

##  Carlos Ghosn at USEK 
Carlos Ghosn serves as Honorary Professor of Global Business Strategies at USEK University in Lebanon. Over the past five years, he has been actively and benevolently engaged in a wide range of support activities and educational initiatives, including executive education programs, startup advisory, and the development of several university-level projects. He also advises the President on matters related to USEK’s growth and development.  
  

[Strategic and Crisis Management Bootcamp with Carlos Ghosn](javascript:;)
This intensive 3-day bootcamp is designed for mid-level managers looking to enhance their leadership skills and accelerate their career growth. Led by the esteemed Carlos Ghosn and other industry experts, this program offers a unique opportunity to engage with real-world case studies and gain invaluable insights into strategic and crisis management. Participants will explore the role of AI in leadership and develop expertise in sustainable management practices, particularly for family-owned businesses. Designed for professionals with at least five years of experience, the program fosters teamwork, leadership, and decision-making through collaborative exercises and expert mentorship.  
  
Gain the skills and confidence to tackle today’s business challenges and take your career to the next level!   
  
**Round 2 - 2026**   
[Know more](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20250911StratigicBootcamp-011010.pdf) | [Apply Now](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/usek-bs-executive-info-202520/new)  
  
**Round 1 - 2025**  
[Know More](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20250204CGBROCHURE-121638.pdf) | [Participants](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20250522BootCampCarlosGhosn-111654.pdf)
[Executive Program in Business Strategies and Performance with Carlos Ghosn](javascript:;)
In the scope of the tridimensional initiative “Moving Forward” launched by USEK and Mr. Carlos Ghosn, the Business School developed a unique world-class executive program targeting senior managers across the MENA region. The curriculum aims to help organizations build a resilient business model while helping develop global leaders.   
  
Organized around 10 modules, this certificate discusses current world business problematics with Mr. Ghosn himself, along with internationally renowned experts, and will be delivered through a combination of online and on-campus attendance options.   
  
It is noteworthy that all proceeds will be directed to the funding of the USEK Skills and Development Center, another program within this initiative.

[New Faculty Orientation](javascript:;)
Each academic year, the Office of the Provost and the Associate Provost for Faculty Affairs organize a welcome session for newly appointed faculty. The session is designed to ensure a smooth integration into the USEK academic community by providing essential information, resources, and support.  
  
The 2025–2026 welcoming session took place on Tuesday, September 2, 2025, from 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., in the Jean El Hawa Auditorium (Building H – 2nd Floor). The event featured presentations by key units, including: 
  * The Office of the Provost.
  * The Information Technology Office.
  * The Learning and Teaching Excellence Center (LTEC).
  * Other academic and administrative support offices.

  
  
The session offered new faculty the opportunity to engage with USEK leadership, ask questions, and gain valuable insights into University policies, teaching tools, and available resources.  
  
**Program**   
11:00 a.m. – Welcome Note – Associate Provost for Faculty Affairs  
11:15 a.m. – Presentations from Offices and Support Units  
12:15 p.m. – Address by the Provost  
12:30 p.m. – Faculty Workload and Related Policies – Associate Provost for Faculty Affairs  
1:00 p.m. – Lunch  
2:00 p.m. – Moodle Training Session  
  
This event reflected USEK’s ongoing commitment to supporting faculty success from day one and fostering a collegial, well-informed academic environment.

[Basic Moodle Session](javascript:;)
An introductory session for instructors new to Moodle. Participants will learn how to navigate the platform, organize course content, upload resources, and set up core activities, such as assignments and quizzes.  
  
Date and time: Wednesday, September 24, from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.  
Audience: Instructors new to Moodle or refreshing foundations  
Duration: 90 minutes  
  
**Description**  
This introductory session is designed for instructors who are new to Moodle or who want to refresh their foundational skills. Participants will explore the essential features of the platform: navigating the interface, creating and organizing course content, uploading resources, and setting up core activities, such as assignments and quizzes. By the end of the session, participants will be able to design a clear, functional course space that supports student engagement and learning.  
  
**Objectives**
  * Navigate Moodle’s interface with confidence.
  * Create and organize course sections
  * Upload and manage files, links, and pages.
  * Set up core activities (assignments, quizzes).
  * Apply simple design practices for student engagement.

  
  
**Outline**  
1. Welcome and context  
2. Getting started with Moodle (navigation, editing)  
3. Building the course structure (sections, labels)  
4. Adding resources (files, pages, links)  
5. Setting up core activities (assignment, quiz)  
6. Hands-on mini-course  
7. Wrap-up & Q&A
[Advanced Moodle Session](javascript:;)
This advanced session is designed for instructors already comfortable with Moodle’s basics. It covers gradebook customization, conditional activities, student progress tracking, integration of external tools, and advanced assessment strategies using question banks and rubrics.  
  
Date and time: Wednesday, October 8, from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m.   
Audience: Instructors comfortable with basics, ready to deepen skills  
Duration: 90 minutes  
  
**Description**  
This session is designed for instructors who are already comfortable with Moodle’s basics and want to expand their expertise. Participants will explore advanced features such as gradebook customization, conditional activities, tracking student progress, and integrating external tools such as H5P. The session also covers advanced assessment strategies, including building and managing question banks and designing effective rubrics. By the end of the session, participants will be equipped to design dynamic, personalized learning environments that make full use of Moodle’s capabilities.  
  
**Objectives**
  * Customize gradebook and grading methods.
  * Design conditional activities and manage tracking.
  * Build question banks and effective rubrics.
  * Integrate H5P and external tools.
  * Create personalized, dynamic learning paths.

  
  
**Outline**  
1. Welcome and review  
2. Advanced course design strategies (conditional activities, tracking)  
3. Assessment innovations (question bank, quizzes, rubrics)  
4. Gradebook customization (categories, reports)  
5. Integrating external tools (H5P, multimedia)  
6. Hands-on application  
7. Wrap-up & Q&A
[Strengthening Faculty Well-Being and Student Engagement with Social Emotional Learning](javascript:;)
Date and time: Wednesday, October 15, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m.  
Audience:   
Duration: 90 minutes  
  
**Description**   
This workshop is designed specifically for faculty in higher education to enhance their personal well-being, emotional awareness, and emotional regulation skills through Social Emotional Learning (SEL). By strengthening their own social-emotional competencies, faculty will be better equipped to support both themselves and their students in navigating the emotional and social challenges of academic life. The workshop guides faculty in understanding their emotions, managing stress effectively, and applying SEL strategies in real-life teaching situations. Participants will also learn how to foster student engagement and well-being by integrating SEL skills into their teaching practices, creating a more empathetic and supportive learning environment.   
  
**Objectives**
  * Develop faculty members’ self-awareness and understanding of their own emotions. 
  * Equip faculty with practical emotional regulation techniques to manage stress and improve well-being.
  * Enhance faculty members’ capacity to apply SEL principles in classroom and everyday academic interactions. 
  * Provide tools for faculty to model SEL skills for students, supporting students’ social and emotional development.

  
**  
Key Content and Topics**  
Understanding and managing emotions exercises on recognizing personal emotions, triggers, and responses; self-care strategies; work-life balance; strategies for emotional regulation; mindfulness and stress management techniques tailored for faculty.   
**  
Real-Life Application Scenarios**   
Case studies and role playing to practice responding to common academic stressors, difficult conversations, and classroom challenges with SEL-informed approaches, while building supportive Faculty-Student relationships based on communication and active listening skills, empathy-building activities, and ways to foster trust and connection to enhance student engagement.   
  
**Action Planning**  
Participants develop personalized action plans for applying SEL techniques in their professional context and for supporting students’ SEL growth.

[Drama Therapy Workshop: The Masks We Wear – Rediscovering Self Through Drama](javascript:;)
Following the success of earlier initiatives, the Department of Performing Arts is pleased to announce a new 12-session drama therapy workshop, designed as a creative and therapeutic space to explore identity, emotional well-being, and the roles we play in life.  
  
**Overview**  
Facilitated by our colleague Ms. Myriam Saadé, the workshop will use drama-based techniques—such as storytelling and symbolic exploration—to help participants: 
  * support emotional expression and stress relief.
  * strengthen self-awareness and empathy.
  * foster authentic connections among peers.
  * explore the balance between professional roles and personal identity.

  
**Date and Time**
  * Faculty sessions: Mondays, 3:30 p.m. – 5:00 p.m. (starting Monday, September 22)
  * Staff sessions: Tuesdays, 4:00 p.m. – 5:30 p.m. (starting Tuesday, September 23)

  
  
**Practical Information**
  * Duration: 12 sessions
  * Cost: Free of charge
  * Requirement: Registration and regular attendance are mandatory

For more information, please contact Dr. Lena Saadé Gebran at: lenasaade@usek.edu.lb.

### Mediation Training Workshop
As part of our commitment to fostering a collaborative academic environment, we are pleased to invite you to participate in a training and awareness workshop on mediation as a tool for conflict prevention and resolution, which will take place on July 9 and 10, 2025, at the USEK Kaslik campus, building H, room H018.  
  
The workshop will be led by Ms. Johanna Hawari-Bourjeily, Director of the Professional Mediation Center (CPM), and is organized in collaboration with the AUF Middle East.  
  
This training aims to equip you with practical tools for positively addressing conflict situations—particularly within the classroom and in interactions with students, as well as in professional relationships among colleagues. It will help foster a culture of dialogue and mutual respect within our university community.  
  
Schedule: 
  * 9:30 AM – 12:30 PM | Workshop 1
  * 12:30 PM – 1:30 PM | Lunch break
  * 1:30 PM – 3:30 PM | Workshop 2

  
  
Your participation in this training would be greatly appreciated and will contribute to strengthening the collective dynamic of our institution.

### Faculty Workload Policy Discussion
Date: April 17, 2024  
Duration: 2 hours (from 10:00 am to 12:00 pm)  
Location: Building D, Room D307  
Start Time: 9:30 am we will be welcoming you with a meet and greet breakfast before the launching of the workshop, providing an opportunity for networking and informal discussions.  
  
During the workshop, we will delve into various aspects of the faculty workload policy, including its current structure, potential areas for improvement, and ways to ensure that it aligns with our institution's objectives while also supporting the well-being of our faculty members. Your participation will be integral to the success of this workshop, as we seek to gather diverse viewpoints and engage in constructive dialogue that will inform any future revisions or updates to the policy. Furthermore, it is important to acknowledge that attendees are tasked with conveying the insights and discussions from the workshop to their fellow faculty members, thereby ensuring that all relevant stakeholders are well-informed and engaged in the implementation of this policy.

### The Catalog Management Workshop, organized for Associate deans and Heads of departments on February 21st, from 10:00 am to 12:00 pm, at the auditorium of Building H- room HS315. 
This workshop shall guide them through managing all areas of the university catalog and shall elaborate on the importance of building a proper catalog, to ensure an efficient process for the course offering creation and registration.  
  

### Faculty Development Workshop entitled "Influential Leadership," scheduled from March 18th to March 22nd, 2024, from 4:30 pm to 6:30 pm at the Antoine Ammar Faculty Lounge, Building H – room H019.

The modules include Influence, Values and Ethics, Leading Change, Core and Managerial Competencies, and Case Study. The training is conducted by Mr. Rabieh Razzouk, the Director of the Learning Systems Institute at Florida State University (FSU). ### DRAMATHERAPY: BEYOND BORDERS
In alignment with USEK continuous effort to improve its faculty well-being, we are introducing in collaboration with Department of Performing Arts at the Faculty of Arts and Sciences a Dramatherapy workshop entitled “Beyond Borders”.   
  
The details of the workshop are as follows:  
Date: EVERY Wednesday starting September 25th, 2024   
Time: from 4:30 p.m. till 6:30 p.m.   
Location: Building D, Room 016  
Duration: 13 sessions  
Moderators/Instructors: Jean Daccache and Natacha Rizk (actors and certified drama therapists)  
  
Rationale: Boundaries to set or to break through?   
Regardless of whether borders are based on physical, ethno-cultural, geopolitical or any other criteria, they are not just lines on a map, they can have serious effects on people’s lives bordering their existence materially, emotionally, psychologically and socially. For some, borders provide safety and security. For others, they are barriers to break through or even boundaries restraining them from moving ahead.   
  
Mission: This workshop aims to identify, establish or communicate your psychological boundaries to maintain healthy relationships while prioritizing your sense of self.  
  
Objectives:   
- Implement an empowering selfcare in your daily life   
- Push through the feeling of guilt   
- Unravel the root problem behind co-dependency, power struggles and more   
- Cope with toxic people and unwanted boundaries   
  
Please confirm your attendance before September 20, 2024 by registering through this [LINK](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fforms.office.com%2FPages%2FResponsePage.aspx%3Fid%3DxKLQBrlZ-EyjapGQ8izR9h7aE4wtapJLpUmFQ-sg1BhUODBaTU1YRVAzR1ZEWFc3STlJSTdBOVcwQy4u&data=05%7C02%7Csandraakiki%40usek.edu.lb%7Ca2a8a61af09443e2c5bb08dcce7ea5c3%7C06d0a2c459b94cf8a36a9190f22cd1f6%7C0%7C0%7C638612290545884069%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=L6S78VF2957RoD%2BvRMhwMOfOev0zSkRaW3wQY%2BLqInw%3D&reserved=0).
[Neuro Leadership: Cognitive triggers](javascript:;)
As part of USEK Faculty Development Program, a workshop entitled **"Unlocking the Brain: Neuroscience Insights for Leadership and Learning"** is offered on Tuesday 17th December 2024, in collaboration with the Doctoral College.   
  
The details of the workshop are as follows:  
  
Date: **Tuesday 17th of December 2024**   
Time: from 10.30 a.m. – 3.30 p.m. (Lunch will be served between sessions)  
Location: Building D, 4th floor, Business Lounge  
Moderator/Facilitator: **Dr. Mark Samuel** , FHEA, DBA, Director of the MBA Portfolio, Audencia Business School, France  
  
Description: Get ready for a dive in your brain!   
Throughout the training, you will learn many fun and intriguing facts about your brain. This workshop takes a deep dive to uncover the science behind focus, learning, and decision making. Most importantly, you will discover how psychology, behavioral theories, and neuroscience can be applied to leadership, and learn to identify factors pertaining to selective perception that can influence your decision as a leader (see attached Workshop Program).  
  
Registration: Limited spaces are available, so please hurry and register today by clicking on this [link](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=xKLQBrlZ-EyjapGQ8izR9h7aE4wtapJLpUmFQ-sg1BhUREExR0hOWUNOSjlXUDhLOFlOWjcwWklQOS4u).   
Deadline for registering: **December 10, 2024.**

## Crisis Management Committee
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/crisis-management-committee/about?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/crisis-management-committee/cmc-subcommittees?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/crisis-management-committee/policies?parent=1)
The Crisis Management Committee (CMC) was established as the primary line of action in the event of any crisis, which may cause mild to severe disruptions of daily activities in USEK. It is chaired by the Vice President for Community Life, who reports directly to the President, and is composed of senior USEK administration officials and key staff from various schools/specializations. In addition to prevention measures, the CMC develops policies, procedures and action plans that are essential for the management of and recovery from crisis situations. The University’s perception as a safe environment is grounded in the committee’s timely and efficient response based on the principles of preparedness, accessibility, care, minimized impact, and effective communication.

## Sustainability Initiatives
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/sustainable-office/about-us?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/sustainable-office/targets-and-actions?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/sustainability-initiatives/administration?parent=1)
  
  
For over a decade the Holy Spirit University (USEK) has been working toward tackling the challenges of sustainability, a major task facing higher education institutions worldwide.  
  
In 2016, the USEK Green Committee was created to advance the environmental management of the institution, increase its environmental and social performance and engage the university community as a whole in sustainable development. Within a year of the creation of the committee, USEK ranked 1st Green University in Lebanon and in the top 10 ‘Greenest’ Universities in the Arab World by GreenMetric World University Ranking in 2017 and sustained the ranking for a further two years. In 2020, it continued its success by ranking 1st Sustainable and Green University in Lebanon and 6th Most Sustainable and Green University in the MENA.  
  
The committee continues to transform the campus environment into a greener setting, remodel infrastructure, improve water management, increase education and research in sustainability to encourage and embed sustainable behaviors. More recently it has worked hard to expand the university’s goals by demonstrating and spreading good environmental practice on a national level.  
  
Students are not only equipped to become responsible professionals or researchers but also to be future social and ecological leaders able to make the right decisions toward sustainability in local and global arenas.  
  
It remains USEK’s top priority to continue growing a culture of sustainability among students, faculty, and staff, empowering them to be green actors in helping reduce environmental footprints through their actions and initiatives.

## Provost
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/provost/about-the-office?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/provost/meet-the-team?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/provost/message-from-the-provost?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/welcome-message?parent=1)
The Office of the Provost supports USEK’s mission, values, and objectives by providing essential academic leadership and guidance.  
  
As the Chief Academic Officer at USEK, the Provost collaborates closely with deans, faculty, and other administrators. With the support of Associate Provosts, the Provost directs the development, review, and implementation of academic policies and educational initiatives to promote the University’s excellence in teaching, research, and service.  
  
The primary responsibilities of the office include, but are not limited to: 
  * offering guidance and support to deans, administrators, and academic support units.
  * supervising all academic programs to ensure every student enjoys a high-quality and engaging learning experience.
  * recruiting and retaining talented and diverse faculty, making decisions about their promotions and tenure, advocating for their needs, and fostering diversity, equity, and inclusion throughout these processes.
  * promoting a culture of shared governance and facilitating dialogue between faculty members to drive institutional excellence.
  * engaging in strategic planning to shape the University’s academic future effectively.

##  Accreditation 
### ABET Accreditation
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/20180904AbetSc.jpg) The [Actuarial and Financial Mathematics (BS) ](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/mathematics-department/bachelor-of-science-in-actuarial-and-financial-mathematics?t=1)program is accredited by the Applied and Natural Science Accreditation Commission of [ABET](http://www.abet.org), the global accreditor of college and university programs in applied science, computing, engineering, and engineering technology.   
  
  
  
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/20160829LogoAbetCom.jpg)The [Computer Science (BS)](https://www.usek.edu.lb/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/computer-science-and-it/bachelor-of-science-in-computer-science?t=1) and the [Information Technology (BS)](https://www.usek.edu.lb/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/computer-science-and-it/bachelor-of-science-in-information-technology?t=1) programs are accredited by the Computing Accreditation Commission of [ABET](http://www.abet.org), the global accreditor of college and university programs in applied science, computing, engineering, and engineering technology.  
  
  
  

### Evalag International Accreditation 
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/Uploaded%20Images/20230725EvalagLogoProgramme.jpg)In June 2017, eight Social Sciences and Humanities programs received the International Accreditation by the Accreditation Commission of evalag, EVALUATIONSAGENTUR BADEN–WÜRTTEMBERG. This recognition was renewed in June 2023 for seven programs for a period of six years.  
  
[evalag](http://www.evalag.de), known as a center of competence for quality assurance and enhancement and a source of support for higher education institutions and other scientific institutions, with commitment for good quality in teaching and learning, research and other services.   
  

  * [Education – Basic Education (BA)](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/department-of-education/bachelor-of-arts-in-education-basic-education?t=1)
  * [Journalism and Communication (BA)](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/department-of-communication/bachelor-of-arts-in-journalism-and-communication?t=1)
  * Language and Literature (BA) Emphasizes: [Arabic](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/department-of-languages-and-literatures/bachelor-of-arts-in-languages-arabic?t=1), [English](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/department-of-languages-and-literatures/bachelor-of-arts-in-languages-english?t=1), [French](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/department-of-languages-and-literatures/bachelor-of-arts-in-languages-french?t=1)
  * [Modern Languages and Translation (BA)](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/faculty-of-arts-and-sciences/department-of-languages-and-literatures/bachelor-of-arts-in-modern-languages-and-translation?t=1)
