##  ERASMUS+ PROJECT – JEAN MONNET MODULE / USEK 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/school-of-law-and-political-sciences)
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/Uploaded%20Images/20210525Erasmus.jpg)The Jean Monnet projects are designed to promote excellence in teaching and research, and to foster innovation, mutual enrichment and the dissemination of European Union-related content. In 2017, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) was awarded a Jean Monnet grant as part of the Erasmus+ 2017 call for proposals in order to support the development of a teaching module on “Europe and the MENA region: Issues and Challenges in Trans-Mediterranean Relations”.   
  
This project is the first Jean Monnet Project to be selected in Lebanon in 10 years and is coordinated by H.E. Ambassador Nassif Hitti, Director of USEK’s Higher Institute of Political and Administrative Sciences with the support of the International Affairs Office.  
  
The first part of the teaching module resulted in the creation of two [Master courses](https://www.usek.edu.lb/isspa-academic-program/master-of-arts-in-middle-eastern-studies?t=2): “MES605 - The Middle East and Europe: Issues and Challenges in Trans-Mediterranean Relations” and “MES600 - Regional Dynamics and Current Issues in the Middle East”. Simultaneously, several activities were also organized.  
  

[Seminar: Middle East: Order and Dis-order in the Middle East Regional System, Rome, January 25-26, 2019](javascript:;)
This seminar, organized by the Istituto Affari Internazionali (IAI), aimed at exploring the ongoing and future developments in the Middle East and the growing destruction of the old regional order. Particular attention was devoted to the case of Syria and the ramifications of the conflict there, by analyzing the stances and interests of several regional and international players. Another highlighted point was the nature and sustainability of the alliances in and on the region as a key aspect to assess the future regional order. Dr. Nassif was invited to participate in this seminar as part of the Jean Monnet Project, enhancing therefore the cooperation plan with the IAI, especially in terms of research.
[Union for the Mediterranean, Barcelona, December 8, 2018](javascript:;)
Dr. Nassif Hitti was invited by the former secretary Fethallah Sijilmassi for a brainstorming session within a very small group of practitioners and officials from EU and the MENA region to discuss the challenges faced in the region. This was part of the Research activities of the Jean Monnet project.
[Roundtable: Les relations transméditerranéennes, November 7, 2018](javascript:;)
A roundtable with Mathieu Rey, Nassif Hitti and Jana Jabbour was organized by the Cultural French Institute as part of the Salon du livre francophone de Beyrouth. USEK and the French Institute met during the month of April 2018 to prepare for this event aiming to promote the Jean Monnet Module during the book fair, a major event in Lebanon hosting more than 80,000 visitors every year and featuring many cultural events, debates, and conferences. USEK’s participation and engagement in this fair enabled it to reach a wider audience, as the audience was not limited to students enrolled in the module only, but also other students majoring in Political Sciences. A rich debate with the audience took place at the end of the roundtable.
[Debate with Gilles Kepel, Salon du livre francophone de Beyrouth organized by the Cultural French Institute, November 3, 2018](javascript:;)
This debate aimed to discuss the last book of Gilles Kepel “Sortir du Chaos”, which is directly related to the relations between Europe and the MENA.
[Conference at the Mediterranean Academy of Diplomatic Studies (MEDAC), Malta, November 2018](javascript:;)
This conference aimed to identify potential solutions to address new challenges, like migrations, terrorism, etc. Dr. Nassif Hitti also underlined the new security issues in the region.
[Conference: Challenges over Power and Regional Stability in the Mediterranean, October 3, 2018](javascript:;)
Moderated by Dr. Nassif Hitti, this conference was given by Prof. Jean-Paul Chagnollaud and Ms. Agnès Levallois who delivered specialized lectures to the USEK students as part of the Jean Monet Module. Very active discussions were conducted with both students and academics. The Erasmus+ National Office Coordinator was also invited and participated in this activity.  

[ PHOTO ALBUM ](https://en-gb.facebook.com/pg/USEKOfficial/photos/?tab=album&album_id=2078842665513309)
[Mediterranean Academy of Diplomatic Studies (MEDAC), March 8-9, 2018](javascript:;)
During this conference, Dr. Nassif Hitti, project coordinator, addressed the trans-Mediterranean relations to diplomats of the Mediterranean region. The conference at the Ministry discussed the same topic.
[The Regional 'Cold War' in the Middle East. Conversation with Dr. Nassif Hitti”, Rome, Italy, January 25, 2018](javascript:;)
This conference was organized as part of the cooperation with the _Istituto Affari Internazionali_ (IAI) in Italy, developed through the Jean Monnet project. Many other activities are now underway, particularly the organization of joint lectures and conferences. This collaboration between a key stakeholder in Europe (IAI) and USEK is crucial to initiate research projects and ensure the sustainability of the Jean Monnet project.
[Brainstorming Session, Barcelona, Spain, January 1, 2018](javascript:;)
Dr. Nassif Hitti was invited by Fethallah Sijilmassi, former Secretary General of the Union for the Mediterranean (UfM), for a brainstorming session within a very small group of practitioners and officials from the EU and the MENA region to discuss the challenges faced in the region. This was part of the research activities of the Jean Monnet project.
[Conference at the Cercle National des Armées, Paris, France, December 12, 2017](javascript:;)
During this conference organized by Les Écoles de Saint-Cyr, Dr. Nassif Hitti shed the light on the challenges facing the trans-Mediterranean relations and how a common agenda can be developed to address these challenges. He also highlighted the Jean Monnet project and the importance of developing an academic cooperation on trans-Mediterranean relations.
[Conference: The EU’s New Resilience Agenda in the MENA Region, November 3, 2017 ](javascript:;)
This conference was organized in collaboration with the Istituto Affari Internazionali (IAI) and the Foundation for European Progressive Studies, with the support of the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. Representatives from the European Delegation in Beirut and the Erasmus+ National Office in Beirut attended this event.   

[ PHOTO ALBUM ](https://www.usek.edu.lb/photo-gallery/eu-new-resilience-agenda-in-the-mena-region)
[Erasmus+ Information Day, Beirut, Lebanon, October 5, 2017](javascript:;)
On the occasion of the Erasmus+ Information Day, organized at the Ministry of Education and Higher Education on October 5, 2017, H.E. Dr. Nassif Hitti, Director of the USEK Higher Institute of Political and Administrative Sciences and coordinator of the project, presented the EU-funded Jean Monnet Module “Europe and the MENA Region: Issues and Challenges in the Trans-Mediterranean Relations”.

##  E-TALEB Project 
The Professional Standards Framework for Excellence in Teaching and Learning in Lebanese Universities “E-TALEB” is a national project co-funded by Erasmus+ co-funded by the Erasmus+ Programme of the European Union. E-TALEB aims at developing the Lebanese Professional Standards in Teaching and Learning and cooperating for innovation and exchange of good practices and experiences relevant to similar frameworks established in Europe.  
  
The main objective of this project is to support the initial and continuing professional development of staff engaged in teaching and foster dynamic approaches to teaching and learning through creativity, innovation and continuous development in diverse academic disciplines and/or professional settings. The project will support in creating a community of researchers in different disciplines who share inter and intra university practices in teaching and learning.  
  
E-TALEB will acknowledge the variety and quality of teaching, learning and assessment practices that support and underpin student learning including instructional technology. It will also demonstrate to students and other stakeholders the professionalism that staff and institutions bring to teaching and their support for student learning.  
  

### Aims and wide objectives
E-TALEB aims to develop faculty members teaching skills and students learning experience in Lebanon by developing a national framework of good practices and shared experiences:  
1. Supporting the initial and continuing professional development of staff engaged in teaching and supporting learning;  
2. Fostering dynamic approaches to teaching and learning through creativity, innovation and continuous development in diverse academic and/or professional settings;  
3. Creating a community of researchers in different disciplines who share inter and intra university practices in teaching and learning;  
4. Acknowledging the variety and quality of teaching, learning and assessment practices that support and underpin student learning including instructional technology;  
5. Assisting individuals and institutions in gaining formal recognition for quality enhanced approaches to teaching and supporting learning.  
  

### Specific Objectives
As a result, the project will have high national impact, providing at once many outcomes: 
  * Establishing the Lebanese Professional Standards Framework in Teaching & Learning LBPSF;
  * Offering a Post-Graduate Certificate Programme in Teaching and Learning in Higher Education for faculty members;
  * Collaborating interuniversity activities centered on training and educational programs;
  * Creating centers for teaching excellence inside each of the participating universities that support faculty and students in their teaching and learning activities;
  * Supporting the universities in their accreditation programs by having a formal process for teaching and learning;
  * Developing human capital and talented experts in teaching and learning in the participating countries;
  * Sustaining the competitiveness of the higher education field in Lebanon, the Middle East and the participating partner countries;
  * Publishing the Lebanese Journal on Teaching and Learning.

##  Mission, Vision and Objectives 
### Mission
The Learning and Teaching Excellence Center (LTEC) at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik is dedicated to the development of the professional qualifications of educators in teaching and learning through the promotion of teamwork, innovation, self-reflection and the efficient use of instructional technologies, and through sharing best practices to enhance the student learning experience.  
  
LTEC serves USEK and non USEK faculty members by engaging and supporting them in their research-based teaching and learning concepts, and bringing them into intentional daily practice both inside and outside the classroom.  
  
The LTEC provides a number of tools that can improve and enhance the online teaching and learning process, and also offers training on emerging digital platforms (such as e-learning) that can be used in both distance and face-to-face classrooms.  
  

### Vision
The Learning and Teaching Excellence Center (LTEC) plays a major role in the success of the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK). It is taking a leading role in the development of faculty qualifications and will be recognized nationally and internationally for best practices, excellence and innovation in teaching and for ensuring a successful student learning experience.   
  

### Objectives
The main focus of the Learning and Teaching Excellence Center at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik is to support, promote and enhance teaching effectiveness and student learning.  
  
LTEC aims to: 
  * Facilitate the professional and intellectual development of faculty, staff, and graduate students as educators. 
  * Promote and support a community of teachers where the theory and practice of teaching and learning are shared. 
  * Help faculty members develop, implement, and assess instructional approaches and methods. 
  * Foster innovations in Higher Education teaching and learning. 
  * Advocate appropriate use of technology in enhancing university teaching and learning. 
  * Help individual instructors assess their teaching effectiveness and their students’ learning. 
  * Sustain a university culture that recognizes and rewards both scholarly teaching and the scholarship of teaching and learning.
  * Develop and maintain learning systems and technologies that can be used by staff and students across the university to facilitate and enable the online and hybrid teaching and learning process.

##  Past events 
### 2017
**The 2017 ABET Accreditation Seminar – First MENA Region Edition**  
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, organized the 2017 ABET Accreditation Seminar – First MENA Region Edition.   
This event took place on Wednesday October 4 and Thursday October 5, 2017 at the USEK Kaslik Campus. It was hosted by the Learning and Teaching Excellence Center (LTEC) and delivered by Dr. Joe Sussman, Chief Accreditation Officer and Chief Information Officer at ABET, and Dr. Winston Erevelles, Adjunct Accreditation Director, Engineering, at ABET.  
The Seminar’s main objective was to enable participants from different Lebanese Universities understand the basic concepts of accreditation, the requirements of the ABET accreditation process, and the process for requesting an initial program review.   
[[Photo Album](https://www.usek.edu.lb/photo-gallery/the-2017-abet-accreditation-seminar%20)]  
  

### 2015
**Opening of the Learning and Teaching Excellence Center (LTEC)** :   
On Friday 22nd of May, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik organized the Opening Ceremony of the Learning and Teaching Excellence Center (LTEC), the first in Lebanon, with the presence of Dr. Ahmad Jammal, Director General of Higher Education. The LTEC mission and activities were presented through a short video with the participation of Dr. Carolyn Creel and Dr. Laura Ewing from The University of Texas at Austin via Skype. This event, hosted by the Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness Office, included speeches from Dr. Georges Yahchouchi, Deputy President for Quality Assurance and Teaching & Learning, Dr. William Clements, Vice-President of Norwich University, Rev. Fr. Hady Mahfouz, USEK President, and Dr. Ahmad Jammal, Director General of Higher Education.   
[[Photo Album](https://www.facebook.com/pg/USEKOfficial/photos/?tab=album&album_id=912628292134758)]  
  
**Ceremony of Certificates - Online Integrated Course Design** :   
As part of the online courses development and implementation process, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik organized a certificates ceremony for the Online Course on « Integrated Course Design », given to 34 of USEK’s academic officers and instructors by Dee Fink and Associates. This event was held on Tuesday 26th of May in the presence of Dr. Stewart Ross, partner of Dee Fink and Associates, at the Learning and Teaching Excellence Center (LTEC)   
[[Photo Album](https://www.facebook.com/pg/USEKOfficial/photos/?tab=album&album_id=913119455418975)]  
  
**Professional Educator Program Awards Celebration** :   
On Friday January 23, 2015, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik celebrated the delivery of Awards for “The Professional Educator Program for Higher Education” with the collaboration of the UT Global Initiative for Education and Leadership of The University of Texas at Austin. The event, organized by the Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness Office, was opened by Dr. Georges Yahchouchi, Deputy President for Quality Assurance and Teaching and Learning, and was followed by speeches from Dr. Carolyn Creel and Dr. Laura Ewing, Workshops facilitators at UTG, Reverend Father Hady Mahfouz, President of the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, and the Director General of Higher Education in Lebanon, Dr. Ahmad Jammal.   
[[Photo Album](https://www.facebook.com/pg/USEKOfficial/photos/?tab=album&album_id=842771182453803)]  
  

### 2014 
**Dee Fink & Associates Workshops Closing Ceremony**:   
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik organized a closing ceremony in collaboration with the Lebanese Army and the Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness Office on Thursday November 13, 2014. The ceremony concluded the four days Dee Fink & Associates workshops on Integrated Course Design & Active Learning Strategies, delivered by Dr. Stewart Ross, the founding Director of the Center of Teaching and Learning at Minnesota State University and Partner of Dee Fink and Associates. During the Ceremony, 60 Certificates were awarded to the participants. The participants included a delegation of Generals and high ranking officers from the Training Directorate of the Lebanese Army, headed by General Doureid Zahereddine.  
[[Photo Album](https://www.facebook.com/pg/USEKOfficial/photos/?tab=album&album_id=802210623176526)]  
  
**Online Certificate in Teaching and Learning provided by Norwich University, United States** :   
In 2014, 7 faculty members successfully completed the Online Certificate in Teaching and Learning provided by Norwich University.   
  

### 2013
**Awards Celebration of the Post-Graduate Certificate – USEK** :  
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized the awards celebration of the Post-Graduate Certificate in Learning and Teaching in Higher Education, and the marking of the the attainment of Fellowship at the Higher Education Academy - UK. This event, implemented in collaboration with the University of Chester, was held on Monday March 17, 2014, at 11:00, in the Archaeological Museum of USEK, at USEK Main Campus. The program consisted of graduates testimonies and speeches by Dr. Georges Yahchouchi, Prorector for Quality Assurance and Teaching & Learning, Dr. Julie-Anne Regan, PGCTLHE program leader from the University of Chester, Ms. Donna McGowan, Director of the British Council Lebanon, Reverend Father Hady Mahfouz, President of USEK, and H. E. Mr. Elias Bou Saab, Minister of Education and Higher Education.

##  NAAB International Certification 
###  ![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/Uploaded%20Images/20200902NAAB.jpg)Master OF ARCHITECTURE - 2019
The term “International Certification” identifies a program as comparable in educational outcomes in all significant aspects to a program accredited by the NAAB in the United States and indicates that it provides an educational experience meeting acceptable standards, even though such program may differ in format or method of delivery. The designation is valid for six years beginning 1 January of the year in which the final visit (Visit 3) took place. In order to maintain the designation, the program must be visited again in the sixth year of the designation.  
  
Schools with programs identified as holding NAAB International Certification are not formally “accredited” as that term is used with reference to programs in the United States and may not refer to their programs as “accredited” by the NAAB. However, students who graduate from internationally certified programs are able to apply for individualized review of their credentials on an expedited basis for purposes of the Educational Evaluation Services for Architects program administered by the NAAB on behalf of the National Council of Architectural Registration Boards.   
  
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, School of Architecture and Design has received the International Certification designation [National Architectural Accrediting Board](https://www.naab.org/) for the following professional degree program:  
  
[Master of Architecture degree](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/department-of-architecture/bachelor-of-science-in-architectural-studies-22?t=2) (193 semester credit hours) – 2019  
  
SEE MORE:  
- [Decision Letter](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20190911DecisionLetter.pdf)  
- [USEK Architecture Program Report (APR) for Visit Three](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20190911APR.pdf)  
- [NAAB Visiting Team Report (VTR) for USEK Visit Three](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20190911VTR.pdf)   
- [NAAB 2012 Conditions for Substantial Equivalency](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20181105ConditionsSubstantialEqu2012.pdf)   
- [NAAB 2013 Procedures for Substantial Equivalency](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20181105ProceduresSubstantialEqu2013.pdf)  
  
The current conditions and procedures for International Certification are found below:  
- [2019 Conditions for NAAB International Certification](https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/NAAB/21e8eae7-e532-47c0-bff1-4111ca0d4fb0/UploadedImages/PDFs/2019-Conditions-for-NAAB-International-Certification.pdf)

##  Public Law Research Center 
The Public Law Research Center (PLRC) is part of the School of the Law and Political Sciences and specializes in research in public law.   
  

### MISSION
The Center conducts and stimulates research, produces works and formulates policy recommendations in areas of public law related to the needs of the reform of the Lebanese State and its activities, both national and international. It also strives to build cooperation with research institutions in the Middle East and other regions of the world.   
  
The Public Law Research Center is also meant to serve as a support laboratory for a Master’s Degree in public law.  
  

### VISION
The Center seeks to promote and develop research in public law both within USEK’s School of Law and Lebanon. It aims to contribute, through work, recommendations, and training, to improving the effectiveness of public policies for the benefit of the Lebanese people.   
  
The Center also seeks to promote a culture of good State governance and respect for human rights. More generally, the Center aims to disseminate a culture of respect for State institutions in Lebanon, i.e. to make society – most particularly young people – aware of the need for stable, transparent, and well-governed state institutions, with laws applicable to all and with policies respectful of fundamental political, economic, and social rights of the Lebanese people.  
  
The research results are made available to the public through the print or online publication of books, conference proceedings, or articles in the [USEK Law Journal](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publications), a peer-reviewed journal indexed on Scopus

More About UCLC
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/uclc/about)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/uclc/directors-word)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/uclc/ongoing-courses)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/uclc/international-summer-school-2025)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/uclc/partnerships-and-collaborations)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/uclc/testimonials)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/uclc/news)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/uclc/photo)
##  About 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/uclc)
The UCLC collaborates with various USEK schools to serve the community by promoting the transfer of knowledge between academia and professional practice.  
  
In line with UNESCO's 1972 definition of lifelong learning, which views it as a tool for improving the quality of life, enhancing education in relation to everyday needs, encouraging individual participation in educational decisions, and fostering open-minded planning and management, UCLC provides inclusive education, life skills training, and professional development services. These initiatives help learners stay current in their fields, continue contributing, and remain competitive, while also expanding the scope of their existing professions.  
  
UCLC’s activities take many forms, addressing relevant social demands to develop skills and competencies that meet the diverse and ever-evolving needs of individuals and communities. These activities link theoretical and practical knowledge, focusing primarily on applying scientific principles to professional domains.  
  
UCLC promotes interdisciplinary professional education through high-quality credit and non-credit programs designed to meet the shifting demands of the job market.  
  
We welcome your suggestions. If you have any feedback or want to make a course request, please feel free to contact us at 09 600 821 or via email at uclc@usek.edu.lb.  
  

[Mission and Vision](javascript:;)
### Mission
UCLC expands the mission of USEK to meet lifelong learning needs by: 
  * offering cutting-edge work-relevant courses and hands-on trainings for career professionals and career changers of all ages;
  * providing learning opportunities to learn while promoting Lebanese culture/heritage and transformative education that strengthens targeted communities;
  * reskilling and upskilling professional abilities by building on the strengths of and collaborating with the resources of the University and the community.

  
  

### Vision
“A central actor in driving and sustaining development”   
UCLC’ vision is to empower lifelong learners, organizations, and communities through impactful and productive educational opportunities for careers enhancement and social development.  

[UCLC’ Core Values](javascript:;)
1. Inclusive Education Policies  
  
2. Sustainability  
  
3. Diversity  
  
4. Transdisciplinary dialogue  
  
5. Common Good
[Strategic Priorities](javascript:;)
UCLC will focus on three strategic priorities:   
  
1. Strategic Priority 1: Enhancing Program Offerings   
2. Strategic Priority 2: Strengthen Community and Industry Partnerships   
3. Strategic Priority 3: Improving Technology Integration
[Policies](javascript:;)
### ADMISSION 
To register in one or several courses, please fill in the [Online Registration Form](https://s.usek.edu.lb/wf/forms/uclc3.aspx?pid=UCLC2&rpid=-24971) and select the chosen course(s). You will be asked to upload a scanned copy of your ID card (or passport for international students) and a photo.  
  
A confirmation email and a payment link will be sent to you shortly after.  
  
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact us on 09 600 821.  
  

### ENROLLMENT AND REGISTRATION REQUIREMENTS
The UCLC Courses are open to anyone who is 18 years old and above. While most courses do not have specific prerequisites, some may require prior education and/or experience to maximize benefits.  
  
To register for one or several courses, please fill in the Online Registration Form and select the desired course(s). You will be asked to upload a scanned copy of your ID card (or passport for international students) and a photo. A confirmation email and a payment link will be sent to you shortly to complete the payment process.  
  
Note: Students already at USEK can enroll in any course without prior payment; the UCLC tuition fees will be added directly to his/her account.  
  
Please feel free to contact us on 09 600 821 if you have any questions.  
  

### PAYMENT POLICY
Once you have registered online, you may choose between two payment options: 
  * via bank (Audi, Bank of Beirut, BLOM, Byblos – using your USEK ID number) or
  * online by VISA/MasterCard (a 3.49% fee will be applied for credit card processing).

  
Please note, there is no registration fee.  
  
For course fees exceeding USD 1000 a payment plan is available upon request.  
  

### WITHDRAW POLICY
If for any reason you must withdraw the course(s) or program, you will need to inform the UCLC by sending an email to uclc@usek.edu.lb or by calling us on 09 600 821. A refund will be issued based on the drop period as stated in the Withdraw Policy below.  
  

### REFUND
During the registration process, students must read the UCLC Refund Policy and verify that they have understood it.  
  
Below are the refundable amounts based on the withdraw period:  
  
**Course Withdraw Policy** |  |  |  |  | **Tuition Refunded** |  |  |  |  |  **Tuition Payment**  
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---  
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |   
Withdrawing the course one week before the start date |  |  |  |  | 50% |  |  |  |  | 50%  
Withdrawing the course after 1st class session |  |  |  |  | 0% |  |  |  |  | 100%  
  
If the refund request meets the above criteria, the refund process will typically take 3 to 4 working days, and the amount(s) will be refunded within 30 working days. Refunds are issued by check, and the student will receive an SMS once the check is ready for collection.  
  

### COURSE CANCELLATION
UCLC reserves the right to cancel or reschedule any course due to insufficient enrollment or other unforeseen circumstances. All registered candidates will be notified, and full reimbursement will be made.   
  

### ATTENDANCE POLICY
Students must attend all classes in order to fulfill the course requirements. For every hour of instruction, no more than fifteen (15) minutes can be missed. Arriving more than 15 minutes late at the start of a class or leaving more than 15 minutes early will also be recorded as unsatisfactory performance. Instructors reserve the right to drop a student from the course if he/she is absent more than 30% of the total class instruction time.  
  

### CERTIFICATE
In order to be eligible for a course certificate, students are required to maintain regular attendance and complete all program requirements.  
  
Grades are not assigned, and the programs do not count towards a degree.  
  

### GENERAL REGULATIONS
Student ID card: All UCLC students will receive a USEK ID card which must be presented when entering the campus and accessing the parking lot. In case of loss or damage, a duplicate can be issued by the Office of the Registrar for a fixed fee.  
  
USEK Rules and Regulations:  
All students are expected to abide by the University rules and regulations.  
  
Change of Personal Information:  
Students are encouraged to inform the UCLC about any changes in their contact information.  
  

### PROGRAM INFORMATION AND CHANGES
The UCLC reserves the right to make changes to the information printed in materials or on this website.   
  

### COURSE OFFERINGS
The updated course listings are regularly posted on the website. However, UCLC is under no obligation to offer any of the courses/programs.

##  Get Involved 
Whether you are an aspiring entrepreneur, a seasoned founder, a faculty member, or a business support organization (BSO), ACIE is your gateway to entrepreneurship and innovation at USEK.  
  

  * Startups: Register your interest to join upcoming programs or pitch your ideas for feedback.
  * Ecosystem partners: Collaborate on joint initiatives, host expert sessions, or become mentors.
  * Students and alumni: Attend workshops, join competitions, and explore entrepreneurial pathways.
  * Researchers and faculty: Partner with us to bridge academic research and real-world impact.
  * Investors and donors: Explore opportunities to support high-potential startups and program growth.

  
  
To get involved, please fill out our [form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf1BafrzgtO9A30arww1PA_Zo0oRuSoHBIQIZHwVngDDc0LFg/viewform?usp=dialog).

March 2022
Visit of Fr. Talal Hachem to Los Angeles
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/alumni/photo-gallery)

##  New USEK Alumni Breakthrough in Cancer Research 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/announcements)
USEK has yet another reason to feel proud as its alumna Cynthia Kassab, M.D., is marking a new milestone in cancer history. Currently a postdoctoral research fellow in the Brain Tumor Immunology and Immunotherapy Lab at MD Anderson, Houston, Cynthia is leading a unique project that studies how immune cells interact with glioblastoma, an aggressive brain tumor. Using new and complex techniques to find out why certain types of immune cells gather in a specific area, this information will help researchers develop more effective immunotherapies and lead to better patient outcomes.  
  
Dr. Kassab speaks fondly of USEK’s influence on her work: “USEK built grit and passion in me towards medicine, and the story did not end here. It is just a start, a small step, and the best is yet to come!”.  
  
To know more about the project: <https://m.facebook.com/notes/md-anderson-brain-and-spine/research-spotlight-glioblastoma-immune-topographical-atlas/2815024108569991/>

## CIRAME – Research Center
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/business/research-center/cirame?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/fgsc-research-center/lines-of-research?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/business-school/international-peer-reviewed-journals?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/business-school/publications?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/business/research/contact?parent=1)
The CIRAME is the research center of the USEK Business School, founded on the basis of professionalizing the management of research activities and increasing the national and international production of first class publications and research.  
  

### Mission and objectives
The mission of CIRAME consists of producing and sharing scientific knowledge in business and management fields with emphasis on local and regional contexts.   
  
The members of CIRAME pursue the following objectives: 
  * Promoting applied research in the fields of management and economics that are relevant to managers, and private and public organizations;
  * Establishing and maintaining close links between professionals and academic researchers;
  * Proposing solutions to managerial and business problems;
  * Carrying out sponsored research in response to a specific need from one or more organizations;
  * Facilitating research training.

  

### Research policy
The USEK Business School (UBS) has developed a solid research policy that has been a main driving force behind better quality education in post-graduate, undergraduate and foundation courses. These Faculty competencies, expanded throughout the University, have contributed in the success of USEK becoming a pioneer in scientific research in Lebanon.  
  
The School’s research policy, in line with the University mission, has secured a position for the University on an international level, which continuously presents opportunities for our Faculty and students to share and improve their academic knowledge and expertise.

##  Dean’s Word 
Committed to your success.   
  
Welcome new students! On this page, you will find all the information needed to embark on your academic journey for a successful career.   
  
Alumni & friends, thank you for keeping in touch with your school.   
  
As an Alumna myself, I am happy to say that a lot has changed at the Business School, but we have kept our focus on creating value for our students and the communities we serve. Our programs are constantly updated to match the needs of the labor market. Our Asher Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (ACIE) is the go-to place for the USEK community members to challenge their thinking and launch their start-ups.   
  
Through our network of foreign partners, we offer you various exchange programs. And if you wish to remain home, we have brought the international experience to your doorstep. Our program with Le Cordon Bleu delivers a world-class BA in hotel management. HEC Montreal and Paris II bring you all the international know-how and practices at graduate level. We want our students to become outstanding entrepreneurs, and future leaders wherever they go.   
  
Having a student-oriented learning environment is a priority for us. Our students study in more places than ever, with blended learning online and on-campus and experiential opportunities around the world. Through our BBA, MBA, EMBA, and Ph.D. programs and our ongoing preparations for AACSB accreditation, we provide the academic excellence that defines the quality of our professional body. We have as well developed unique world-class executive programs tackling the latest business problematics. The most recent one is delivered with Mr. Carlos Ghosn and other globally renowned experts.

##  Eligibility 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/students)
Students considered eligible are those who meet the following criteria:  
  
Undergraduate Students: 
  * Have already accomplished 30 credits of their program;
  * Have a cumulative GPA of 75/100 and above;
  * Have never been on probation for academic or disciplinary matters;
  * Have never been engaged in any political activity;
  * Are able to serve for one full academic year before graduation.

  
Graduate Students: 
  * Have already accomplished 9 credits of their program;
  * Have a cumulative GPA of 85/100 and above;
  * Have never been on probation for academic or disciplinary matters;
  * Have never been engaged in any political activity;
  * Are able to serve for one full academic year before graduation.

  
Doctoral Students: 
  * Have already accomplished 1 year of their academic program;
  * Have never been engaged in any political activity;
  * Are able to serve for one full academic year before graduation.

##  Career Center 
[ ![Mission and Vision](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/59582Image1.png?v=202509110827) Mission and Vision ](javascript:;)
[ ![International memberships](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/3249Image1.jpg?v=202509110827) International memberships ](javascript:;)
[ ![Meet The Team](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/3210Image1.png?v=202509111306) Meet The Team ](javascript:;)
### Mission
We assist USEK students in exploring their career options and enhancing their employability through the development of lifelong career management skills by: 
  * Creating an energized student-centered environment that makes career education accessible to all.
  * Providing expertise and leading the integration of career development and experiential education into USEK life and promoting their benefits to students, faculty, staff, and partners.
  * Providing high-quality career development and experiential education to students, faculty, staff, and partners.

  

### Vision
Our vision is to see all USEK students actively engaged in career exploration in a way that enriches their student life experience, enables them to understand the connection of their education to their professional development, and allows them to realize their career objectives and make constructive contributions to society.
The CSO is now active member in three international associations with expertise in career guidance and development.   
  

### NCDA: National Career Development Association
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/NCDA.jpg)The National Vocational Guidance Association (NVGA) was founded in 1913. In 1985 NVGA was renamed and became the National Career Development Association (NCDA). Thus NCDA is the first, longest running and preeminent career development association in the world. NCDA is the recognized leader in developing standards for the career development profession, for the provision of career counseling programs and services, and for the evaluation of career information material .   
  

### National Association of Colleges and Employers (NACE)
NACE has a rich history in the field of career development within higher education, in terms of setting industry standards, guiding ethical practices, advancing career services, and disseminating valuable career information. Established in 1956, it plays a pivotal role in bridging the gap between education and the workforce. NACE’s ongoing efforts empower career services professionals and educators to effectively prepare students for the dynamic job market.

[Doctoral Studies Days - Middle East Edition](javascript:;)
### Call for Papers
Following the success of the first two editions of the Doctoral Studies National Days, the USEK College of Doctoral Studies, in collaboration with the HCR, is pleased to announce the call for papers for the upcoming Middle East edition, taking place on **May 21–23, 2025** at USEK - Lebanon.  
  
This edition aims to highlight the achievements of PhD students on a regional scale, providing a dynamic platform for sharing, discussing, and advancing innovative research within the Lebanese and Middle Eastern academic community.  
  

### Competition and Awards
The Higher Center for Research, in collaboration with the College of Doctoral Studies, will organize an award competition recognizing students whose research presentations (oral and/or poster) are judged outstanding by a panel of faculty experts. Awards will be granted in each of the following research axes:  
1. Law and Political Science  
2. Education  
3. Economy and Finance  
4. Music, Cinema, Television and Performing Arts  
5. Languages, Literature and Communication  
6. Sociology, Psychology and Philosophy  
7. Architecture, Design and Visual Arts   
8. Basic/Fundamental Sciences   
9. Applied Sciences and Technology  
10. Medicine and Health Sciences  
11. Agriculture and Food Sciences  
12. Energy and Natural Resources  
13. Environmental Sustainability  
  
Like last year's conference, CNRS-Lebanon will play a pivotal role, and the jury members will represent various sister universities.  
  
To participate, please follow the steps below and complete the required fields in the webform by March 9, 2025. If your proposal is accepted, you will be notified of the next steps by March 26, 2025.  
  
1. Visit the [USEK APPLY platform](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/academic-applications)   
2. Navigate to the Doctoral College section on the Academic Applications page and locate the USEK Doctoral Days – Middle East Edition card.  
3. Click "APPLY NOW" and log in using one of the following methods to access the webform:  
- Gmail account  
- MS Office 365 account  
- USEK Account (for the USEK Community)  
  
Wishing you the best of luck in your endeavors and eagerly anticipating the submission of your ongoing projects.

##  Selection Process 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/students)
  * Prospective student council members are invited to fill out an online application within the relevant deadlines (mentioned in the [Academic Calendar](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/calendar)).
  * Applicants will receive a confirmation email on their eligibility status.
  * The students selected will be invited to an interview, during which their skills and capabilities will be assessed for this position.
  * The interviewing committee includes representatives of the Office of the Deputy President for Student Development and Enrolment Management (ODP-SDEM), the Student Affairs Office (SAO), and the respective academic units.
  * The student council consists of 7 members, each representing their respective unit for one academic year.

##  Selection Process 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/students)
  * Prospective student council members are invited to fill out an online application within the relevant deadlines (mentioned in the [Academic Calendar](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/calendar)).
  * Applicants will receive a confirmation email on their eligibility status.
  * The students selected will be invited to an interview, during which their skills and capabilities will be assessed for this position.
  * The interviewing committee includes representatives of the Office of the Deputy President for Student Development and Enrolment Management (ODP-SDEM), the Student Affairs Office (SAO), and the respective academic units.
  * The student council consists of 7 members, each representing their respective unit for one academic year.

## 
September 9, 2009
USEK completes an Institutional Evaluation Program conducted by the European Association of Universities (EUA) 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
A press conference was held in the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), on the occasion of the Institutional Evaluation Program completion, conducted through the expertise of the European University Association (EUA), a main body of Higher Education in Europe. The said Evaluation Program lasted for an entire year. This association aims mainly to guarantee the realization of the predetermined missions and objectives. It also seeks to ensure the conformity of its academic and administrative activities with the European standards of Quality Assurance.  
  
USEK is the first university in the Middle East that conducts such an Institutional evaluation program through the EUA. This association has developed more than 250 university evaluation programs all over the world, notably in Europe. Following the autoevaluation phase which extended over more than 6 months, USEK hosted, twice, a team of 5 experts from the EUA: 
  * Professor Ustün Ergüder, President of Bogaziçi University in Turkey, President of the Evaluation Committee
  * Professor Jethro Newton, Dean of Learning and Teaching, University College Chester, England
  * Professor Carles Solà, former President of Universitat Autonoma de Barcelona, Minister of Universities in Catalan (2003-2006), Spain
  * Professor Philippe Rousseau, former President of the University of Lille III, France
  * Mr. Tobias Walser, student at the Swiss Institute of Technology in Zurich, Switzerland

The experts did not only evaluate the action plan and the applied practices inside the university, but they have also met the majority of officials, a group of students, as well as different stakeholders involved in the university community (Director of Higher Education in Lebanon, representatives of NGOs and associations, entrepreneurs, etc.). The President of the evaluation committee, Professor Ustün Ergüde, noted that the decision of auto-evaluation taken by USEK and the will to discover its points of strength and weakness clearly reveals the strategic vision of the University’s leadership. Furthermore, the experts praised the University’s constructive policy as well as its financial aid policy. The latter clearly reflects the social responsibility that USEK proudly assumes.  
  
Fr. Hady Mahfouz, Rector of USEK, sincerely thanked the team of experts for their valuable recommendations as well as the USEK family for the efforts they invested in this program. He underlined the fact that USEK has been seeking throughout this initiative to prove the importance of Quality Assurance in the Lebanese university milieu, since it contributes to the construction of societies as well as to the development of human beings and the respect of their rights. He also highlighted that the undertaken procedure has reinforced and consolidated the dialogue between the university and its stakeholders. Moreover, Fr. Mahfouz drew attention that the Quality Assurance is more than a mere complementary project that the university aims to realize. It is indeed an obligation that USEK is striving to properly fulfill. As for the European experts in Higher Education, they emphasized the responsibility that a university should assume regarding Quality Assurance and the necessity to form in each university qualified teams in charge of the issue in hands. At USEK, a team of more than 10 instructors was formed in 2008 within the framework of a European program that works on Assurance Quality in universities. These instructors received training sessions in Italy, upon which the USEK “Assurance Quality Office” opened its doors.  
  
A lunch was held afterwards in honor of the experts and other guests.

##  Director’s Word 
Greetings,   
As the newly appointed director of the Alumni Relations Office and the Advancement Office at USEK, it is an honor to serve our vibrant community.   
  
Together, we embark on a journey of fostering connections, celebrating accomplishments, and advancing the legacy of our esteemed institution. The bond between alumni and our alma mater is a testament to the enduring spirit that defines USEK.  
  
As an alumna myself, I realize the importance of strengthening ties with our graduates worldwide, driving initiatives and collaborations that propel our university to new heights. I am excited about the transformative impact we can achieve together.  
  
This platform will serve as a hub for updates, events, and opportunities to reconnect. I encourage you to explore, engage in, and be an active part of the USEK family. Your support is instrumental in shaping the future of our alma mater.  
  
Thank you for entrusting me with this responsibility. Here’s to a future filled with shared successes and continued growth.  
  
**Cosette A. El Kamar**

##  Outreach and Engagement office 
The Outreach and Engagement office is a newly formed entity which seeks to incorporate a non-classic approach to the existing USEK Community and its operations. This office adopts the mission of seeking new ideas and challenges to maximize social impact and increase the outreach of USEK towards its community.  
  
**Mission**
  * Engage external audiences (entrepreneurs and investors, international aid foundations, governmental & non-profit organizations, diaspora, alumni, corporations and individuals) interested in being part of USEK’s new business model by providing the necessary resources and talent. 
  * Lead outreach initiatives with new and existing partners of USEK to secure the required funding for the project. Funding ranges from governmental and nonprofit organization grants to corporate and individual donations.
  * Utilize the university’s technology and tools to conduct projects and executive opportunities to create a full-scale working space within the USEK Community.
  * Represent the University at public speaking engagements, community meetings, boards, events, and presentations designed to seek potential outreach partnerships and opportunities.
  * Oversee, follow up, and produce the necessary reports related to new and existing projects which aim to develop the corporate aspect of the university by holding follow up meetings and making sure essential goals are reached in a timely manner.
  * Deal closely with teams to ensure strategic use of university media tools and develop the necessary marketing material for funding and collaboration recruitment.

## 
May 29, 2022
Alumni Chapter in UK – Gathering with USEK president Fr. Talal Hachem 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/alumni/events)
The UK Alumni Chapter organized a gathering with USEK President Father Talal Hachem and Alumni Relations Office Director Father Antoine Tahan, who gave the latest news about the institution’s successes and shared thoughts and plans about the potential of your alma mater.   
  
This gathering was also an opportunity to discuss new ways to support struggling students during the most severe economic crisis in Lebanon’s modern history.  
  
This event took place on Sunday, May 29, 2022, from 4pm to 6pm, at Grosvenor House Hotel, Mayfair, London.

# About USEK
[](javascript:;)
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/usek-at-a-glance)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/governance)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/university-facts)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/welcome-message)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/carlos-ghosn-at-usek)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/accreditation)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ruc)[](http://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/ltec)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/administrative-and-technical-personnel/mission-and-activities)[](https://jobs.usek.edu.lb/)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/social-development)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/advancement-and-outreach)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/one-step-ahead)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/rankings)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/fundamental-texts)
## Faculty Affairs
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/welcome-message)
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/welcome-message?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/faculty-handbook?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/faculty-affairs/faculty-orientations?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/about-usek/faculty-affairs/workshops?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/faq?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/contact-us?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/faculty-affairs/directory?parent=1)
[What should I expect on (or before) my official start date?](javascript:;)
You should expect to visit the Human Resources Office (Kaslik Campus – Building G – 3rd floor) on or even before your official start date to complete all necessary hiring paperwork. Your paperwork will include ID Photocopy (or passport for foreigners), recent passport photo, photocopy of diplomas obtained, photocopy of professional experience certification from previous employer and list of publications.   
  

### Human Resources Office
  * Opening hours: from 8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. and from 2:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. (closed on USEK holidays)
  * Location on the plan: building G – 3rd floor
  * Contacts:  
E-mail: hr@usek.edu.lb   
Tel.: (+961) 9 600 185  
Fax: (+961) 9 600 181 


[What benefits are available for faculty at USEK?](javascript:;)
USEK offers a comprehensive Faculty Benefits Package, which includes health coverage, retirement, and School allowance, and University Educational Scholarship.  
  
For more details, please visit the following link: [USEK Policy Details](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/usek-policy-details?name=USEK-POLICY-00005)
[Who can I speak with to discuss benefits?](javascript:;)
The Human Resources Office is available to discuss benefits with all new faculty. Please contact Ms. Josette Saliba on her email address josettesaliba@usek.edu.lb or on her office number (+961) 9 600 186.
[What should I know about parking?](javascript:;)
Parking enforcement will begin no later than the first day of the academic year. Campus parking requires a permit. You may obtain a permanent faculty parking permit by appearing in person at the HR Office and presenting your USEK Identification card and a copy of your car registration car for accurate information related to your vehicle (vehicle license plate number, make, model, color, and year).
[HELP! Is there support for building my course page?](javascript:;)
Yes! The Center for Teaching and Learning (LTEC) manages teaching tools, course design assistance, and professional development for teaching. There are a variety of resources to cover essential topics that include in- person workshops offered by LTEC to assist faculty. Contact LTEC at (+961) 9 600 203 or ltec@usek.edu.lb  
The IT Service Desk is also available to provide additional assistance with technical support. Contact them at it.servicedesk@usek.edu.lb
[Who do I contact with IT issues?](javascript:;)
ITS manages a myriad of technology needs for university-wide applications, services, and infrastructure. They can be reached in person at building AC001, or [submit a ticket](https://ticket.usek.edu.lb/) at USEK Services
[What is my campus mailing address?](javascript:;)
The address to ship materials to your office is: Your Name  
Your Department   
P.O. Box 446 | Jounieh | Lebanon
[How do I access my university email?](javascript:;)
Upon confirmation of your recruitment, the HR office shares by email with each newly recruited faculty the credentials related to USEK accounts to facilitate their on-boarding process (USEK ID, Username, USEK Email and password (to be reset).  
  
You can access your University email through the USEK Webmail link, which can be found on the University Intranet [MyUsek - Home](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/) and the University website
[Where do I go to build my course webpage?](javascript:;)
Moodle is the campus learning management system. Login and start building your courses right away by visiting the USEK website. Click on Quick links and enter the E-learning portal by navigating to Home | USEK | eLearning  
  
By using your USEK account, you should connect to the [E-learning platform](https://elearning.usek.edu.lb/).
[How do I access Moodle and add activities?](javascript:;)
1. Log in   
url: elearning.usek.edu.lb   
Username: username@usek.edu.lb   
Password: same password as for the email and the Wi-Fi at USEK   
  
2. Go to Dashboard   
Your course will appear here.   
  
3. Under Course Overview, there is a Filter tool, click on it and choose “In progress.”   
Your current courses will appear.  
  
4. Click on a specific course to get to the course page   
  
5. In the settings panel on top right of the page click on “turn editing on”.   
  
6. Start adding your activities   
a. Assignments (where students can post their work)   
b. Forum (for questions and answer)   
c. File (to add a file; but you can also drag and drop directly on the course page)   
d. URL (to add a link to a webpage, a document on a SharePoint, a video, and audio, etc….)   
  
7. Assignment Activity   
Select “Assignment” then click on “Add” to access the assignment settings page.   
After all options are defined, click on “Save and return to course”.   
  
8. Forum Activity   
Select “Forum” then click on “Add”.  
After all options are defined, click on “Save and return to course”.   
  
9. File Resource   
You can drag and drop the file to the course page directly or Select “File” and the click on “Add”.  
After all options are defined, click on “Save and return to course”.   
  
10. URL Resource   
Select “URL” then click on “Add”.  
After all options are defined, click on “Save and return to course”.
[How do I use Microsoft teams?](javascript:;)
1. Download and Installation  
a) If you don’t have Microsoft Teams, download it from the following link: [Download Microsoft Teams Desktop and Mobile Apps | Microsoft Teams](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-teams/download-app)   
b) Install the application.  
c) Sign in using USEK email & password.  
  
2. Create your course, click on Join or create Teams, enter Class, enter the name of your course, then add the students to the class by using their USEK email addresses or by their names.  
  
3. During the Meeting (Class), the following options can be used:  
a) Mute and unmute audio and video for any student.  
b) Share the desktop, any opened window separately or whiteboard for free hand drawing.  
c) Record the conference to be able to share the related link on Moodle.  
d) Show meeting notes for better communication with students.  
e) Show participants to display the list of students in the meeting.
[Can the library support me in my role as a faculty member?](javascript:;)
Yes! Teaching and research in today’s complex information environment demand an academic library that pays attention to what faculty members need to do their work.  
For example, digital collections have significantly increased this past year, offering more new titles, backfiles and full text articles. The library offers growing collections and other resources at the faculty’s disposal.  
For more details about the support provided by the Library to faculty members, please visit the following link: [USEK Library | Faculty](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/faculty)  

[I found a resource for my course at the library. Can I "reserve" it?](javascript:;)
Yes! Staff members assist faculty in placing course materials on reserve for classes each semester. Please visit the following link for more information: [USEK Library | Place Materials on Reserve](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/place-materials-on-reserve)
[How do I receive guidance on locating intramural funding?](javascript:;)
The Office of Deputy President for Research acts as a one-stop shop for several intramural funding mechanisms by managing the dissemination, submission, review and award for these opportunities. For more information, contact at dp.research@usek.edu.lb
[Who can I contact with general questions about external grants?](javascript:;)
If you have any question related to grant pre-award, award, or post-award, please contact the Grants and Projects Unit (GPU) at gpu@usek.edu.lb
[How do I develop a budget for the external grant proposal?](javascript:;)
The Grants and Projects Unit GPU can help you with the mechanics of proposal preparation, budget development, submission, as well as contracting, and project management through different stages. Contact GPU at (+961) 9 600 319 or gpu@usek.edu.lb
[How can I protect research involving new technology and/or innovation brought to the market?](javascript:;)
The Office of Technology Transfer identifies, protects, and commercializes university research and intellectual property and works closely with faculty, students, and staff to help bring new technology and innovation to market. Contact Dr. Sandy Rihana at (+961) 9 600 948 or email: technology.transfer@usek.edu.lb

Welcome to Faculty Affairs at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK).   
  
From recruitment to retirement and beyond, we work collaboratively with all campus stakeholders to develop and maintain an outstanding and diverse community of academics.  
  
Within the Office of the Provost, we do this by initiating programs that support career development, enhance instruction abilities, promote research, and provide opportunities for collaboration. We also oversee the application of faculty policies and guidelines, including those related to faculty appointments, assessments, and promotions, as well as appeals and grievances. This office also maintains the Faculty Handbook, oversees and monitors the faculty annual review process, supports the transition to retirement and manages the emeritus processes.

USEK Faculty Handbook is a comprehensive guide designed to support and empower you in your role as a faculty member at USEK. Within these pages, you will find invaluable resources and information to help you navigate the various aspects of academic life and teaching responsibilities. It is designed to present general information about the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), and some of the more important University policies and practices as they apply to the Faculty of the University. Content is intentionally brief where possible, more expansive when necessary, and provides resources for additional information including relevant links.

##  Skills Development Center (SDC) 
### 1. Mission
The Skills Development Center (SDC) at USEK empowers individuals through upskilling and reskilling initiatives, providing them with practical knowledge and hands-on skills essential for success in today’s dynamic job market. We address the specific needs of our local community and the wider region by offering tailored, short-term training programs aligned with industry demands. Our commitment extends to supporting trainees with the necessary knowledge and equipment to advance their careers.  
  

### 2. Vision
The Skills Development Center (SDC) at USEK is driven by a vision to revolutionize the way individuals engage with the job market, transforming challenges into opportunities through a skill-based approach. We are dedicated to equipping our community with the practical knowledge and hands-on skills required to excel in today’s and tomorrow’s dynamic and competitive environments. Our goal is to create an ecosystem where cutting-edge training and industry demands converge, by focusing exclusively on market-relevant training programs. The SDC aims to bridge the gap between traditional education and the real-world needs of the workforce, ensuring that every trainee is not just employable, but primed to lead and innovate.  
  

### 3. Core Principles
  * **Skills Enhancement**  
We are committed to providing high-quality, industry-relevant training that equips our participants with the competencies and capabilities needed to excel in their chosen fields.
  * **Employability**  
Our focus is on increasing the employability of our trainees by emphasizing practical, market-driven skills that directly translate into job opportunities. Our training programs are designed to bridge the gap between education and employment.
  * **Upskilling and Reskilling**  
We recognize the significance of upskilling and reskilling in today’s rapidly evolving job market. Our mission extends beyond initial training to supporting individuals throughout their careers, helping them stay current and adaptable or facilitating career shifts in response to the evolving job landscape.

  

### 4. Upcoming Trainings
**Python Programming Training  
**As part of its mission to empower the community with cutting-edge skills, the Skills Development Center (SDC) offers the Python Programming Training program. Delivered in collaboration with the Mouna Bustros Foundation (FMB), CME, and Holcom Group, this program provides participants with practical Python skills for personal and professional growth.  
  
The training is designed to accommodate diverse learners, from beginners to advanced professionals, aiming to enhance their competencies in programming, data analysis, and automation. Participants will gain industry-relevant knowledge through hands-on sessions conducted exclusively on campus.  
  
**Round 2 – February 2025**  
Beginner Level – PCEP

[ Apply Now ](https://forms.gle/cBQtYVv6yvKB2s2c9%0A)

[ Apply Now ](https://forms.gle/fxsy7scC4WoqWhdp9%0A)
  
  
**Round 1 – May 2024**  
A 40-hour beginner-level training session was successfully delivered in Kaslik.  
  

### 5. Connect With Us!
At the Skills Development Center, we are committed to expanding our training portfolio to meet your needs. Have a training suggestion? Your input is invaluable in helping us provide the most relevant and impactful training programs.  
  
You Name It, We Train It.

##  Integral Human Development Center 
**THE CONCEPT OF INTEGRAL HUMAN DEVELOPMENT**  
  
The concept of integral human development, primarily promoted by His Holiness Pope Paul VI in his encyclical Populorum Progressio (1967) following the Second Vatican Council, was re-emphasized by His Holiness Pope Benedict XVI in the encyclical Caritas in veritate (2009).   
  
In August 2016, His Holiness Pope Francis announced the creation of the Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development. This new dicastery of the Roman Curia brings together the following four dicasteries: the Pontifical Council for Justice and Peace, the Pontifical Council for the Pastoral Care of Migrants and Itinerant People, the Pontifical Council “Cor Unum” (for Human and Christian Development), and the Pontifical Council for Health Care Workers.  
  
The new dicastery is called upon to express the Church’s deep interest in the fields of justice, peace and the safeguarding of the whole of creation, as well as in health and works of charity.  
**  
THE CREATION OF THE USEK CENTER FOR INTEGRAL HUMAN DEVELOPMENT (THE POPE FRANCIS INSTITUTE FOR INTEGRAL HUMAN DEVELOPMENT)**  
  
In the wake of its vocation and mission to promote the social teaching of the Catholic Church, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) decided to create a center for promoting the concept of integral human development and its implementation at the pastoral and social levels in Lebanon. Through this initiative, USEK expresses the Church’s keen interest in the various fields of human development, justice, peace, and the safeguarding of the whole of creation: “the whole man and [...] every man”.  
  
**THEORETICAL AND METHODOLOGICAL BASIS FOR THE ACADEMIC ACTIVITY OF THE USEK CENTER FOR INTEGRAL HUMAN DEVELOPMENT**  
  
The theoretical and methodological basis for the academic activity of the center is multidisciplinary in nature and tackles the concept of integral human development, at the level of groups and territories, through anthropology, ethnology, the psycho-sociology of groups, socioeconomic development, the sociology of organizations, religious sociology, the sociology of cultural heritage, geography, history, etc. The center aims to make the social teaching of the Church known and to put it into practice by fostering an interdisciplinary dialogue between the different social systems.  
  
**OBJECTIVES OF THE USEK CENTER FOR INTEGRAL HUMAN DEVELOPMENT**  
  
The objectives of the USEK Center for Integral Human Development are as follows: 
  * To master the social teaching of the Catholic Church in its fields of competence.
  * To monitor and observe the evolution of the sociocultural reality in its fields of competence by establishing the appropriate observatories.
  * To establish a development database. 
  * To undertake action-oriented research with development as its end purpose.
  * To develop and execute local development projects.
  * To assess the evolution of the sociocultural reality on a continuous basis in line with the teachings of the Catholic Church and vice versa.
  * To generate and continuously promote teaching adapted to the evolution of society.
  * To offer training for those involved in the relevant pastoral work.
  * To spread the teachings of the Church.
  * To repopulate the Maronite and Christian countryside based on a modern and productive strategy.
  * To encourage the sharing and exchange of experiences and testimonies in its fields of competence.

##  Institutional Research and Assessment Office 
### Mission and Vision
**Mission**  
The Institutional Research and Assessment Office (previously known as Quality Assurance and Institutional Effectiveness Office) supports the University to achieve its mission through various initiatives such as planning, assessing, and improving administrative and academic performance in alignment with international accreditation standards, where applicable. The office collects and analyzes data that are disseminated for decision making and reporting purposes.  
  
**Vision**  
The vision of the Office is to become a national and regional model through assessment and accreditation.  
  

### Accreditation
The Institutional Research and Assessment Office supports International Institutional Accreditation on both European and American levels. It also promotes and provides support for program accreditation by serving as a resource, for the academic units, on matters pertaining to assessment and curricular and program improvement.  
For more information, click [here](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/accreditation).  
  

### Institutional Research
USEK's Institutional Research and Assessment Office plays a pivotal role in promoting academic excellence and data-driven decision-making. This scope includes thorough data gathering, in-depth analysis, and insightful reporting on a range of aspects related to the University's operations. This includes monitoring students’ academic progress, analyzing the success of programs, and evaluating institutional outcomes. The office enables the institution to strategically plan, carry out improvements, and fulfill its mission and goals by giving fast and reliable information. Our commitment to transparency is demonstrated by the release of the University Factbook, an extensive tool that offers useful data to a range of internal and external stakeholders.  
  

### Assessment
The IRA Office carries out systematic assessment of student learning outcomes, academic programs, and institutional effectiveness. To get a thorough grasp of the educational impact, the office collects both qualitative and quantitative data using a range of assessment tools. This includes designing and administering surveys with different stakeholders to assess course and program-level effectiveness, satisfaction with academic offerings, and alignment of programs with the highest standards of quality and the job market. The main focus is to ensure attainment of program educational objectives and outcomes by providing faculty and administrators with detailed feedback and practical insights and assisting in enhancing curriculum design and teaching approaches.   
  

### Adherence to Quality Networks
USEK is institutionalizing its quality culture, through its adherence to the most well-known international quality networks that promote excellence and share the best practices adopted by American, European and regional universities:

The bylaws here outline the regulations, policies, and procedures, designed to protect, and maintain standards and transparency, and outline the rights and responsibilities of institutional actors for the University including:

  * The USEK Board of Trustees

##  Doctorate in Business Administration 
English 
60 credits
## Courses
[ Major Courses](javascript:;)
[.Thesis Dissertation](javascript:;)
45 credits
[DBA710Management Research for DBA](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course provides an in-depth introduction to the principles and practices of management research tailored for DBA students. It covers advanced methodologies, data collection, and analysis techniques essential for addressing complex business issues. Students will develop skills in identifying research problems, conducting literature reviews, and designing high-quality research proposals, with an emphasis on ethical considerations and academic rigor in management research. 
[DBA720Research Design](javascript:;)
3 credits
This course focuses on the foundations and principles of designing effective research studies in business and management. Students will learn to develop research questions, hypotheses, and study designs suited to address real-world business challenges. Emphasis is placed on various research design approaches, including experimental, quasi-experimental, longitudinal, and case study methodologies, as well as considerations for validity, reliability, and ethical integrity in research. 
[DBA730Theoretical Perspectives of Strategy and Supply Chain](javascript:;)
1 credits
In this course, students will explore advanced theoretical perspectives in strategic management and supply chain operations. Topics include competitive strategy, resource-based views, network theories, and global supply chain dynamics. Through case studies and critical analysis, students will examine how strategic frameworks apply to supply chain management, understanding the complexities of global operations and the interplay between strategy and supply chain performance. 
[DBA740Innovation for Sustainable Growth: Theory, and Practice](javascript:;)
1 credits
This course delves into theories and practices of innovation with a focus on achieving sustainable growth. Students will explore innovation strategies, models for sustainable business practices, and approaches to managing innovation in organizations. Case studies and real-world applications will help students understand how to foster a culture of innovation, drive sustainable growth, and balance social, environmental, and economic goals. 
[DBA750Leading Change & Organizational Transformations ](javascript:;)
1 credits
This course examines the theories, models, and strategies behind leading effective change and transformation within organizations. Students will study frameworks for organizational change, the psychology of change, and leadership practices that promote resilience and adaptability. Through practical exercises, students will gain insights into managing resistance, communicating change, and fostering organizational buy-in, preparing them to lead transformations successfully in complex business environments 
[DBA760Fundamentals of Financial & Extra-financial Performance](javascript:;)
1 credits
This course covers the essential principles of financial and extra-financial performance metrics, including environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors. Students will learn how to analyze financial performance using key indicators, as well as assess the impact of non-financial factors on overall business sustainability and long-term value creation. The course emphasizes the integration of financial and extra-financial data to guide strategic decision-making. 
[DBA770Research Workshops I](javascript:;) [DBA775Research Workshops II](javascript:;) [DBA810Qualitative Research Methods](javascript:;)
3 credits
This course provides an in-depth study of qualitative research methodologies applicable to business research. Students will learn techniques such as interviews, focus groups, case studies, and ethnography, as well as methods for coding and analyzing qualitative data. Emphasis is placed on designing robust qualitative studies, ensuring validity and reliability, and applying qualitative insights to solve complex business challenges. 
[DBA820Quantitative Research Methods ](javascript:;)
3 credits
This course introduces students to advanced quantitative research techniques commonly used in business and management research. Topics include survey design, data sampling, statistical analysis, and the use of software tools for data analysis (e.g., SPSS, R, or Stata). Students will gain proficiency in interpreting statistical findings and applying quantitative methods to inform decision-making, with a focus on producing reliable and actionable research outcomes. 
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/Uploaded%20Images/20250612Excelia.png)In partnership with Excelia Business School (France), USEK Business School (UBS) offers a prestigious Dual Doctorate in Business Administration (DBA) program tailored for senior professionals who aspire to lead transformative change in an increasingly complex business environment.  
  
The mission of the Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) is to advance the frontiers of business knowledge by providing cutting-edge research training, mentorship from world-class faculty, and opportunities for scholarly publication to aspiring academicians and industry thought leaders.  
  
Learning Goal 1: Graduate will acquire an advanced knowledge of the latest academic theories, concepts, techniques, and applications in their field of study.  
Learning Goal 2: Graduates will develop advanced research skills through practical experience, and special projects.  
Learning Goal 3: Graduates will acquire critical thinking, problem-solving, and analytical abilities to address complex business challenges   
Learning Goal 4: Graduates will demonstrate a commitment to ethical principles in both research and decision-making.

##  Strategic Planning 
### A Transformational Journey: USEK Strategic Plan for Academic Excellence and Global Leadership
The strategic plan of the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) centers on enhancing academic reputation through proactive recruitment of constituents, cultivating an innovative and entrepreneurial mindset, and establishing distinctive academic excellence. By aligning our efforts with these goals, we will pave the way for becoming the transformative institution that prepares future leaders in Lebanon and beyond.  
  
Vision: The vision of this strategic plan is to become a transformative institution renowned for exceptional academic excellence, preparing the next generation of leaders in Lebanon.  
  
Purpose: To achieve our vision, we will focus on three strategic priorities: recruiting for excellence, cultivating innovation, and strengthening academic excellence.  
  
Strategic Priority 1: Striving to Recruit for Excellence  
  
Strategic Priority 2: Promoting Innovative and Entrepreneurial Governance   
  
Strategic Priority 3: Strengthening the University’s Distinctive Catholic Maronite Academic Excellence
