[Frequently Asked Questions](javascript:;)
**1. I have applied for a scholarship. When will I be notified of the application result?**  
Notification of the scholarship results will be sent to you via email. You can expect to receive this notification by May 11, 2026, for Fall Semester 2026–2027 applications.  
  
**2. What must I do to maintain my scholarship?**  
To retain the scholarship, it is crucial to uphold the academic standards for which it was awarded. This entails maintaining a minimum GPA of 80/100 for Bachelor's degree students and 85/100 for Master's degree students.  
  
**3. Does USEK offer specific guidance and services for international students?**  
Certainly! As an international student at USEK, you will receive personalized support to seamlessly integrate into the university community and ensure a successful experience. Upon arrival, you will attend an orientation session for all new students, as well as a welcome session specifically designed for international students. These sessions will provide you with essential information about your stay at USEK and life in Lebanon. Additionally, through our [Be-A-Buddy program](https://www.usek.edu.lb/internationl/be-a-buddy-program), you will be paired with a Lebanese student who will assist you with administrative procedures and introduce you to the vibrant student life at USEK.  
  
**4. Will I receive assistance in applying for a visa or residency permit and finding accommodation in Lebanon?**  
Yes, selected applicants will receive guidance on applying for a visa or residency permit in Lebanon. USEK's on-campus dormitories are available for female students only. For more information, you can contact the Student Affairs Office (SAO) at sao@usek.edu.lb. If you are interested in off-campus housing, we can provide you with a list of dorms and studios in the area. Please note that USEK does not assume any responsibility regarding any external dorm owners or managers.  
  
**5. What makes a good motivation letter?**  
A strong motivation letter must effectively express genuine enthusiasm, highlight relevant qualifications and aspirations, and demonstrate a clear vision for the future. It should explain how receiving the scholarship aligns with your academic and career goals, highlighting relevant experiences and accomplishments that demonstrate your qualifications and commitment. Additionally, it should address the scholarship criteria and reflect how your values and aspirations resonate with those of the scholarship and USEK. Overall, the letter should be concise, professional, and persuasive, leaving a strong impression on the Selection Committee.  
  
**6. What makes a good letter of recommendation?**   
A compelling letter of recommendation must provide specific insights into your academic prowess, personal attributes, and potential for success in your studies. It should be written by someone familiar with your academic achievements and can offer a credible assessment of your qualifications, such as a school principal for undergraduate applicants, and a professor or dean for graduate applicants. The letter should include concrete examples and anecdotes that highlight your strengths, contributions, and unique qualities relevant to your field of study.   
  
**7. Who can I contact if I need more information?**   
For more information, you can contact the International Affairs Office (IAO) at internationalscholarships@usek.edu.lb

#### Mission
The Doctorate Program seeks to help student become self-directed, evidence-based learners through the ability to access and critically evaluate the reliability of all databases and resources related to music subjects.  
Originality will lie more in the way in which theoretical and conceptual understandings are applied in managerial and organizational contexts than in simple extension of those theories and concepts.  
In addition to the applied character of the doctorate thesis, it is also action-based and transformational in that students will be challenged to change their managerial practices.

##  USEK-NAM Scholarship Program 
### Overview
The USEK-NAM Scholarship offers up to 12 students each summer the opportunity to study for one Summer Session at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) in Lebanon.   
  

### What the Scholarship Covers
The USEK–NAM Scholarship provides: 
  * a tuition waiver for the designated summer session courses.
  * on-campus accommodation in USEK’s student housing.
  * a $500 travel contribution from the National Apostolate of Maronites (NAM), awarded to each recipient once enrollment at USEK is confirmed, as partial coverage of their travel expenses to Lebanon.

  
  
Note: The scholarship applies specifically to tuition and housing for the Summer Session. Additional courses, private instruction, meals, and personal expenses are not covered and remain the responsibility of the student.  
  

### Eligibility Criteria
Applicants must meet all of the following requirements: 
  * Be at least 18 years old.
  * Be a citizen or legal permanent resident of the United States.
  * Be currently enrolled in a four-year undergraduate program at an accredited U.S. college or university.
  * Maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale.
  * Be an active NAM member.
  * Demonstrate an interest in studying in Lebanon.
  * Be enrolled in a major compatible with USEK’s academic programs.

  

### Application and Contact Information
To access the application form and further details, please visit the [official NAM scholarship page](https://www.namaronites.org/scholarship-programs)

## USEK Law Journal
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publications?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/about?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/aim-and-scope?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/editorial-board?parent=1) [](http://webapp.usek.edu.lb/k1/forms/lawjournal/Subscribe.aspx?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-ethics?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-guidelines-for-the-journal-of-law?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/contact?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/submitting-a-paper?parent=1)
Launched in 1992 by the School of Law and Political Sciences, the USEK Law Journal aims to provide relevant scholarly articles pertaining to changes and contemporary developments on all legal aspects. It is published by PUSEK, the USEK Publication Office.  
  
Indexed on Scopus since 2019, the Journal strives to enhance progressive research on the most relevant legal issues through a stringent intellectual selection and editing process. With more than 250 articles published by 220 authors, the Journal is amongst the most influential law journals in the MENA region.  
  
An expert editorial board has spent more than 25 years searching for articles with strong academic and legal values that maintain a consistently high standard of peer reviewed publications.

## USEK Law Journal
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publications?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/about?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/aim-and-scope?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/editorial-board?parent=1) [](http://webapp.usek.edu.lb/k1/forms/lawjournal/Subscribe.aspx?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-ethics?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-guidelines-for-the-journal-of-law?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/contact?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/submitting-a-paper?parent=1)
The USEK Law Journal, launched in 1992 and Scopus indexed since 2019, is a yearly peer-reviewed trilingual journal, aiming to provide an opportunity for the legal community to keep abreast of new ideas and the progress of legal reforms.  
  
Topics cover all areas related to law and political sciences. All papers, accepted in English, French or Arabic, are subject to double blind international peer review. For more details, please refer to our peer review policy.  
  
All publications may be viewed and downloaded for $40 per issue and $10 per article.  
  
We invite you to explore our website and to contact us with questions and comments.  
  
Articles for publication in the USEK Law Journal can be [submitted online](http://webapp.usek.edu.lb/k1/forms/lawjournal/Subscribe.aspx?parent=1).  
  
Articles in the USEK Law Journal represent the opinions of their authors, and do not essentially reflect the views of the members of the Editorial Board.

##  Outgoing Mobility 
USEK offers its students the chance to broaden their academic and cultural horizons by taking part in an international exchange program, through bilateral agreements signed with prestigious partner institutions across the globe.  
  
Studying abroad is one of the most enriching experiences students can have, allowing them to experience different styles of education in a multicultural environment. They will learn new languages, meet people from around the world, and form lifetime memories and friendships.   
  

[How to Apply?](javascript:;)
Any regular student enrolled at USEK may participate in an international exchange for one or two semesters, provided they meet the following eligibility criteria:  
  
1. Undergraduate students: 
  * Must have completed a minimum of 30 validated credits.
  * Must have good academic standing and not be under probation. 
  * Must not be in their final semester of studies.

  
  
2. Graduate students: 
  * Must have completed 9 to 12 validated credits.
  * Must have good academic standing and not be under probation.
  * Must not be in their final semester of studies.

  
  
Check the list of USEK’s partner institutions to select your preferred mobility destination.  
  
Once you have chosen your destination, submit the [Study Abroad Application Form](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/app/student-services) before the stated deadline.  
  
Review the course catalog of the host institution.  
  
Consult the academic advisor at USEK to select your courses and set the Learning Agreement.  
  
Send your signed Learning Agreement to your advisor, who will forward it to the Associate Dean for approval before sending it to the International Relations Office (IAO), which will manage the nomination process with the partner institution.
[Application Deadlines](javascript:;)
**March 15** for mobility in the Fall Semester.  
  
**October 15** for mobility in the Spring Semester.  

[Financial Conditions](javascript:;)
The student remains enrolled at USEK and continues to pay tuition fees there.  
  
The student is exempt from paying tuition fees at the host university.  
  
The student is responsible for all other expenses related to the mobility period, including visa fees, airfare, international insurance, accommodation, and transportation, among others.  
  
The latest scholarship announcements and calls for applications are frequently shared in the Student Mobility section.  
  
For more information: outgoingmobility@usek.edu.lb.

# International
[](javascript:;)
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/international/international-affairs)[](https://outlook.office.com/book/StudentsStudyAbroadConsultancy@net.usek.edu.lb/s/cTeW5Fibx02KlNKEX3Q0wQ2?ismsaljsauthenabled)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/erasmus-international-credits-mobility)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/memberships)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/international-summer-school)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/study-at-usek)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/incoming-mobility)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/outgoing-mobility)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/international/opportunities-abroad)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/faculty/staff-mobility-2025-2026)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/international/semester-abroad-opportunities)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/usek-diplomacy-academy)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/ajyal-program)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/internationl/be-a-buddy-program)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/global-engagement-certificate)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/international/usek-nam-scholarship-program)[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/international/news)
##  Be-a-Buddy Program 
[ REGISTER NOW ](https://myusek.usek.edu.lb/app/student-services)
  

### What is the “Be-a-Buddy Program”?
Arriving in a new country and a new university can be both exciting and challenging. To ensure a smooth transition at USEK, the International Affairs Office (IAO) has introduced the Be-a-Buddy Program. This initiative pairs you with a current USEK student who will assist you with practical information about the University, guide you through student life, and support your settling-in process. Our Buddies are dedicated volunteers who will be with you every step of the way, both before your arrival and throughout your stay in Lebanon.  
  

### What are my responsibilities as a Buddy?
As a Buddy, you will: 
  * help exchange students adjust to their new surroundings.
  * introduce them to other Lebanese peers.
  * help with administrative tasks.
  * guide them around the campus to familiarize themselves with it.
  * assist in finding accommodation.
  * organize leisure activities, like sightseeing 

  
  
Why is having a Buddy important for incoming international students?<  
A Buddy will: 
  * help you know more about USEK.
  * address any concerns or uncertainties.
  * help you find accommodation, nearby banks, stores, and essential services.
  * introduce you to Lebanon and its culture.
  * show you popular tourist spots.
  * accompany you on leisure activities.
  * connect you with experts when necessary.
  * simply be your friend.

  
  

### Why become a Buddy as a USEK student?
Joining the Be-a-Buddy Program offers numerous benefits for USEK students, including: 
  * meeting students from diverse cultures and backgrounds.
  * improving your language and communication skills.
  * sharing experiences and discovering new perspectives.
  * supporting peers who are adjusting to an unfamiliar environment.
  * making new friendships.
  * participating in international activities.
  * earning 75 points towards your USEK Global Engagement Certificate.

  
  

### For how long can I be a Buddy?
You can be a Buddy for one semester or even longer if you wish.

### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publications?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/about?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/aim-and-scope?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/editorial-board?parent=1) [](http://webapp.usek.edu.lb/k1/forms/lawjournal/Subscribe.aspx?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-ethics?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-guidelines-for-the-journal-of-law?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/contact?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/submitting-a-paper?parent=1)
[Peer review policy](javascript:;)
The purpose of a peer review is to help selecting the highest quality articles for publication. It is an effective and objective form of research evaluation by specialists in the same field. Our aim is to publish papers that might influence thinking in a specific field in law, in order to maintain the high standards of USEK Law Journal. To maintain high‐quality publication, all submissions undergo an arduous review process following the procedure outlined below.
[The review process](javascript:;)
All papers are assessed by the Journal’s editorial committee on their originality, appropriate methodology, accuracy, and suitability for publication. Papers that do not meet our general criteria are rejected without any external review and their authors are informed within five weeks of receipt.
[Type of peer review](javascript:;)
_USEK Law Journal_ adopts a double‐blind review procedure, where both the reviewer and the author remain anonymous during the procedure to avoid any conflict of interest.
[Peer‐reviewers selection](javascript:;)
Peer‐reviewers are experts in a specific field who will provide a constructive and balanced review of a paper. They are selected from around the world. It’s vital to get global perspectives on manuscripts during the peer review process. International reviewers should provide new insights on authors work. They have the required knowledge and experience to fulfill their mission.   
The reason behind such expertise is to make sure that the manuscript would stand up to intense scrutiny. In addition, our reviewers’ database is being constantly updated.
[Reviewers’ reports](javascript:;)
Reviewers have the responsibility to assess the articles for: 
  * Uniqueness, novelty, weight of their input and the use of an appropriate methodology. 
  * Interest to topics combining human rights and practice. 
  * International suitability.


[Confidentiality](javascript:;)
Protecting confidentiality is a major concern in our Journal to ensure that reviewers feel safe and provide honest open opinions. Reviewers’ names are withheld from authors and from each other. For some mistakes would be eliminated from later versions, all ideas and results in the papers are protected until the paper is published. Articles submitted to our Journal would only be available to editors and reviewers.
[Editing guidelines](javascript:;)
Authors are invited to respect the publication guidelines of the journal.   
By submitting their papers, authors accept all necessary editing operated to their paper by the journal’s editorial board prior to publishing.   
The editorial board ensures communication with the authors over any necessary substantial modifications.  
Authors should provide complementary information required by the editorial board, as well as retractions or corrections pointed out by the board.
[Plagiarism](javascript:;)
Fighting plagiarism is a substantial value of our journal. Jurists and scholars prosper in openness and honesty.   
Our journal’s reputation is essential to our success as jurists, and we are conscious that a serious, tangible risk of plagiarism will put our reputation at risk.   
Papers are checked for plagiarism and self-plagiarism using Turnitin database.   
Plagiarism is not tolerated. Papers with plagiarism will be refused.   
If despite the thorough pre-publishing examination, plagiarism is discovered after publication, the journal reserves its right to publish all necessary corrections, clarifications, retractions or apologies.  
Depending on the gravity of the plagiarism, further steps would be taken, as permitted by the law.
[Copyright](javascript:;)
Research papers and articles are protected and would not be accessible to anyone outside the editorial board or reviewers before their publishing.   
Authors are entitled to their author’s moral rights according to the law. Authors assign to the journal the right to publish and reproduce their papers once accepted.   
The journal has a copyright over all the material it publishes: none of this material may be reproduced in whole or in part, stored in a retrieval system, or transmitted in any form or by any means, without the permission of the editor in chief.
[Access and archiving](javascript:;)
USEK Law Journal is published yearly, both online and in paper version.   
  
Paper issues can be bought at the USEK bookshop.  
  
Subscription for the online version is available [here](http://webapp.usek.edu.lb/k1/forms/lawjournal/Subscribe.aspx?parent=1).  
  
The preservation of the published issues is secured by electronic back-up in the archives of USEK.

The Book of Psalms was printed in the monastery of Saint Anthony of Qozhaya in 1610. Since it is the first book ever printed in the Eastern part of the Ottoman Empire, it is considered as one of the most distinguished works in the history of typography.

### Preventive measures against coronavirus (COVID-19) @ USEK Library
**1.** USEK Library is closed until further notice.  
**2.** Electronic Resources are accessible to all USEK community from off-campus.  
**3.** Document Delivery Service (article requests) is available to all USEK community.  
**4.** All borrowed books have been renewed until 31 May, 2020.  
**5.** For help and other reference services, use the library chat service, or send an email to reference@usek.edu.lb.  
  
⚠️ Online research consultation (Refworks, APA, etc.): meet with our reference librarian online via Microsoft Teams or Skype. Please book your appointment at least 24 hours in advance by contacting us on: reference@usek.edu.lb. ⚠️  
  

#### Stay safe and check back for updates!

## USEK Law Journal
### In this section
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publications?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/about?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/aim-and-scope?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/editorial-board?parent=1) [](http://webapp.usek.edu.lb/k1/forms/lawjournal/Subscribe.aspx?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-ethics?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-guidelines-for-the-journal-of-law?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/contact?parent=1) [](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/submitting-a-paper?parent=1)
**For authors**  
By submitting a paper, the author confirms his/her authorship of the manuscript, and agrees to USEK Law Journal guidelines and policies included on this site.   
Authors are not allowed to publish the same paper(s) in more than one journal.   
Authors of published papers are entitled to a paper copy of the issue in which their paper was published, and to five single print-outs of their paper.  
  
**Submitting guidelines**  
The process of submitting papers to the USEK Law Journal is free of charge.   
Papers must be submitted in Word format.   
The journal accepts papers in English, French or Arabic. For all papers, authors must provide: 
  * An English title for the paper 
  * An abstract in English (no more than 200 words). 
  * A list of references at the end of the paper. 
  * Their academic titles and their address. 

  
Authors are invited to follow the [Publication guidelines](https://www.usek.edu.lb/law-journal/publication-guidelines-for-the-journal-of-law?parent=1) of the Law Journal.   
Papers or abstracts of papers can be submitted online via this page, or sent by email to: lawjournal@usek.edu.lb

##  Legal Skills Competitions 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/academics/school-of-law-and-political-sciences)
Legal skills competitions are an important method of developing and practicing a wide variety of legal competencies, including research and analysis, legal writing, teamwork, and oral argument. Another equally important side of those competitions is the opportunity it provides for building friendships and professional networks throughout the global legal community.   
  
USEK Faculty of Law highly encourages interested and eligible students to participate in local, regional, and national competitions.  
  

### Faculty of Law Established Legal Skills Competitions
Each year, USEK Faculty of Law authorizes student teams to participate in the following competitions: 
  * The Annual Willem C. Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot – Vienna, Austria
  * The Annual Willem C. Vis Middle East International Commercial Arbitration Moot – Pre-Vis Moot Middle East
  * Monroe E. Price Media Law Moot Court Competition – Oxford University, United Kingdom
  * International Criminal Court (ICC) Moot Competition – The Hague, The Netherlands

  

### Other Legal Skills Competition Opportunities
From year to year, the Faculty of Law also authorizes teams of students to participate in other Legal Skills Competitions. Students interested in participating in a competition other than one of the "established" competitions must first seek approval from the Faculty of Law by submitting an application no later than 90 days before the first submission deadline.   
  

### Expenses
The Faculty of Law pays reasonable travel expenses for participants to attend the regional round of the approved legal skills competition.  
  
  

[The Annual Willem C. Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot – Vienna, Austria](javascript:;)
The Annual Willem C. Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot is one of the most renowned moot competitions, dedicated to international commercial arbitration and cross-border litigation, drawing lawstudents from more than 300 law schools from around the world every year. The competition is judged by some of the world’s preeminent arbitrators, litigators, judges, and international law scholars.  
  
The competition is a simulation of a fictitious dispute over a sale of goods between companies in two imaginary countries. The applicable law will include law governing international arbitration, as well as the United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (“CISG”).  
  
Teams prepare written and oral pleadings arguing both the Claimant and Respondent positions.   
  
USEK Faculty of Law team consists of six participants, four of whom are oralists and two of whom are "of counsel"; the latter’s objective is to help with research and written submissions (Memoranda). The "of counsel" is also a backup oralist at the competition.   
  
Serving on the team is a two-semester commitment, beginning in the fall semester.   
  
Coach / Faculty Contact:  
Mrs. Myriam Eid  
myriameid@usek.edu.lb  
  
Prerequisites:  
Successful completion of the International Arbitration Course  
  
Selection:   
Tryouts for the team are held in summer, usually around end of August-beginning of September, and are open to students in good standing in their third or fourth year of law studies.   
  
Candidates should satisfy the following prerequisites: 
  * Be fluent in English, both written and spoken
  * Be used to public speaking
  * Have good research skills and sense of legal analysis
  * Have a high sense of discipline and dedication

  
Competition Timeline (25th Edition of the Vis Moot):  
(Check the competition website for exact dates.) 
  * Problem released: 6 October 2017
  * Deadline for submission of Claimant’s Memorandum: 7 December 2017
  * Deadline for submission of Respondent’s Memorandum: 18 January 2018
  * International Rounds: 23 till 29 March 2018

  
  
Academic credit:  
Five credits units (three credits in the fall semester; two credits in the spring semester)  
  
Meetings:  
Team members meet with their professor at least twice a week, but will be expected to meet additional times, including weekends, on an as-needed basis. Meetings will involve a combination of instruction, discussion, and practice.  
  
Expenses:  
USEK Faculty of Law pays reasonable travel expenses for participants to attend the international round of the competition in Vienna and at least one prior Pre-moot Round.  
  
  
**24th Annual Vis Moot - 7-14 April, 2017, Vienna**  
Preceded by the Permanent Court of Arbitration Premoot, 3-4 April, 2017, The Hague  
Team Members: George El Khoury, Michel Mansour, Adel Bou Younes, Nathalie Matta, Joyce Abi Abboud and Joan Samaha.  
  
**25th Annual Vis Moot – 23-29 March, 2018, Vienna**  
Upcoming event.
[The Annual Willem C. Vis Middle East International Commercial Arbitration Moot – Pre-Vis Moot Middle East](javascript:;)
The Annual Willem C. Vis Middle East International Commercial Arbitration Moot is a sister moot to the Annual Willem C. Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot that takes place every year in Vienna.   
  
USEK sends one team to compete in both, the Vis Moot in Vienna and the Middle East Pre-Moot.  
  
The same problem is used for both the Vienna and the Middle East moots, and USEK team typically present the same briefs for the two competitions.  
  
Serving on the team is a two-semester commitment, beginning in the fall semester.  
  
Coach / Faculty Contact:  
Mrs. Myriam Eid  
myriameid@usek.edu.lb  
  
**8th Annual Vis Middle East Pre-Moot 2018, Bahrain**  
19 - 23 February 2018  
Team Members: Albert Dakar, Stephanie Bou Chalhoub, Ingrid Ghanem, Rosabelle Saba, Fidele Kamel, Marina Ibrahim  
Awards: Runner Up (second place)  
  
**7TH Annual Vis Middle East Pre-Moot 2017, Kuwait**  
07 - 11 February 2017  
Team Members: Michel Mansour, Adel Bou Younes, Nathalie Matta, Joyce Abi Abboud and Joan Samaha.  
Awards: Semi Finalists (third place), Award for Best Oralist for Respondent (Joan Samaha)
[Monroe E. Price Media Law Moot Court Competition – Oxford University, United Kingdom](javascript:;)
Every year, the University of Oxford organizes the "Price Media Law Moot Court Programme", a competition that challenges students to engage in comparative research of legal standards at the national, regional and international levels, and to develop their arguments (in written and oral forms) on cutting-edge questions in media and Information, Communication and Technology law.   
  
The USEK team has to participate first at the Regional Rounds for the Middle East. After they qualify, they will participate in the International Rounds held in Oxford, England.  
  
Teams prepare written and oral pleadings arguing both the Applicant and Respondent positions.   
  
USEK Faculty of Law team consists of six participants, four of whom are oralists and two of whom are "of counsel"; the latter’s objective is to help with research and written submissions (Memoranda). The "of counsel" is also a backup oralist at the competition.   
  
Serving on the team is a two-semester commitment, beginning in the fall semester. The fall semester is mandatory as the team must pass through the Middle East Rounds. If the team is qualified, the International Rounds will be held during the spring semester.  
  
Coaches / Faculty Contact:  
Mr. Sean Mills  
seanmills@usek.edu.lb  
Dr. Marianne Hanna  
mariannehanna@usek.edu.lb   
  
Selection:   
Tryouts for the team are held in the beginning of the fall semester, usually around September, and are open to students in good standing in their second, third or fourth year of law studies.   
  
Candidates should satisfy the following prerequisites: 
  * Be fluent in English, both written and spoken
  * Be used to public speaking
  * Have good research skills and sense of legal analysis
  * Have a high level of discipline and dedication

  
Competition Timeline (11th Edition of the Price Media Moot Court):

  * Middle East Regional Rounds: 30 January till 2 February 2018
  * Qualification to the International Rounds Confirmed by: 19 February 2018
  * International Rounds: 9 till 13 April 2018

  
Academic credit:  
Three credits units (fall semester).   
  
Meetings:   
Team members meet with their professor at least twice a week, but will be expected to meet additional times, including weekends, on an as-needed basis. Meetings will involve a combination of instruction, discussion, and practice.  
  
Expenses:  
USEK Faculty of Law pays reasonable travel expenses for participants to attend the Middle East Rounds and International Rounds of the competition in Oxford once qualified.

Team Members: Alina Korkomaz, Rafca Nawfal, Marilyne Zgheib, Roana Tarabay, Rosette Mouawad  
The Team was the only Lebanese team nominated, after the Regional rounds, to participate in the International Rounds that will take place at Oxford University.

[The International Criminal Court (ICC) Moot Competition – The Hague, The Netherlands](javascript:;)
The Grotius Centre for International Legal Studies organizes annually in May “The International Criminal Court Moot Court Competition” in The Hague, in the Netherlands. During this competition, universities from all over the world are handed a problem with fictive facts, and they will stimulate the case as if the proceedings are held before the International Criminal Court (ICC).   
  
The Competition involves collaboration with judges from international courts and tribunals, professors of international (criminal) law, and other legal professionals. This network makes the ICC Moot Court Competition a realistic replica of ICC proceedings. The Competition’s case addresses fundamental issues of substantive and procedural international criminal law.  
  
Teams prepare written and oral pleadings arguing three positions: Defense Counsel, Office of the Prosecutor and Legal Representative for Victims.  
  
USEK Faculty of Law team consists of six participants, three of whom are oralists and three of whom are "of counsel"; the latter’s objective is to help with research and written submissions (Memorials). The "of counsel" is also a backup oralist at the competition.   
  
Serving on the team is a two-semester commitment, beginning in the fall semester.  
  
Team Manager:  
Dr. Ghada Karam  
ghadakaram@usek.edu.lb  
  
Selection:   
Tryouts for the team are held in the beginning of the fall semester, usually around September, and are open to students in good standing in their third or fourth year of law studies.   
  
Candidates should satisfy the following prerequisites: 
  * Be fluent in English, both written and spoken
  * Be used to public speaking
  * Have good research skills and sense of legal analysis
  * Have a high level of discipline and dedication

  
Competition Timeline (2018 Edition of the ICC Moot Court Competition):  
(Check the competition website for exact dates.) 
  * Problem released: 20 October 2017
  * Deadline for submission of the three memorials (Defense Counsel, Office of the Prosecutor and Legal Representative for Victims) : 26 February 2018
  * Oral Rounds: 27 May till 1 June 2018

Three credits units.  
  
Meetings:   
Team members meet with their professor at least twice a week, but will be expected to meet additional times, including weekends, on an as-needed basis. Meetings will involve a combination of instruction, discussion, and practice.  
  
Expenses:  
USEK Faculty of Law pays reasonable travel expenses for participants to attend the Oral Rounds in The Hague – The Netherlands.

## Courses
[ Specialization](javascript:;)
[DRG510Advanced Corporate Law](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course examines the following three topics: 1) the main operations that may affect the company as a group; 2) the legal acts that the partners can conclude to perfect the rules of corporate operations; 3) the rules of powers and responsibilities applicable to each corporate player, legal person and corporate organs. 
[DRG520Advanced Business Law](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course undertakes a comparative study of the French and Lebanese law concerning the acts and assets of a commercial enterprise, including commercial transactions, business and business transactions, and commercial lease. 
[DRG525Financial Instruments](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course studies the various legal instruments used in financing operations, such as banking practice contracts, assorting guarantees, and the financial instruments of corporate law. 
[DRG535Bankruptcy and Reorganization](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course examines the main rules and the philosophy of preventing and addressing business difficulties in French and European law, as compared to the Lebanese law, which takes after an older tradition. 
[DRG545Law and Business of Corporate Transaction](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course provides a comparative approach to contract law, including intermediary contracts, commercial agencies, mandates, commissions, and brokerage under French and Lebanese law. 
[DRG555Criminal Business Law](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course provides an overview of the criminal offenses applicable to the business and corporate world: 1) common law offenses also applicable to enterprises, especially fraud, breach of trust, and money laundering; 2) specific business offenses, including the misappropriation of corporate assets, and bankruptcy. 
[DRG625International Contract Law](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course examines several transversal topics, such as the conflicts of laws and jurisdictions, arbitration, and the United Nations Vienna Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. 
[DRG665Contractual Technique](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course adopts a practical approach to contract law, by examining the general structure of a contract and its principal provisions, and includes the analysis and drafting of clauses. 
[DRG670Competition Law](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course examines the rules of competition in international, European and national laws. 
[DRG675Distribution Contracts](javascript:;)
2 credits
This course examines all main contracts related to structuring a distribution network, including exclusivity agreements, selective distribution, exclusive concession, and franchise. 
[ Capstone](javascript:;)
[DRG590AResearch Dissertation](javascript:;)
6 credits
The student prepares a research paper under the direction of a Master’s teacher and defends it before a jury composed of three teachers, at least two of whom are part of the Master’s teaching team. The third member may be a USEK teacher and doctor of law. 
[DRG599Internship Report & Project](javascript:;)
6 credits
#### Mission
The Master II in Business Law of the USEK Faculty of Law, in partnership with the Faculty of Law of the Université de Poitiers, aims to offer its students an in-depth training, through a comparative approach, in French, European and Lebanese Business Law.   

#### Program Outcomes
a. Students will familiarize themselves with and deepen their knowledge of French, European and Lebanese business law in general, including corporate law, financial law, contract and distribution law, business law, and bankruptcy law.  
b. The legal techniques of commercial contract drafting are covered through a practical approach.   
c. Students will learn a research methodology specifically designed for business and corporate

##  Cite Your Sources 
Learning how to reference correctly is a very important skill and an essential requirement when referring to the sources used in an academic paper or thesis.  
  
USEK has approved the adoption of three standard styles depending on the Faculty. The style for each Faculty is listed below with links for further information:  
  
Faculty | Style | Resources  
---|---|---  
Law | The Bluebook: A uniform system of citation | [The Bluebook: A uniform system of citation](http://sierra.usek.edu.lb/record=b1211142)  
All other Faculties | APA (American Psychological Association) Citation Style |  [APA Style Guide to Electronic References](https://sierra.usek.edu.lb/record=b1197719)  
  
There is numerous [citation software](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/citation-software) to help you write the proper citations and bibliographies.

##  Administrators & Staff 
### Access
  * To borrow material, you will need your USEK ID Card;
  * Your USEK ID Card is also used to pay for [printing and photocopying](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps) in the Library. 

  

### [Borrow & Renew](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-and-renew)
Category | Item Type  
| N° of Items Allowed to Check-Out | Loan Period   
---|---|---|---  
**Administrators**

| 42 days

Renewing of items is allowed once for an additional 14 days.   
  

### [Interlibrary Loan Service](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/interlibrary-loan-service)
  * [Obtain materials](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-from-other-libraries1) (books, articles and chapters) from other libraries that are not available at the USEK Library.
  * Administrators can request up to 20 items.
  * Staff can request up to 10 item.
  * The loan period for books is 14 days, or according to the exceptions policy of the lending library.
  * Renewing of items is not guaranteed; renewals should be made one week prior to the due date indicated on the item.

  

### Find Resources
  * [Catalog](https://sierra.usek.edu.lb/*frf) for searching the USEK Library print collections including books, journals, newspapers, theses and dissertations, music recordings, etc. 
  * [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) for searching a large and varied collection (article databases, e-book collections…) of electronic resources.
  * [Find a title](http://yf7lm7ay6z.search.serialssolutions.com/ejp/?libHash=YF7LM7AY6Z#/?language=en-US&titleType=ALL) with this search tool to find a book or journal.
  * [One Search](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/search-everything) for searching the USEK Library Catalog and many of our databases simultaneously to quickly provide credible library results through a single search box.
  * [Off-campus access to electronic resources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/off-campus-access) to access online resources from anywhere off campus using your USEK username and password.

  

### [Reserve a Study Room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room)
  * [Reserve a group study room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room2) in the Kaslik campus Library.
  * You can reserve up to 2 hours of study room use per day and up to 6 total hours per week.
  * You can reserve the multipurpose room for meetings and administrative sessions.
  * Reservations can be made up to two weeks in advance.
  * Reserved rooms must be claimed within the first 15 minutes of the reservation.
  * Rooms are available Monday-Friday only during Library opening hours but not on weekends, holidays, or during periods when the Library is closed.

  

### Get Help
  * [Ask Us](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us) for assistance with your research by contacting a librarian in person, by phone, by e-mail or chat.
  * [Research appointments](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/appointment) with a librarian for in-depth help with your research paper or assignment.
  * [Research Workshops](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/register-for-a-workshop1) for workshops on how to learn about using library resources, [electronic resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php), the scholarly research process, citation styles, plagiarism, and other topics.
  * [Research guides ](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/)provide you with targeted information on a specific topic or tool to help you in your research.
  * [Cite your sources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/cite-your-sources) for how to cite your references properly.

  

### [Copy/Print/Scan](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps)
  * To activate or recharge your account, ask for the Retail Cash Officer at the Registrar Office.

  

### [Suggest a Purchase](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/suggest-a-purchase)
  * Provide suggestions for the purchase of resources that would improve our collection.

  

### Activities
  * [Exhibitions](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/exhibit-your-artwork) to exhibit your artwork (paintings, photos, etc.) in the Library.
  * [Film, Photography and Recording](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/filming/photography-and-recording-in-the-library) for organizing your session with the Library to make use of the premises to film, photograph or record.

##  Donors Gallery 
One way for USEK Library to enlarge its collection is by acquiring, preserving, and making books available from the private libraries of prominent Lebanese individuals. These books are of enduring value because of their intellectual and academic content. These Collections fit into the mission of the USEK Library to ensure the preservation and long-lasting availability of resources of national and ethnic heritage, as well as to support the research needs of the undergraduates, graduate students, faculty, researchers, and the academic community at large.   
  

### Collections
Major collections include the private libraries of:  
  

  * [Maurice El Gemayel](javascript:;)
Lebanese politician, lawyer and economist  
Date of birth: 1907  
Place of birth: Mansourah, Egypt  
Date of death: 31 October, 1970, Beirut  
Family: Married Josette Awad and had six daughters  
Education: Antoura College; Paris Law University.  
Career: He was elected head of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) for two consecutive terms. He created the Ministry of Planning in Lebanon. He was a court attorney, and was elected deputy of Metn in 1960, Minister of State for the Financial Affairs from August 1st, 1960 to May 20, 1961 and re-elected deputy of Metn in April 1964. Gemayel was also member of the Political Office of Phalanges Party (Kataëb).  
Publications:   
Numerous books about economy and Lebanese resources  
Gemayel, M. (1951). _La planification intégrale des eaux Libanaises_. Beyrouth: S.N. 
  * [Joseph Oughourlian](javascript:;)
Date of birth: 1948  
Place of birth: Paris  
Family: Spouse, Jenny, and three children  
Education: Graduated from the HEC Business School and from IEP (Sciences Po.), both in Paris, and earned his MSc in Economics from Sorbonne in Paris.  
Career: Founded Amber Capital in New York in November 2005 and leads the investment offices in London and Milan. He began his career at Société Générale in Paris in 1994 and soon moved to New York. In 1997, he started managing proprietary money of Societé Générale, which led to the first Amber Fund being stablished in October 2001 with seed capital from the Bank. In addition to the board of PRISA, he currently sits on the board of AGBU (the world's largest Armenian charitable organization, based in New York). He is based in London. Elected to the AGBU Central Board of Directors in 2010  
Publications:  
Oughourlian, J. (1982). _Histoire de la monnaie Libanaise: Une monnaie, un État_. Toulouse: Erès. 
  * [Boutros Dib](javascript:;)
Date of birth: August 23, 1922  
Place of birth: Banias, Syria  
Family: Married to Lily Charaoui and has four children.  
Career: Was Director-General of the Presidency of the Lebanese Republic, Rector of the Lebanese University, Ambassador of Lebanon to the Holy See, UNECSO and France.  
Honours and awards: received numerous decorations from several Countries, including Grand Cross, Grand Officer, and Commander.  
Publications:   
He led a team of nine historians in the elaboration of Lebanon's history: from its origins to the 20th century: Dib, B. (dir.) (2006). _Histoire du Liban: Des origines au XXe siècle_. Paris : Philippe Rey. 
  * [Assaad Germanos](javascript:;)
Date of birth: 1931  
Place of birth: Lebanon  
Family: Married and has three children  
Education: Studied at St. Joseph University of Beirut in the Law Faculty and got his L.L.B. diploma  
Career: He was the judge, the Court President, and the advisor of the First Chamber of the Court of North Lebanon in 1964. Germanos was the President of Labor Court in North Lebanon in 1965, the sole judge of summary jurisdiction, an examining judge of Beirut in 1967 and an examining judge in banking affairs in 1968, Military General Attorney of Lebanon in 1971, and finally, he was a Counselor at the Court of Appeals from 1983 till 2005. 
  * [Kamal Salibi](javascript:;)
Lebanese historian  
Date of birth: May 2, 1929  
Place of birth: Bhamdoun  
Date of death: Sept. 1, 2011, Beirut  
Education: Studied at the American University of Beirut, London University, and obtained his Doctorate in History from London University in 1953  
Career: Professor Emeritus at the American University of Beirut; historian of modern Lebanon, the Arab world, and the Bible.  
Publications:   
Author of several articles and studies published in specialized journals and books  
Grassmuck, George & Salibi, K. S. (1964). Reformed administration in Lebanon. Ann Arbor: University of Michigan. Center for Near Eastern and North African Studies.  
Salibi, K. S. (1977). The modern history of Lebanon. New York: Caravan Books.  
Salibi, K. S. (1976). Crossroads to Civil War: Lebanon 1958-1976. Delmar, N.Y.: Caravan Books.  
Salibi, K. S. (1977). Syria under Islam: Empire on trial 634-1097. Delmar, N.Y.: Caravan Books  
Salibi, K. S. (1980). A history of Arabia. Delmar, N.Y.: Caravan Books.
  * [Robert Abdo Ghanem](javascript:;)
Date of birth: 1939  
Place of birth: Baskinta  
Career: Poet, philosopher, theologian and journalist. Founded the magazine Maraya (Mirrors). His father is the writer Abdullah Ghanem 
  * [Anna Tabet](javascript:;)

##  Cite Your Sources 
Learning how to reference correctly is a very important skill and an essential requirement when referring to the sources used in an academic paper or thesis.  
  
USEK has approved the adoption of three standard styles depending on the Faculty. The style for each Faculty is listed below with links for further information:  
  
Faculty | Style | Resources  
---|---|---  
Law | The Bluebook: A uniform system of citation | [The Bluebook: A uniform system of citation](http://sierra.usek.edu.lb/record=b1211142)  
All other Faculties | APA (American Psychological Association) Citation Style |  [APA Style Guide to Electronic References](https://sierra.usek.edu.lb/record=b1197719)  
  
There is numerous [citation software](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/citation-software) to help you write the proper citations and bibliographies.

##  Borrow and Renew 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/use-your-library)
  

[Am I entitled to have a USEK Library account?](javascript:;)
All USEK students, faculty, staff, and courtesy borrowers (alumni and visitors) who have current USEK identification cards are entitled to borrow items from the Library. Please make sure you have your USEK card with you. You will need it for checking out and renewing items.  
  
Please note that your card cannot be used by anyone else.
[What if I lose my card?](javascript:;)
If you have lost your USEK card, please report it to the Registrar Office to obtain a replacement. The Library is not responsible for any outcome arising from the unauthorized use of a card.  
  
USEK Library respects Library users’ right to privacy and confidentiality while using library materials; names of borrowers and their accounts will not be disclosed.
[What are my responsibilities as a USEK Library user?](javascript:;)
  * You are responsible for all materials checked out to your name until they are returned and checked in by Circulation staff;
  * You are responsible for the timely return of library materials;
  * Renew your items before their due date;
  * Do not depend on others to return items for you;
  * Do not lend your USEK ID card or borrowed items;
  * Make sure to keep your residential and contact details updated;
  * Check your Library account to access your library information online;
  * Return recalled materials promptly;
  * Protect all library materials from damage or theft;
  * Keep materials in good condition: make sure not to write on the books, not to fold pages, and not to use sticky notes, rubber bands, paperclips, or anything else which could cause any damage. 

  
Please see Fines and Penalties below for list of charges.
[Where can I locate the items I need?](javascript:;)
You can find the majority of USEK’s printed collection in the Library Catalog, which is accessible to you on/off campus. Each item has a Library shelf mark and is arranged in its corresponding area, mostly located in Reading Room 1 or Reading Room 2. If the material you require is located in Reading Room 1 or Reading Room 2, you can personally retrieve the material from the shelf. If the item is not located in Reading Room 1 or 2, you can request it online through the Library Catalog and a librarian will retrieve the item for you, and you can collect it from the Circulation Desk.  
  
If you need assistance with locating any items, do not hesitate to ask our staff at the Circulation Desk for help.

[What materials cannot be borrowed from the Library?](javascript:;)
Not all items available at the Library can be borrowed, including: 
  * Reference books: encyclopedias, dictionaries, almanacs, handbooks, biographical and literary sources, as well as bibliographies;
  * Latest issues of periodicals and magazines;
  * Newspapers;
  * USEK theses and dissertations;
  * Non-circulating material including books dated prior to 1970, rare books and private collections;
  * Microfilms and microfiches;
  * Music scores;
  * Maps, visual materials, graphic materials and digitized files.


[How do I renew items I wish to keep for a longer period?](javascript:;)

  * If the item is on hold by another user;
  * If the item is placed on course reserve;
  * If the borrower’s ID is blocked;
  * If the loan has already been renewed twice;
  * If the item has been recalled by the Library.

[What is a Course Reserve?](javascript:;)
USEK Library receives requests from faculty members to reserve material for registered students in a specific course. Reserve lists normally include mandatory and recommended readings for USEK courses, and include books, textbooks, journal articles, bound periodicals, CDs, DVDs, and course packs.  
  
If you are a student registered in the course, you are eligible for borrowing these items, and can borrow a maximum of two items at a time.   
  
Students can borrow these items for a period of three hours (between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.), or keep them overnight till 9:00 a.m. the next morning if borrowed after 4:00 p.m.  
For more details on Course Reserves for Faculty members, please go to the [Place Materials on Reserve page](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/place-materials-on-reserve).  
  
If you are a course instructor, you can place a reserve request by filling out the online [Course Reserve form](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/course-reserves-request).
[How can I request books from other library branches?](javascript:;)
The Intercampus Loan Service provides USEK students, faculty and staff members with the transfer and delivery of materials between library branches (Kaslik Main Campus Library, Chekka Campus Library and Zahle Campus Library).  
We will do our best to deliver the requested items within three (3) business days, except if the item is already on loan at the time of the request.   
A notification email will be sent to the user’s USEK e-mail account when the item is available for pickup.  
Note that transferred items will remain on hold at the Circulation Desk of the USEK Library branch of your choice for two (2) business days only.
[Recalls of Checked-Out Items](javascript:;)
Recalls are official requests for an item to be returned to the Library as soon as possible. Eligible users such as Faculty members may request that items checked out be recalled and made available for their use.   
  
Kindly return recalled items at the library branch you borrowed them from, not later than the due date stated on the recall notice, so as to make them available to the requestor.
[Items Already on Loan](javascript:;)
If the item you need has been checked out to someone else, you may place a hold through your Library account. The due date for the item does not change, but it does prevent the item from being renewed.   
  
We will notify you by e-mail once the requested item has been returned, and it will be placed on hold for two (2) business days at the Circulation Desk.  
  
Note that a hold will not be placed if: 
  * Two or more copies of the item are available;
  * The item is located on reserve, or the item circulates for a short loan period (e.g. video, audio materials);
  * The item is lost, missing, on order, in process or non-circulating;
  * Your borrowing privileges are blocked or expired;
  * You have reached your hold limit.


[Email Notices](javascript:;)
Current USEK faculty, students and staff receive library notices via their USEK email account. Other users and Library card holders (alumni and visitors) are advised to add an e-mail address to their library records to enable e-mails to be received.   
  
These notices are important as they relate to the following library services and hold pick-up information:   
  
Courtesy | When a borrowed item is soon due for renewal or return  
---|---  
Overdue | When an item becomes overdue  
Hold request | When a reserved item is awaiting collection from the Circulation Desk. Items are placed on hold for two (2) business days  
Recall | When a borrowed item is reserved by another user  
Summary bill for lost material | Once a borrowed item is 30 days overdue.   
This incurs a lost/replacement fee  
Sighting/re-issue | Borrowing privileges are blocked until overdue items are returned  
[Fines and Penalties](javascript:;)
Fines apply when items are not returned or returned late. Overdue notices are issued as a courtesy to all Library users three days before the due date. The table below lists the various types of fines that may apply:   
  
**Fee Structure**  
1st Overdue Charge (first five days) | 0.5 USD per item / day   
---|---  
2nd Overdue Charge (day 6 onwards) | 1 USD per item / day  
Overdue Course Reserves Charge (first hour) | 1 USD per item  
Overdue Course Reserves Charge (hour 2 onwards) | 1.5 USD per item / hour  
Recall Overdue Charge (first day) | 0.5 USD per item  
Recall Overdue Charge (day 2 onwards) | 1 USD per item / day  
Replacement Cost for lost or damaged material* | The cost of the item plus a 20 USD processing fee per item.  
For old items or items that cannot be replaced, users will be fined twice the cost of the item   
  
  
*Note that if a lost item is found and returned within 90 days, the cost of the item will be refunded.   
  
**Payment**  
  
An email notifying the Library user of incurred fines will be sent and can be printed.  
Cash payments of fines will be accepted at the Circulation Desk of all USEK Library branches.   
  
**Penalties for failing to pay a library fine  
  
**
  * Borrowing privileges will be suspended if the material is not returned within 30 days of the second overdue notice.
  * In case users fail to pay their library fines, holds will be placed on their academic records.

##  Fact Book 
### COMMITMENT TO EXCELLENCE
At USEK Library, we are dedicated to fostering an inclusive culture that connects us with our patrons of today and tomorrow. Our roadmap focuses on optimizing our resources and enhancing our discoverability.  
  

### OVERVIEW
USEK Library is steadfast in its mission to support academic endeavors by preserving and conserving Lebanese cultural heritage across various formats, including newspapers, manuscripts, rare books, archives, photographs, and maps. Our fully automated library ensures that many resources and reference services are accessible from off-campus, offering a virtual environment that supports research.  
We provide tailored reference and instructional services both online (via webinars, emails, chat) and in person, promoting a culture of information literacy at all levels. Researchers from Lebanon and beyond frequently visit our library for its rich historical collections, especially those on Lebanon and the Middle East. The library operates 40 hours a week, continually enriching its print and electronic collections to support university curricula.

##  Copy / Print / Scan (CPS) 
The USEK Library is equipped with self-service CPS multifunction machines in Reading Rooms 1 and 2.   
  
With the CPS system, you can: 
  * Scan documents directly to your email free of charge (for USEK users, alumni, and visitors).
  * Print jobs from any library computer and hold them in the queue for up to four hours; release your job by swiping your credited USEK ID card at the printer.
  * Photocopy materials after swiping your credited USEK ID card at the CPS station.

  
All users with an active USEK account may access CPS services from any public library workstation. You must also have a CPS account with sufficient funds.   
  
To activate your account, purchase units, or recharge your balance, please visit the Student Accounting Desk in the Registrar’s Office.  
  
[CPS Printer Installation Guide](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20250522CPSPrinterInstallationGuide-112454.pdf)  
  

### CPS pricing
Size | Copy/Print Price (USD/page) | Scan Price (USD/page)  
---|---|---  
A4 (B&W)  
| $0.10  
| No Charge  
A4 (Color)  
| $0.20 | No Charge  
A3 (B&W) | $0.20 | No Charge  
A3 (Color) | $0.50 | No Charge  
  
  
You may copy limited portions of a copyrighted work for private study or research. Please see the Copyright Reminder section for details on acceptable copy limits.  
  

### Copyright reminder
Source | Copy Limit  
---|---  
from a book  
| one chapter or 5%, whichever is the greater  
  
from an article (or conference proceedings or other non-literary collective work)  
| one article or 5%, whichever is the greater  
  
from a law report | one case or 5%, whichever is the greater  
from a collective literary work (e.g. short stories, poems, etc.) | one short story or poem only, up to 10 pages in length  
  
  
All library users should responsibly exercise their rights under Lebanese Copyright Law and fair use guidelines when using copyrighted materials.  
  

### Need assistance?
Our Circulation Team is here to help with any Copy-Print-Scan (CPS) questions or issues: 
  * Visit us at the Circulation Desk (Reading Rooms 1 & 2)
  * Email us at circulation@usek.edu.lb
  * Call us at +961 9 600 071
Feel free to stop by or get in touch whenever you need help releasing a print job, troubleshooting a scan, or with any other CPS-related request.

##  Exhibit your artwork 
### Are you interested in displaying your artwork or collection at the USEK Library?
We offer the opportunity for selected artists and groups to showcase their artwork in our exhibition spaces in an effort to enhance the cultural and intellectual life of the community.  |  [ Submit Exhibition Application ](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/exhibition-application)  
---|---  
Our goal is to provide an enriching library experience by presenting users with a wide range of art, collections or displays; supporting community culture and artistic activities; enhancing community appreciation of art; as well as helping artists increase their public exposure.   
  
Artists, professional or amateur, are invited to exhibit their artistic, cultural and educational works including paintings, photographs, sculpture, crafts or other forms of artwork.  
  
Please read our [Art Exhibits Policy](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/policy-for-art-exhibits) for details on our terms and procedures.

##  Faculty 
### Access
  * To borrow material you will need a valid USEK ID card.
  * Your USEK ID card is also used to pay for [printing and photocopying in the library](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps).

  

### [Borrow & Renew](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-and-renew)
Category | Item Type  
| N° of Items Allowed to Check-Out | Loan Period   
---|---|---|---  
**Full-time Faculty**

Renewing of items is allowed once for an additional 14 days.   
  

### [Interlibrary Loan Service](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/interlibrary-loan-service)
  * [Obtain materials](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-from-other-libraries1) (books, articles and chapters) that are not available at the USEK Library from other libraries.
  * Full-time faculty can request up to 20 items.
  * Part-time faculty can request up to 10 items.
  * The loan period for books is 14 days, or according to the exceptions policy of the lending library.
  * Renewing of items is not guaranteed; renewals should be made one week prior to the due date indicated on the item.

  

### Find Resources
  * [Catalog](https://sierra.usek.edu.lb/*frf) for searching the USEK Library print collections including books, journals, newspapers, theses and dissertations, music recordings, etc.
  * [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) for searching a large and varied collection (article databases, e-book collections…) of electronic resources.
  * [Find a title](http://yf7lm7ay6z.search.serialssolutions.com/ejp/?libHash=YF7LM7AY6Z#/?language=en-US&titleType=ALL) with this search tool to find a book or journal.
  * [One Search](http://usek.summon.serialssolutions.com/) for searching the USEK Library Catalog and databases simultaneously to quickly provide credible library results through a single search box.
  * [Off-campus access to electronic resources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/off-campus-access)to access online resources from anywhere off campus using your USEK username and password.

  

### Teaching Support
  * [Course Reserve](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/course-reserves-request) : Place print course materials that are of high demand in the reserve section.
  * [Research guides](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/) : Provide you with targeted information on a specific topic or tool to help you in your research.
  * [Library Instruction](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/request-a-library-instruction/orientation-session): Reserve a session to instruct undergraduates and graduates on how to conduct effective library research.

  

### [Reserve a Study Room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room)
  * [Reserve a group study room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room2) in the Kaslik campus Library.
  * You can reserve up to 2 hours of study room use per day and up to 6 total hours per week. 
  * You can reserve the multipurpose room for meetings and administrative sessions.
  * Reservations can be made up to two weeks in advance.
  * Reserved rooms must be claimed within the first 15 minutes of the reservation.
  * Rooms are available Monday-Friday during Library opening hours but not available on weekends, holidays, or during periods when the Library is closed.

  

### Research Support
  * [Ask Us](http://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us) for assistance with your research by contacting a librarian in person, by phone, by e-mail or chat.
  * [Research appointments](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/appointment) with a librarian for in-depth help with your research paper or assignment.
  * [Research Workshops](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/register-for-a-workshop) for workshops on how to learn about using the library resources. [Electronic resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) the scholarly research process, citation styles, plagiarism, and other topics.
  * [Research guides](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/) provide you with targeted information on a specific topic or tool to help you in your research.
  * [Cite your sources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/cite-your-sources) for how to cite your references properly.

  

### [Suggest a Purchase](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/use-your-library/suggest-a-purchase)
  * Provide suggestions for the purchase of resources that would improve our collection.

  

### [Copy/Print/Scan](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps)
  * To activate or recharge your account, ask for the Retail Cash Officer at the Registrar Office.

  

### Activities
  * [Exhibitions](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/exhibit-your-artwork) for exhibiting your artwork (paintings, photos, etc.) in the Library.
  * [Film, Photography and Recording](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/filming/photography-and-recording-in-the-library) for organizing your session with the Library to make use of the premises to film, photograph or record.

# Feedback
Welcome, Hisham | [Logout](javascript:WebForm_DoPostBackWithOptions\(new%20WebForm_PostBackOptions\("ctl00$lbtnLogout",%20"",%20true,%20"",%20"",%20false,%20true\)\))
We do our best at USEK Library to assess our performance and provide an optimized experience to our users. We treat your feedback seriously and will use it to improve our services in the future. Whether you wish to leave a general comment, share an experience, make a suggestion or raise an issue, you can tell us what you think by submitting the Feedback Form. Equally, if you receive good service, we would be glad to hear about it.   

[ Submit your feedback](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/feedback-form)
  

### How we respond to your feedback
Once your feedback form has been submitted, the Library will respond within three (3) working days.   
  
By submitting feedback on our services you are permitting the Library to share your feedback and the response on our website. Your name will not be mentioned, but your subject area, for instance, will be shared if relevant.  
  

### Complaints
We encourage and value all feedback. If you are unhappy with the response to your feedback, please contact the [person most relevant to your complaint](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/contact-us).

##  Citation Software 
As any researcher knows, engaging in academic research means it is important to think critically, conduct thorough online research, and identify appropriate sources to ensure that your work reflects your thoughts in a clear and coherent way.  
  
Citation software can help you organize your journal article, book, or other document citations by collecting them together in one place to create properly formatted bibliographies in almost any style. It can enable you to: 
  * import citations from your favorite databases, library catalog, e-journals and websites;
  * build and organize bibliographies;
  * format citations for papers;
  * take notes on articles and save them in your collection of citations.

  
The USEK Library has RefWorks at your disposal.   
  

### USEK Subscriptions
[RefWorks](http://refworks.proquest.com/)  
RefWorks is a powerful online research management, writing and collaboration tool designed to help researchers of all levels easily gather, organize, store and share all types of information, and to instantly generate citations and bibliographies.  
  
USEK users need to create an account to be able to use RefWorks on and off-campus.  
  
Additionally, there are many more products and tools that are available for free.  
  

### Free software
[Mendeley](https://www.mendeley.com/)  
Mendeley is a free reference manager and academic social network that can help you organize your research, collaborate with others online, and discover the latest research.  
  
[Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/)  
Zotero is a free, easy-to-use tool to help you collect, organize, cite, and share your research sources. Zotero automatically senses content, allowing you to add it to your personal library with a single click.  
  
[Citavi Free](http:/www.citavi.com/)  
Citavi Free is a starter edition and is ideal for testing small solo and team projects up to 100 references. Citavi supports the entire research process - from searching for sources to finishing your paper.  
  
[CiteULike](http://www.citeulike.org/)  
CiteULike is a free service for managing and discovering scholarly references.  
  
For further instructions on how to manage your references, [Ask a Librarian](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us).

##  Alumni 
### Access
As USEK alumni, you can access a variety of USEK Library services and resources. The Library's resources are available to the University’s alumni for their personal and professional development, strictly for non-commercial use. To use the Library, you must present your alumni card issued by the [Alumni Office](https://www.usek.edu.lb/alumni).  
  

### Account and Cards
  * A valid USEK alumni card is required to access the alumni services and resources we offer.
  * To borrow books, a one-time deposit non-refundable fee of 100 USD is required. The deposit will be paid at the Student Accounting Desk in the Registrar Office. 
  * When borrowing books, you must show the deposit receipt at the Library circulation desk.
  * Every library user has a right to privacy and confidentiality while using library materials. Names of borrowers and their accounts are never disclosed.

  

### Library Services
[Borrow](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-and-renew)

| NUMBER OF BOOKS | LOAN PERIOD

To borrow material you will need to show your USEK Alumni Card along with the deposit receipt.  
  

### Find Resources
  * [Catalog](http://sierra.usek.edu.lb/) for searching the USEK Library print collections including books, journals, newspapers, theses and dissertations, music recordings etc.
  * [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) for searching specific e-collections (article databases, e-book collections, etc.) (See walk-in access service).
  * [One search](http://usek.summon.serialssolutions.com/) for searching the complete USEK Library catalog and databases simultaneously through a single search box (see: walk-in access service).

  
  

### WALK-IN ACCESS SERVICE
USEK Library offers its alumni a walk-in access service, which allows our alumni to access certain databases, e-journals and e-books for use on-site. To use the walk-in access service please ask for assistance at the circulation desk in either reading room.   
  
_Please note that even in the library, some e-resources are not available to external users due to licensing restrictions._  
  

### WIRELESS ACCESS
USEK Library provides its alumni a short-term Wi-Fi connection. Ask for your login details at the circulation desk.   
  
**Eduroam:  
All visitors from participating institutions can use USEK’s Eduroam secure wireless network by selecting the Eduroam wireless network (SSID) anywhere on USEK Campus. Users should use their institution’s username (email format: username@domain) and password to login to Eduroam.**   
  

### [Get Help](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/get-help)
  * [Ask Us](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us) for assistance with your research by contacting a librarian in person.
  * [Research guides](hhttp://libguides.usek.edu.lb/) provide you with targeted information on a specific topic or tool to help you in your research.
  * [Cite your sources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/cite-your-sources) for learning how to cite your references properly.

  

### [Copy/Print/Scan](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps)
  * Alumni may set up a CPS account on their USEK alumni ID card.
  * For activation, purchase units and recharge, please refer to the Student Accounting Desk in the Registrar Office.

  
  

### Activities
  * [Exhibitions](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/exhibit-your-artwork) for exhibiting your artwork (paintings, photos, etc.) in the Library.
  * [Film, Photography and Recording](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/filming/photography-and-recording-in-the-library) for organizing your session with the Library if you would like to make use of the premises for a film, photography or recording session.

  

### Change of Address
It is the responsibility of individuals to keep the Library informed of any address changes. Library fines will not be waived if alumni fail to notify us of a change of address. You can update your address with library staff at the circulation desk of the USEK Library.  
  
IMPORTANT  
Rules and regulations of USEK Library are to be respected. Failure to do so may result in the suspension of user borrowing privileges. Membership is discretionary and the administration reserves the right to refuse applications for membership without redress. The Library is responsible for safeguarding the confidentiality of a borrower's transactions and for providing an environment conducive for research.

##  How to Create Permanent Links to Online Resources 
The Library provides USEK users with access to an array of [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php). Access is open from any computer located on-campus, and if USEK members wish to log in off-campus they can use their USEK username and password.   
  
To make an article, e-book, journal or chapter available on the e-learning platform or even share it with another USEK user, follow the procedure below to create a permanent link. Please note, simply copying the URL from the browser will not work.   
  

### How to Locate and Save a Permanent Link for an Article 
  * Access the USEK [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) page, and select the desired database;
  * The publisher usually provides a permanent link somewhere on the article information page, indicated by words such as ‘persistent URL’, ‘stable URL’, ‘infomark’, ‘permalink’, ‘document URL’, ‘durable link’, ‘linking options for this record’ or ‘DOI’. 

  
Here’s an example of a permanent URL taken from the _Academic Search Complete database_ :  
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/links.png)  
  
If you stop at this stage, the URL will only be accessible from on-campus.   
  

### How to Create a Proxied Link for Off-Campus Access
  * To make it accessible off-campus, add our ‘web proxy prefix’ to the beginning of the URL.   
Our web proxy prefix is: <http://ezproxy.usek.edu.lb/login?url=>

  
Example: 
  * The permanent link for the previous article above is: [http://search.ebscohost.com/login.aspx?direct=true&db=a9h&AN=93325130&site=ehost-live](http://search.ebscohost.com/login.aspx?direct=true&db=a9h&AN=93325130&site=ehost-live)
  * Add this to our web proxy prefix: <http://ezproxy.usek.edu.lb/login?url=>
  * The off-campus link should look like this:  
[http://ezproxy.usek.edu.lb/login?url=http://search.ebscohost.com/login.aspx?direct=true&db=a9h&AN=93325130&site=ehost-live](http://ezproxy.usek.edu.lb/login?url=http://search.ebscohost.com/login.aspx?direct=true&db=a9h&AN=93325130&site=ehost-live)

  
Congratulations! You have created a permanent link, which you can access on or off campus, post on e-learning or send in an e-mail.  
  
For more information, please contact the Electronic Collections Department.

##  Interlibrary Loan Service 
Our Interlibrary Loan and Document Delivery Service (ILL/DDS) can assist you in gaining access to materials not available in the University’s Library collections. These include books, e-book chapters, journal and e-journal articles, as well as conference papers and bound periodicals amongst others.   
  
The ILL/DDS service is accessible to all current USEK faculty, staff and enrolled students.   
We regret that this service is not available for personal non-university research and recreational reading purposes.  
  
If you wish to place a request, please make sure you read our [ILL/DDS policy](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/user-policies-and-guidelines/illdds) first, then complete the ILL/DDS request form.   
  
To place a request, log in below with your USEK credentials and fill out the ILL/DDS request form.  
  
Before placing your request, please check the item you want is not already in our collection.

##  Filming/Photography and Recording in the Library 
USEK Library has been a featured setting in various video productions and is a much sought-after locale for photography shoots.  
  
If you would like to use the USEK Library for any commercial and academic filming and/or photography/ or audio recording for educational and/or public interest purposes, please submit a request online.   
  
Please note, all requests must be approved by the University Library according to the [filming and photography and Recording policy](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/filming-and-photography-and-recording-policy).
