##  Hidden Treasures 
The _Book of Psalms_ was printed in the monastery of Saint Anthony of Qozhaya in 1610. Since it is the first book ever printed in the Eastern part of the Ottoman Empire, it is considered as one of the most distinguished works in the history of typography.
In 1485, the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II issued a decree banning all forms of printing in the Empire, and this prohibition was reinforced by Sultan Selim I in 1515. The supposed purpose was to safeguard the contents of Islamic religious books from being modified in the process of printing. However, some researchers believe that the real motivation was to control the work of calligraphers and painters, and to ensure that Istanbul benefited financially. This ban remained in force until the establishment of the first Ottoman printing press in Istanbul in 1727 which printed only in Arabic and Turkish.
The Christian minorities living in the eastern part of the Ottoman Empire were unaware of the printing process during the majority of the 16th century. The first published work seen by the Maronites was a book on Christian catechism in Garshuni, printed in Rome in 1580. In this same year, it was brought to Mount Lebanon by the papal legate Giovanni Battista Eliano, who distributed it to the members of the Synod of Qanoubine. Eliano also distributed another book he translated himself from Latin into Arabic (printed in Garshuni, 1580). It was entitled _Creed of the Catholic Faith_ , approved by the Council of Trent, and known as the _Creed of Pope Pius IV_.
However, this development of typography was not paralleled in the Middle East. Although Stefano Evodio Assemani recorded in the catalogue of the Bilblioteca Medicea Laurenziana (Florence - Italy), that the _Book of Psalms_ was printed in the Qozhaya monastery in 1585, this statement remains questionable, since there is no physical evidence of the existence of this edition in any library. Furthermore, the papal legate Girolamo Dandini noted, during his apostolical visit to the Maronites in 1596, that there were no printing presses in the region. Therefore, it can be concluded that the first book in the eastern part of the Ottoman Empire was this Syriac-Garshuni _Book of Psalms,_ printed at Qozhaya monastery in 1610.
Researchers tend to believe, without any reliable sources, that Sarkis, ater named Archbishop of Damascus, purchased printing tools from a city in Italy and carried them back to Mount Lebanon after the election of Patriarch Makhlouf (circa 1609). It is important to mention that since printing presses at that time were made of wood, and required great dexterity and expertise, the printing of the _Book of Psalms_ was not completed before November 10th, 1610, as is written in the colophon at the end of the book. However, the fact that this book was the only one printed at that time raises many questions such as: why other books were not printed, what happened to the printing press or even if the printing press was dismantled. The relevant historical sources do not delve into this topic at all, and most of them actually ignore the existence of this printing press. For these reasons, we wonder whether the _Book of Psalms_ was only printed in a limited number of copies before the printing press was dismantled.
The _Book of Psalms_ is made up of 268 pages and uses Syriac letters for pagination (except for the first eight pages which were not paginated). The psalm verses are not numbered but divided into groups of five, with a number placed in the margin to mark each of these groups.
We still do not know exactly how many copies were printed and distributed. All we can confirm is that a German traveler bought one copy in Tripoli in 1611. Currently we have tracked six copies in various public and private libraries: National Library of France, the Saint Geneviève Library in Paris, the Staatsbibliothek in Nürnberg (Germany), the Herzog August Bibliothek, in Wolfenbüttel (Germany), the Saint Joseph University Library in Beirut and lastly the Holy Spirit University Library of Kaslik (Lebanon).
**Excerpt from**
Moukarzel, J (Ed.). 2016. _The Book of the Psalms of David, King and Prophet:__A facsimile of the Editio Princeps published in 1610 (Qozhaya - Lebanon)._ Kaslik: Holy Spirit University of Kaslik Press.

##  Graduates 
### Access
  * To borrow material you will need a valid USEK ID card.
  * Your USEK ID card is also used to pay for [printing and photocopying in the library](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps). 

  

### [Borrow & Renew](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-and-renew)
Category | Item Type  
| N° of Items Allowed to Check-Out | Loan Period   
---|---|---|---  
**Graduate**  
  
  
  
| Books | 10  
| 28 days  
  
Audiovisual Material  
| 1  
| 5 days   
  
Periodicals | In-library use only  
| In-library use only  
**Postgraduate**  
| Books | 15  
| 42 days   
  
Audiovisual Material | 1 | 5 days  
  
| Periodicals  | In-library use only | In-library use only  
Renewing of items is allowed once for an additional 14 days.   
  

### [Interlibrary Loan Service](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/interlibrary-loan-service)
  * [Obtain materials](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-from-other-libraries1) (books, articles and chapters) from other libraries that are not available at the USEK Library.
  * Graduates can request up to 15 items.
  * Postgraduates can request up to 20 items.
  * The loan period for books is 14 days, or according to the exceptions policy of the lending library.
  * Renewing of items is not guaranteed; renewals should be made one week prior to the due date indicated on the item.

  

### Find Resources
  * [Catalog](https://sierra.usek.edu.lb/*frf) for searching the USEK Library print collections including books, journals, newspapers, theses and dissertations, music recordings, etc.
  * [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) for searching a large and varied collection (article databases, e-book collections, etc.) of electronic resources.
  * [Find a title](http://yf7lm7ay6z.search.serialssolutions.com/ejp/?libHash=YF7LM7AY6Z#/?language=en-US&titleType=ALL) with this search tool to find a book or journal.
  * [One Search](http://usek.summon.serialssolutions.com/) for searching the USEK Library Catalog and our databases simultaneously to quickly provide credible library results through a single search box.
  * [Off-campus access to electronic resources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/off-campus-access) to access online resources from anywhere off campus using your USEK username and password.

  

### [Reserve a Study Room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room)
  * [Reserve a group study room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room2) in the Kaslik campus Library.
  * You can reserve up to 2 hours of study room use per day and up to 6 total hours per week.
  * Reservations can be made up to two weeks in advance.
  * Reserved rooms must be claimed within the first 15 minutes of the reservation.
  * Rooms are available Monday-Friday during Library opening hours but not on weekends, holidays, or during periods when the Library is closed.

  

### [Get Help](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/get-help)
  * [Ask Us](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us) for assistance with your research by contacting a librarian in person, by phone, by e-mail or chat.
  * [Research appointments](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/appointment) with a librarian for in-depth help with your research paper or assignment.
  * [Research Workshops](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/register-for-a-workshop) for workshops on how to learn about using library resources, [electronic resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php), the scholarly research process, citation styles, plagiarism, and other topics.
  * [Research guides](hhttp://libguides.usek.edu.lb/) provide you with targeted information on a specific topic or tool to help you in your research.
  * [Cite your sources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/cite-your-sources) for how to cite your references properly.

  

### [Copy/Print/Scan](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps)
  * To activate or recharge your account, ask for the Retail Cash Officer at the Registrar Office.

  

### [Suggest a Purchase](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/suggest-a-purchase)
  * Provide suggestions for the purchase of resources that would improve our collection.

  

### Activities
  * [Exhibitions](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/exhibit-your-artwork) for exhibiting your artwork (paintings, photos, etc.) in the Library.
  * [Film, Photography and Recording](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/filming/photography-and-recording-in-the-library) for organizing your session with the Library to make use of the premises to film, photograph or record.

###  Kamal Youssef El Hage Between the Philosophy of Lebanese Nationalism and the Philosophy of the Arab Nation
From November 17, 2017 to February 2018
On the occasion of the centenary of Kamal Youssef El Hage’s birth (17 February 2017 – 16 February 2018) and World Philosophy Day, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), in collaboration with _Bayt Al-Fikr – Asassiyat Kamal Youssef El Hage_ , organized a seminar entitled: “Kamal Youssef El Hage – Between the Philosophy of Lebanese Nationalism and the Philosophy of the Arab Nation”. The seminar was followed by the opening of an exhibition entitled: “Kamal Youssef El Hage: life and works in pictures”, at the USEK Library.  
  
This event, hosted by the Office of the Deputy President for Cultural Affairs, took place on Friday, November 17, 2017, at 5 p.m. in Auditorium B.  
  
The exhibition will continue to run till the end of February 2018.

##  Library Partnerships 
In the spirit of collaborative development, open communication and collegiality, USEK Library strives to enrich its efforts to fulfill its mission to expand its network through national and international initiatives and partnerships. 
### International

![e-corpus](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45228Image.png?v=201907241036)
e-corpus is a collective digital and heritage library founded in 2009. Updated regularly, it classifies and provides multiple types of documents: manuscripts, archives, books, newspapers, prints, sound recordings, and videos.
[Read More](https://www.wdl.org/en/search/?countries=LB&institution=holy-spirit-university-of-kaslik)
![World Digital Library](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45229Image.png?v=201907121314)
The World Digital Library provides free extensive documentation in several languages from countries and cultures around the world on the Internet.
[Read More](http://www.wdl.org/en/search/gallery/?countries=LB&institution=holy-spirit-university-of-kaslik)
![Hill Museum & Manuscript Library](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45230Image.png?v=201907241037)
Hill Museum & Manuscript Library is a leading cultural preservation organization with the mission to identify, digitally photograph, catalog, and archive material to make available the contents of endangered manuscripts belonging to threatened communities.
[Read More](http://hmml.org/)
![I-Revues](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45231Image.png?v=201907241037)
I-Revues is a service offered to publishers in any scientific field for the electronic dissemination of journals, scientific conferences and book services, with a catalog containing approximately forty publications, and more than 20,000 documents.
[Read More](http://irevues.inist.fr/?mmdedit=on&valeur=Universit%C3%A9+Saint-Esprit+de+Kaslik&tri=ab)
![e-ktobe](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45232Image.png?v=201907121319)
e-ktobe is a database for Syriac manuscripts which gathers information about texts and their physical nature (materials, composition notebooks, binder, writing, etc.), colophons and notes of Syriac manuscripts.
[Read More](http://www.mss-syriaques.org/usek.html)
![Ninawa Daher Foundation](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/47763Image.jpg?v=202012161013)
The Ninawa Daher Foundation strives to support young people’s dreams by promoting equal opportunity initiatives and inclusive participation in diverse communities. Born in 1979 into a Lebanese family in Argentina, Ninawa became a renowned journalist and a prominent voice for empowering youths as leaders of social justice. Her tragic death in a car crash in 2011 inspired Argentina to choose her birthday on October 3 to celebrate Lebanese-Argentinian Youth Day.
[Read More](https://www.ninawadaher.org/)
![The Arab-Brazilian Chamber of Commerce](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/47764Image.jpg?v=202012161018)
The Arab-Brazilian Chamber of Commerce has been operating for over 68 years to strengthen the ties between Brazilians and Arabs and to promote economic, social, and cultural development. It plays an essential role in the development of the relationship between these two parts of the world.
[Read More](https://www.ccab.org.br/)
![Casa Árabe \(The Arab House\)](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/47765Image.jpg?v=202012161019)
The Arab House represents people’s homes and way of life across 22 Arab countries. Initially a virtual space affiliated to the Arab-Brazilian Chamber of Commerce (ABCC) in São Paulo, Brazil, it is a space dedicated to cultural activities, library information, and an Arabic language forum with discussions on the lives of Arab immigrants and their descendants in Brazil.
[Read More](https://www.ccab.org.br/)

![Lebanese Academic Library Consortium](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45233Image.png?v=201907241037)
Lebanese Academic Library Consortium (LALC) is the first national consortium “to cooperate in the selection, pricing negotiations and access methods of electronic resources” for the best interests of Universities and their library users.
[Read More](http://lalc.lau.edu.lb/)
![Lebanese ILL/DD Services](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45234Image.png?v=201907121320)
Lebanese ILL/DD Services – LIDS is another national consortium whose main objective is to implement a Lebanese interlibrary loan and document delivery service by which “the request or supply of books or copies of articles are managed between libraries.”
![WorldShare Interlibrary Loan](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45235Image.png?v=201907241038)
WorldShare Interlibrary Loan connects you to thousands of libraries whose entire collections can be viewed at a glance in WorldCat®.It allows you to get resources from thousands of libraries all over the world while saving time and money with each ILL request.
[Read More](https://www.oclc.org/en/worldshare-ill.html)

![Lebanese Library Association](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45236Image.png?v=201907241039)
Lebanese Library Association (LLA) provides leadership for the development, promotion and enhancement of the library and information sector to deliver quality services to the Lebanese community.
[Read More](http://lebaneselibraryassociation.org/)
![American Library Association \(ALA\)](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/46419Image.jpg?v=201907241055)
American Library Association (ALA) is a nonprofit organization based in the United States that promotes libraries and library education internationally. It is the oldest and largest library association in the world, with more than 57,000 members. The mission of ALA is “to provide leadership for the development, promotion, and improvement of library and information services and the profession of librarianship in order to enhance learning and ensure access to information for all.” USEK Library is registered in the following LLA divisions:  
  
[Association of College and Research Libraries (ACRL)](http://www.ala.org/acrl/)   
[Library Leadership and Management Association (LLAMA)](http://www.ala.org/llama/)   
  

[Read More](https://www.ala.org/)
![International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45237Image.png?v=201907241041)
The International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions (IFLA) is the leading international body representing the interests of library and information services and their users. It is the global voice of the library and information professions. USEK Library is registered in the following IFLA sections and Special Interest Group (SIG):   
  

  * Section 02: [Academic & Research Libraries ](https://www.ifla.org/academic-and-research-libraries)
  * Section 05: [ Social Science Libraries](https://www.ifla.org/social-science-libraries)
  * Section 14:[ Acquisitions & Collection Development ](https://www.ifla.org/acquisition-collection-development)
  * Section 15:[ Document Delivery & Resource Sharing ](https://www.ifla.org/docdel)
  * Section 18:[ Rare Books and Manuscripts](https://www.ifla.org/rare-books-and-special-collections)
  * Section 19:[ Preservation & Conservation ](https://www.ifla.org/preservation-and-conservation)
  * Section 26:[ Asia & Oceania ](https://www.ifla.org/asia-and-oceania)
  * Section 36:[ Reference and Information Services ](https://www.ifla.org/reference-and-information-services)
  * Special Interest Groups:[ RELINDIAL: Religions: Libraries and Dialogue](https://www.ifla.org/about-relindial)


[Read More](http://www.ifla.org/)
![Islamic Manuscript Association](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/46420Image.jpg?v=201907241055)
Islamic Manuscript Association is an international non-profit organization dedicated to protecting Islamic manuscript collections and supporting those who work with them. It was formed in response to the urgent need to address the poor preservation and inaccessibility of many Islamic manuscript collections around the world.
[Read More](http://www.islamicmanuscript.org/)
![Institut du Monde Arabe](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/46421Image.jpg?v=201907241107)
Institut du Monde Arabe is an organization founded in Paris in 1980 by 18 Arab countries with France to research and disseminate information about the Arab world and its cultural and spiritual values. The Institute was established to cultivate real dialogue between the Arab world, France and Europe.
[Read More](https://www.imarabe.org/)
![MELCom International](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45238Image.png?v=201907241107)
MELCom International, the European Association of Middle East Librarians, is a non-governmental organization devoted to promoting co-operation among individuals and institutions in Europe the Middle East and throughout the world concerning all aspects of librarianship in the Middle East, book collecting, the book trade and publishing.
[Read More](http://www.melcominternational.org/)
![MLA](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45239Image.png?v=201907121329)
MLA is a nonprofit, educational organization with more than 4,000 professional members and partners in health sciences information worldwide. MLA provides lifelong educational opportunities, supports a knowledgebase of health information research, and works with a global network of partners to promote the importance of quality information to improve the health of the community and the public. USEK Library is registered in the following MLA sections:   
  

  * Section 02: Educational Media and Technologies
  * Section 10: Nursing and Allied Health Resources 
  * Section 20: Public Services
  * Section 22: Collection Development
  * Section 26: International Cooperation


[Read More](https://www.mlanet.org/)
![North American Serials Interest Group](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/45240Image.png?v=201907121330)
Established in 1985, the North American Serials Interest Group, Inc. (NASIG) is an independent organization that promotes communication and sharing of ideas among all members of the serials information chain – anyone working with or concerned about serial publications.
[Read More](http://www.nasig.org/)
![Société d'études Syriaques](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/46422Image.jpg?v=201907241110)
Société d'études Syriaques is a scholarly society whose objective is the cultivation of Eastern Syriac-speaking Christianity (Aramaic of Edessa / Urhay, now Urfa in Turkey of the S.E.), whatever their confession. For scientific and academic purposes, its members are interested in history, art, literature and, generally, anything that has enriched the culture of Syriac-speaking communities.
[Read More](https://www.etudessyriaques.org/)
![Oral History Society](https://www.usek.edu.lb/ContentFiles/46423Image.jpg?v=201907241111)
Oral History Society promotes the collection, preservation and use of recorded memories of the past. As well as offering practical advice and support, the Society aims to raise standards in oral history practices across a range of activities and disciplines.
[Read More](http://www.ohs.org.uk/)

##  Newpapers & Periodicals 
Our newspapers and periodicals collection contains more than 1,600 titles on a broad range of subjects, and in various languages.  
  
These titles have been collected throughout the history of USEK Library, as well as from generous donations.   
  
The most important titles that have fundamental research and heritage value are: A _l-Hoda, New Lebanese American Journal, Al-Muhajjer, Al-Haqiqa, Al-Maarad and Al-Moktataf_.  
  
Search Newspapers and Periodicals  
  
Please note that: 
  * Newspapers are available for use in the building only
  * The latest issues of periodicals are for use in the building only
  * Bound periodicals are available for short term loans

##  Manuscripts 
On May 14th, 2002, the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM) decided to relocate all the manuscripts of the OLM monasteries, about 30 monastic libraries in total, to the Library of the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), to be gathered in one collection. This huge collection is known today as the OLM Collection. Moreover, there are some other private collections which have been donated to the Library to be preserved and digitized for scholarly studies.  
  

### Mission
The Mission of the USEK Manuscripts Department is to present new historical source materials which may play a vital role in Lebanese historical studies. By facilitating access to the original manuscripts, scholars and students are encouraged to access the manuscripts they need to complete their scholarly research.   
  

### Contents of Manuscripts
There are approximately 2,000 manuscripts, handwritten in Syriac, Arabic, Latin, and Greek. They cover a wide variety of topics, such as theology (including many liturgical Maronite texts), Islam, philosophy, Syriac and Arabic grammar, literature, astronomy, and history. Many of these manuscripts are translations from Latin to Garshuni (Arabic in Syriac letters), and some are unique like OLM 263, which is claimed to be the oldest Maronite Syriac Liturgical textbook for the Palm Sunday Office of Readings, copied at Qozhaya Monastery in 1493.  
  
This collection also provides valuable pieces of information about Lebanese heritage and historiography; many of these Maronite manuscripts contain unique remarks recorded by Lebanese manuscripts copyists, which convey rare historical and local events.   
  

### The Project
Although the work is still in progress, a comprehensive database for the content and digital online samples of these manuscripts is being created; however, for the time being, a [checklist](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20200205Checklist-030123.pdf) can be accessed at the USEK main library.  
If you cannot find what you are looking for, or need help, please contact us.   
  
Steps for Cataloguing and Preservation:   
1. Providing a full codicological description of the manuscripts  
2. Preserving the manuscripts for their cultural and historical value  
3. Digitizing the manuscripts for long term preservation  
4. Adding a descriptive record and image to the digital library

###  Exhibition: “Lebanon: A ‘Caricature’ History”
From April 18 to October 18, 2023
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized an exhibition showcasing the caricatures of Pierre Sadek, titled "صادق... بريشتو" - “Lebanon: A ‘Caricature’ History”.   
  
This exhibition, hosted by the USEK Library, in collaboration with the Pierre Sadek Foundation, took place from April 18 to October 18, 2023, from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., at the USEK Library.

##  Research Workshops 
USEK Library offers high-quality instruction sessions for students, staff, and faculty on Library resources and services to help in developing their research competencies.  
  
The workshops are free and open to all USEK registered students, faculty and staff.  
  
USEK Alumni may also attend the workshops, space permitting.  
  
Workshops may be cancelled due to insufficient registration.  
Registrants will be notified if a workshop is cancelled.  
  
Faculty members interested in scheduling a customized, librarian-led instruction session tailored for their class, simply need to request a [Library Instruction Session.](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/request-a-library-instruction-session1)  
  
For further assistance: 
  * [Ask Us](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us): Get assistance with your research by contacting a librarian in person, by phone, by e-mail or chat;
  * Research appointments: Make an appointment with a librarian for in-depth help with your research paper or assignment;
  * [Research guides](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/?b=g&d=a): Use for help finding discipline-specific resources;
  * [Cite your sources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/cite-your-sources): Learn how to cite your references properly;
  * Avoid plagiarism: Get tips and guidance on how to avoid plagiarism in your research papers.

##  Request a Library Instruction Session 
USEK Library Instruction Sessions can help your students develop their library skills and take advantage of our academic resources available for their research tasks, instead of relying on Google and other non-credible resources. Book a session today to help your students develop best practices in their study skills.  
  
As faculty/instructors, you are encouraged to book a librarian-led Instruction Session for your students to help them take advantage of all our academic resources and tailored specifically for your course.  
  
Please read our [Library Instruction Guidelines](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/library-instruction-guidelines) before submitting a request.   
  
Only faculty members can fill out the form to request a library instruction session.

##  Rare Books and Incunabula 
In the spirit of the University’s aspiration to “contribute to the welfare of the human being, all human beings, throughout education, research and publication in all fields of knowledge”, the Library has acquired notable collections of rare books and incunabula. These exceptional texts which are difficult to locate and replace, have fundamental research value.   
  
There are several factors that play a major role in deciding what is categorized as a rare book (printed before 1880) or an incunabulum (printed before 1501): provenance, age, scarcity, significance in content, research value, and unique characteristics. Because these materials are fragile and/or have a unique nature, they are not placed for loan and circulation; they can only be consulted in the reading rooms.  
  
It has taken years of consistent researching and collecting, making the Library strong in the areas of humanities, literature, history, art, theology, and philosophy. Our literary Rare Books and Incunabula hold works in Arabic, English, French, German, Italian, Latin, Ancient Greek, Syriac and Garshuni.  
  
**Search Rare Books and Incunabula**  
Please note only part of our collection is currently available online.  
We are working to add hard-copy catalogs to the online version.  
If you cannot find what you are looking for, Ask a Librarian.

##  Place Materials on Reserve 
### Overview
The USEK Library Course Reserve Service allows faculty members to set aside print and non-print library items required for coursework.  
Reserve items are intended for registered students in a specific course, as well as other USEK community members including faculty and staff. Unlike other library materials, course reserves have non-renewable, short-term loan periods to ensure equitable access throughout the semester.  
  

### For Faculty
**Placing Materials on Reserve**  
  
Eligible Materials  
Faculty may request to place the following items on reserve: 
  * Library-owned books, book chapters, and journal articles
  * Bound periodicals
  * CDs and DVDs
  * Instructor-provided copies of required materials

  
  
The following items are not eligible for reserve: 
  * Materials from other libraries
  * Items obtained via Interlibrary Loan
  * Reference-only items
  * Entire works or a majority of a work without proper copyright clearance
Submission Process 
  * Complete the Course Reserve Request Form with detailed information
  * Submit requests at least two weeks before the semester begins
  * To retain items for a subsequent semester, notify the Circulation Desk before the end of the term

  
  

### For Students and Staff
**Accessing Reserve Materials**  
  
Borrowing Guidelines 
  * Eligibility: All USEK students, faculty, and staff may access course reserves
  * Loan Period:  
- Short-term loan: Up to 3 hours (9:00 a.m. – 4:00 p.m.)
  * Restrictions:  
- Some items are for in-library use only  
- Reserve materials are non-renewable  
- A maximum of two items may be checked out or placed on hold at a time

  
  
Fines and Penalties 
  * Overdue fines: $1 USD per item per hour (maximum: $10 USD per item)
  * Repeated offenses: Users who repeatedly return items late or restrict access may face borrowing limitations

  
  

### Contact Information
For assistance or questions, please contact:  
USEK Library: circulation@usek.edu.lb

##  Register for a Workshop 
Attend a session and get to know what your library can do for you.  
  
USEK Library workshops are a great place for you to learn about the Library services and its resources to improve your research skills. The sessions are open to all, so if you are a USEK student, faculty or staff with a valid ID card, just sign up.   
  
We offer several workshops covering a wide range of topics to help you get to know your library better and use the library services, resources and research tools to improve your learning and research experience. Our workshops cover topics such as: 
  * Improving your research skills and methods, and managing research data; 
  * Accessing and using electronic resources;
  * Searching for materials and information resources;
  * Referencing materials;
  * Detecting and avoiding plagiarism. 

  
Click [here](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/research-tools/research-workshops) for more details on available workshops and registration.

##  Off-Campus Access 
Access to [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) that the USEK Library subscribes to is available to current USEK students, faculty and staff.   
  
1. On-campus users logging on from a campus IP address are allowed access to ALL electronic resources without restrictions.  
2. If logging on off-campus, follow the procedure below:  
a. Visit the USEK Library website as usual  
b. After selecting the required database, you will be prompted to authenticate that you are currently an enrolled student, faculty member, or staff  
c. Enter your USEK username and password  
d. Once authenticated, you will be automatically transferred to the database you selected.  
  
Note 
  * No configuration is required on your part; you can simply begin your research.
  * Almost all [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) are available to USEK off-campus users.
  * However, due to licensing restrictions, some databases are only available on campus; this will be indicated in the description of the database.

  
For more information about the off-campus access service, you may contact the Electronic Collections Department.

##  Reserve a Library Tour 
With over 300,000 print volumes and other items, USEK Library is also home to a Digitization Center and a Preservation Center, and accommodates rich Rare and Special Collections in an effort to preserve our Lebanese heritage, and support the instructional needs of our community.   
  
USEK Library tours will guide you through the wide variety of study spaces, library collections, technologies, equipment, and facilities available to library users. To help you find your way around, the Library offers an introduction to our many services.   
  

### Types of visits
Library visits are divided into the following: 
  * Guest or school tours. To reserve a tour, please complete a [Reserve a Library Tour form](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-library-tour2). 
  * Student tours organized by Faculty/instructors for their classes. To reserve a library tour for a class, please complete this [form](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-an-orientation-session).
  * Visiting guests, researchers and academia can contact us to book a tour by sending an email to biblio@usek.edu.lb

  

### Booking Requirements
  * A minimum notice of five (5) working days is required;
  * After submitting an online library tour or orientation session request, the Library will process your request and email you the response;
  * In the event of any change or cancellations, the requestor should notify the Library 24 hours in advance, by emailing biblio@usek.edu.lb;
  * Walk-in tours are not permitted without prior arrangement;

  
For any inquiries regarding library tours, please email biblio@usek.edu.lb.

##  Finding Aids 
###  The following Finding Aids provide information on notable archival and special collections housed in the Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies at USEK Library.
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/Uploaded%20Images/20240123Haimari.jpg) |  |  |  **Georges and Maroun Haimari Collection, 1920-2014**  
The Georges and Maroun Haimari Collection is a significant archive of historical photos and press clippings documenting Lebanon's history from the French Mandate to post-Independence. As key figures in the Presidency Palace protocol, the Haimaris' contributions further enhance the collection’s value for understanding Lebanon’s political evolution.  
[VIEW PDF](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20250624GeorgeMarouHaimari.pdf)  
  
  
---|---|---|---  
![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/Uploaded%20Images/20250624PierreMandajian.jpg) |  |  |  **Pierre Maadanjian Photographic Collection**  
The Pierre Maadanjian Photographic Collection showcases the work of the renowned Lebanese photographer, capturing Lebanon’s cultural and social history. His images document Beirut’s pre-war charm, societal transformations, landscapes, and iconic figures, including singers, actors, politicians, and key public events.  
[VIEW PDF](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20250624PierreMadanjian.pdf)

##  Reproduction Service 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/use-your-library)
USEK Library provides researchers with digital reproductions and paper photocopies of items available in the library’s collections.  
  
Reproductions are intended for personal or scholarly use only.  
  
USEK Library reserves the right to refuse any reproduction request, in its sole discretion. The Library reserves the right to refuse orders when the item is deemed too fragile to be photographed or scanned. All requests are also subject to [Lebanese copyright law and regulations](https://www.economy.gov.lb/public/uploads/files/4600_3516_9524.pdf).

[Terms and Conditions](javascript:;)
1. Normal processing time for duplication orders is 5 to 10 working days.  
  
2. Reproduction of rare books, manuscripts, newspapers, and archives housed in the USEK Library should be credited. Credits for film, television, and video may be run at the end of the program or presentation.  
Credit Format:  
Name or title of the item, name of collection, name of Center or special collections, USEK Library, Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, Lebanon.  
  
3. For reproduction or publishing, a “[Notice of Intent to Publish Special Collections Material from USEK Library](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Assets/20210121Notice-050923.pdf)” should be filled and signed for approval.  
  
4. A copy of any publication resulting from extensive research using USEK Library materials should be offered gratis to the Library.  
  
5. In all cases, the USEK University Library only owns the physical item and therefore does not assume any responsibility for literary property, copyright, or any other legal issues involved in the publication and reproduction of items in its collections. In the case of both textual and visual materials (including photographs and works of art), it is the responsibility of the user to secure permission from the appropriate copyright holder.  
  
6. The researcher agrees not to reproduce copies as dust jackets, as end papers, or to use in an advertisement or any commercial use of a similar nature, nor to mass reproduce, unless specifically authorized by USEK Library.  
  
7. Content may not be altered or manipulated without special permission from USEK Library, except for minor cropping, brightness, contrast adjustment and noise reduction.
[Copyright and Permissions](javascript:;)
According to [WIPO](https://www.wipo.int/portal/en/index.html) “Copyright legislation is part of the wider body of law known as intellectual property (IP) which refers broadly to the creations of the human mind. IP rights protect the interests of innovators and creators by giving them rights over their creations”.  
  
**1. How Do I Get Permission for Copyrighted Works?**  
[Lebanese Law on the Protection of Literary and Artistic Property*. (No. 75 of April 3, 1999)](https://wipolex.wipo.int/en/legislation/details/2786) says:  
“The copyright holder shall have the exclusive right to exploit the work commercially and, accordingly, shall have the right to authorize or prohibit the following: any copying, printing, recording and reproduction of the work in any manner or form including photography, cinematography, sound or visual recordings of any kind or any other form”. For more information check Chapter V, pp. 14-22.  
  
**2. What is the Public Domain?**  
The public domain term refers to works that are not protected by copyright law.  
Works become in the public domain because their copyright duration has expired, or they have been dedicated to the public domain by the copyright owner, or the work is ineligible for copyright protection.  
No permission is needed to copy public domain works. Author’s moral right is a must even in Public Domain works; user should preserve the integrity of the author work and cite it properly.  
  
**3. Terms of Protection (copyright duration)** According to the Lebanese Law | Copyright Duration  
---|---  
Author | Life of the author and 50 years after his/her death, to be computed from the end of the year in which the death has occurred.  
  
Joint authorship | Life of the joint authors and 50 years after the death of the last joint author, to be computed from the end of the year in which the death has occurred. Should one of the authors die without leaving heirs, his/her share shall pass to the co-authors or to their heirs, unless stated otherwise.  
Collective / Audiovisual works  
| 50 years to be computed from the end of the year in which the work has been made available to the public.  
Anonymous or pseudonymous work | The term of protection shall expire 50 years after the work has been lawfully made available to the public.  
Performers | 50 years to be computed from the end of the year in which the performance has been carried out.  
Producers of sound recordings | 50 years to be computed from the end of the year in which the first fixation of sound on tangible material has taken place.   
Broadcasting organizations | 50 years to be computed from the end of the year in which the broadcasting of their programs has taken place.  
Publishing houses | 50 years to be computed from the end of the year in which the first publication has taken place.   
  
For detailed information, check: [Lebanese Law on the Protection of Literary and Artistic Property*. (No. 75 of April 3, 1999)](https://wipolex.wipo.int/en/legislation/details/2786)

##  Reserve a Study Room 
You can book one of our two (2) fully equipped project rooms located in the Library. These study spaces are ideal for independent study, working with a partner, for collaborative project work, or course work meetings.  
  
You can reserve a room online up to two (2) weeks in advance. Use the button below to book your room.  
  
Check our options and policies for further details on available equipment and on how to use the rooms.   
  

[ Reserve a Study Room ](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room2)
  
OPTIONS  
These rooms are available for USEK students, staff, faculty and administrators upon reservation. The Library also offers a Multipurpose Room for use by USEK staff, faculty and administrators only.  
All the study rooms are located in Reading Room 2 area. To reserve a room, send an online request up to two (2) weeks in advance.  
  

### Available Equipment
**Project Rooms 1 & 2**  
Seating capacity: 4 in each room  
43″ LED Screen (You can connect your laptop to the monitor for projection)  
Wireless internet access  
**  
Multipurpose Room**  
Seating capacity: 25-30  
65″ LCD Screen (You can connect your laptop to the monitor for projection)  
Wireless internet access  
Flip charts and markers (available on demand)  
  

### Reservations and availability
Rooms are available Monday-Friday only during Library opening hours; they are not available on weekends, holidays, or during periods when the Library is closed.  
Library rooms may not be used for classes on an on-going basis.  
Users can reserve study rooms for a period of two hours per day and up to 6 total hours per week.  
Before reserving a study room, please read our [Study Room Reservation Policy](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/study-room-reservation-policy).

##  USEK Library: Long History, New Look 
### A stunning, newly refurbished state-of-the-art Library is now available at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), following a renovation that took the space from old and tired to fresh and inspired.
During the renovation, the Library has been redesigned to provide critical physical spaces that support research, to offer readers reading areas that meet their study needs, and to create a public area that provides access to our unseen treasures through exhibitions in our new gallery.  
  
The Library building is one of USEK’s original structures. It has aged with grace, but has also kept up with contemporary library trends, including: 
  * Study rooms, which feature ergonomic spaces with the latest technology;
  * Adaptable seating options which can facilitate individual work or collaborative learning;
  * A large multipurpose room which can accommodate a range of events and activities;
  * A quiet study area capable of accommodating approximately 100 readers at a time.

##  Undergraduates 
### Access
  * To borrow material, you will need your USEK ID Card;
  * Your USEK ID Card is also used to pay for [printing and photocopying in the library](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps). 

  

### [Borrow & Renew](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-and-renew)
Category | Item Type  
| N° of Items Allowed to Check-Out | Loan Period   
---|---|---|---  
**Undergraduate**  
  
  
  
| Books | 5  
| 14 days  
  
Audiovisual Material  
| 1  
| 5 days   
  
Periodicals | In-library use only  
| In-library use only  
  
Renewing of items is allowed once for an additional 14 days.   
  

### [Interlibrary Loan Service](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/interlibrary-loan-service)
  * [Obtain materials](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-from-other-libraries1) (books, articles and chapters) from other libraries that are not available at the USEK Library.
  * Undergraduates can request up to 5 items.
  * The loan period for books is 14 days, or according to the exceptions policy of the lending library.
  * Renewing of items is not guaranteed; renewals should be made one week prior to the due date indicated on the item.

  

### Find Resources
  * [Catalog](https://sierra.usek.edu.lb/*frf) for searching the USEK Library print collections including books, journals, newspapers, theses and dissertations, music recordings, etc.
  * [One Search](http://usek.summon.serialssolutions.com/) for searching the USEK Library Catalog and our databases simultaneously to quickly provide credible library results through a single search box.
  * [Electronic Resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php) for searching a large and varied collection (article databases, e-book collections, etc.) of electronic resources.
  * [Find a title](http://yf7lm7ay6z.search.serialssolutions.com/ejp/?libHash=YF7LM7AY6Z#/?language=en-US&titleType=ALL) with this search tool to find a book or journal.
  * [Off-campus access to electronic resources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/off-campus-access) to access online resources from anywhere off campus using your USEK username and password.

  

### [Reserve a Study Room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room)
  * [Reserve a group study room](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/reserve-a-study-room2) in the Kaslik campus Library.
  * You can reserve up to 2 hours of study room use per day and up to 6 total hours per week.
  * Reservations can be made up to two weeks in advance.
  * Reserved rooms must be claimed within the first 15 minutes of the reservation.
  * Rooms are available Monday-Friday during Library opening hours but not on weekends, holidays, or during periods when the Library is closed.

  

### [Get Help](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/get-help)
  * [Ask Us](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us) for assistance with your research by contacting a librarian in person, by phone, by email or chat.
  * [Research appointments](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/appointment) with a librarian for in-depth help with your research paper or assignment.
  * [Research Workshops](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/register-for-a-workshop) for workshops on how to learn about using library resources, [electronic resources](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/az.php), the scholarly research process, citation styles, plagiarism, and other topics.
  * [Research guides](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/) provide you with targeted information on a specific topic or tool to help you in your research.
  * [Cite your sources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/cite-your-sources) for how to cite your references properly.

  

### [Copy/Print/Scan](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps)
  * To activate or recharge your account, ask for the Retail Cash Officer at the Registrar Office.

  

### Activities
  * [Exhibitions](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/exhibit-your-artwork) for exhibiting your artwork (paintings, photos, etc.) in the Library.
  * [Film, Photography and Recording](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/filming/photography-and-recording-in-the-library) for organizing your session with the Library to make use of the premises to film, photograph or record.

###  Cooperation with Moise Khayrallah Center in USA
2022
The USEK Library is delighted to announce its cooperation with Moise Khayrallah Center in USA aimed at implementing the Arabic OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology to the digital periodicals from the Latin American collection housed at the USEK Library. These periodicals were written in Arabic and published in Latin America by Lebanese immigrants, dating back to the 19th century, era of the great immigration wave, onwards.  
  
This partnership is part of the arabicarchives.org project initiated by Khayrallah Center, which collects the early Arab immigrants’ archives that have left remarkable legacy in North and South America. These records were not accessible because they were dispersed and stored in disparate locations, and hence not digitally searchable. Consequently, the Center has created a completely searchable database of these publications by developing Arabic OCR technology to render the digitized images of these history pages into searchable text.  
  
The objectives of this collaboration are to contribute to scholarly research, explore a heritage that spans years and tells the stories of Lebanese/Arab pioneers, and expand non-English content on the web.  
  
Accordingly, our digital periodicals from the Latin American collection will be fully searchable, allowing users to easily search their content by keyword.  
  
_“We at USEK Library, entrusted with this legacy, are proud to join this remarkable initiative, to bring our treasures and efforts in support of the expertise of Khayrallah Center to achieve this worthy goal”, said Fr. Joseph Moukarzel, USEK Library Director.  
  
“Joining this partnership allows us to share our collection with scholars, researchers and public worldwide, a step forward in keeping with our commitment to discoverability and to the growth of our renowned collections”, added Fr. Moukarzel.  
  
“The Khayrallah Center is delighted and privileged to collaborate with USEK Library, one of the premiere archives in the world for Lebanese history. This partnership will add a treasure trove of periodicals to our Arabic database and give researchers and the general public unprecedented access to a wealth of historical literature about Lebanese migration to South America. We regard this as the first step in a very important partnership between NC State University and USEK."_ stated Dr. Akram Khater, Director of Moise Khayrallah Center.  
  
To know more about the Latin American collection at the USEK Library, click [here](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/latin-american-collection).

###  IFPO Doctoral Training 2018
May 30, 2018
The 2nd session of Doctoral Training 2018 on Critical Studies of Arabic Manuscripts, Archives and Inscriptions (دراسات نقدية في المخطوطات والمحفوظات والنقوش العربية), organized by the Institut Français du Proche-Orient (IFPO) under the coordination of Mr. Frédéric Imbert, was held at the USEK Library on May 30, 2018.

##  Visitors 
### Access
USEK Library welcomes the use of its collections by researchers, scholars, or others, and institutions that are not affiliated with the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, under certain conditions.  
  
Visitors are entitled to consult and borrow books if their subscription category permits; they can also consult journals and other materials and obtain some information and reference assistance. To use the library, you need to apply for a Library card.  
  

### Library Account and Cards
  * To obtain a Library card (Category A, B, C and D), individuals must submit an [online application form](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/library-applications) along with a scanned passport photograph and proof of identity (National ID, passport, etc.). You will be notified by e-mail once the card is ready.
  * As for institutions (Category E), they must fill out an [institutional application form](https://apply.usek.edu.lb/library-applications).
  * When requesting books, you must present your Library card. Library cards cannot be used by anyone else, and lost cards must be reported immediately. The Library is not responsible for any outcome arising from the unauthorized use of your Library card.
  * Every Library user has a right to privacy and confidentiality while using Library materials; therefore, names of borrowers and their accounts are never disclosed.

  
**Subscription Fees** Category | Subscription | Fee in USD  
---|---|---  
A | One day | 5   
B | One week | 10  
C | Three months | 50   
D | One-year | 100   
E | Institutional (one year)  
| 150  
If you wish to use on-campus parking facilities, a yearly charge of 30 USD will be added to the subscription fee.  
  
**Payment method**
  * Local visitors pay cash at the Library Access Office on the ground floor.
  * International visitors can pay by wire transfer - please contact us at libinfo@usek.edu.lb for more details.

### Walk-in access service
USEK Library offers its visitor a walk-in access service which allows our visitors to access certain databases, e-journals and e-books on the library premises (only).   
  
Please note that even in the library, some E-resources are not available to external users due to licensing restrictions.   
  
To use the walk-in access service please ask for assistance at the circulation desk in either reading room.   
  

###  [Borrow and Renew](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/borrow-and-renew)
Subscription | No. of Items | Loan Period | Audio-Visual and Bound Periodicals Loan  
---|---|---|---  
One day | ---- | ---- | ----

### Wireless access
USEK Library provides all its subscribed visitors a temporary Wi-Fi connection. Login details will be delivered to you by email once your card is issued.   
  
**Eduroam** :  
**All visitors from participating institutions can use USEK’s Eduroam secure wireless network by selecting the Eduroam wireless network (SSID) anywhere on campus. Users should use their home institution’s username (email format: username@domain ) and password to login to Eduroam.**  
  

### [Get Help](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/get-help)
  * [Ask Us](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/ask-us) for assistance with your research by contacting a librarian in person.
  * Research appointments with a librarian for in-depth help with your research paper or assignment.
  * [Research guides](http://libguides.usek.edu.lb/) provide you with targeted information on a specific topic or tool to help you in your research.
  * [Cite your sources](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/cite-your-sources) for how to cite your references properly.

  

###  [Copy/Print/Scan](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/copy-print-scan-cps) (CPS)
  * All visitors may set up a CPS account on their USEK Library card.
  * To activate or recharge your account ask at the Circulation Desk.
  * Note that scanning a document to your email address is free of charge.

  

### Activities
  * [Exhibitions](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/exhibit-your-artwork) to exhibit your artwork (paintings, photos, etc.) in the Library.
  * [Film, Photography and Recording](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/filming/photography-and-recording-in-the-library) for organizing your session if you would like to make use of the premises for filming, photography or recording.

  

### Change of Address
It is the responsibility of individuals to keep the Library informed of any address changes. Library fines will not be waived if visitor fail to notify us of a change of address. You can update your address with Library staff at the Circulation Desk.  
  
IMPORTANT  
Rules and regulations of USEK Library are to be respected. Failure to do so may result in the suspension of user borrowing privileges. Membership is discretionary and the administration reserves the right to refuse applications for membership without redress. The Library is responsible for safeguarding the confidentiality of a borrower's transactions and for providing an environment conducive for research.

###  Opening of Mr. Redha Tabet’s Exhibition
From February 15 to March 8, 2019
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik organized the opening of Mr. Redha Tabet’s exhibition, entitled “Fenêtres sur l'Arctique: Extraits du quotidien au camp de recherche de Coats Island, Nunavut, Canada”.  
  
This event, hosted by the USEK Library, took place on Friday, February 15, 2019, at 5:00 p.m., in Reading Room II – USEK Library  
  
The exhibition ran until Friday, March 8, 2019.

Aspire Roundtable on International Women’s Day

## 
October 25, 2025
Beirut International Conference on Intercultural and Interfaith Dialogue for Sustainability – BICIDS 2025 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
Under the High Patronage of His Excellency, the President of the Republic of Lebanon, General Joseph Aoun, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) and the One Voice Foundation, in collaboration with the Faith for Earth Coalition (UNEP), are organizing the Beirut International Conference on Intercultural and Interfaith Dialogue for Sustainability.   
  
The event will take place on Saturday, October 25, 2025, from 8:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., at the John Paul II Amphitheater.   
  
Building on Lebanon’s unique history of coexistence, this conference reaffirms the country’s role as a global hub for dialogue and action on peace, pluralism, and sustainability. It offers a unique platform to bring together international leaders, academics, diplomats, and civil society to turn dialogue into concrete solutions for people and the planet.   
  
For registration, please click [here](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fapply.usek.edu.lb%2Fusek-bicids-confirmation%2Fnew&data=05%7C02%7Ccynthiazeinoun%40usek.edu.lb%7Cd1369e34f72f4d98863308de08ab6c85%7C06d0a2c459b94cf8a36a9190f22cd1f6%7C0%7C0%7C638957729891914485%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=2doUUy%2BtSGf1e6hI0g9Ipz37VLdzh5VK5OEK2%2BRkBa8%3D&reserved=0).

## 
February 27, 2025
Breaking the Silence: A Reel Look at Eating Disorders 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
Eating disorders are often misunderstood; however, they impact many individuals physically, emotionally, and socially. “Breaking the Silence” was an event, in collaboration with the Department of Nutrition & Food Sciences and the Department of Psychology & Social Sciences, that aims to raise awareness and encourage open dialogue about these conditions.   
  
A panel discussion with experts and a movie screening shed lights on the struggles of individuals affected by eating disorders.   
  
**Event Details**   
Panel discussion   
Date: February 27, 2025   
Time: 11:00 am   
Location: Jean El Hawa Auditorium   
Movie screening of To the Bone   
Time: 6:30 pm   
Location: Building H (Ground Floor)

## 
August 18, 2021
Collaboration between USEK and Phoenix Medical 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
Recognizing the need to design and manufacture healthcare technologies locally, and strengthen the Lebanese healthcare system, USEK’s Biomedical Engineering Department has recently signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Phoenix Medical (member of INDEVCO Group) to bring together personnel, technological, and clinical resources.  
  
This MoU is based on the mutual recognition of the importance of research in the field of medical devices and form a nucleus for promoting excellence and professionalism in the field of healthcare technology to ultimately empower the health-tech industry in Lebanon and the region.  
  
As a result of this collaboration, USEK has officially launched the USEK-Phoenix joint medical program entitled “Medical Device Design”, open to all biomedical, electrical, computer, mechanical and telecom engineering students.

## 
June 12, 2023
Conference: The Future of the Rachid Karami International Fair 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized a conference on “The Future of the Rachid Karami International Fair”, animated by the guests below: 
  * Mr. Wassim Naghi, Professor at the Lebanese University, former president of the Union of Mediterranean Architects (UMAR)
  * Ms. Maya Hmeidan, Cultural heritage management specialist
  * Ms. Renata Negrelly, Cultural attaché at the Embassy of Brazil
  * Mr. Ahmad Nabulsi, independent filmmaker
  * Messrs. Nicolas Fayad and Charles Kettaneh, two architects and founding partners at East Architecture Studio

  
  
This event, hosted by the School of Architecture and Design and the International Affairs Office, in collaboration with the Institut français de Jounieh, took place on Monday, June 12, 2023, at 3:00 p.m., in the Conference Hall.   
  
As a unique complex in the Middle East recently added on the UNESCO list of World Heritage in Danger, the Rachid Karami International Fair in Tripoli was designed in 1962 by renowned Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer. This emblematic 70-hectare site remains a key architectural achievement of 20th-century modernism in the Middle East and a remarkable example of intercontinental cultural collaboration.

From November 2 to 30, 2022
Exhibition: “Faces & Places” 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized an exhibition entitled “Faces & Places”, featuring the most prominent modern Lebanese painters from the late 19th century to the early 20th century.  
  
This exhibition, curated by the School of Architecture and Design students as part of their research project “History of Modern Art in Lebanon”, ran from November 2 to 30, 2022, from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., at the USEK Archeological Museum.

## 
November 4, 2024
Inaugural Mass of the 2024-2025 Academic Year 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Pontifical School of Theology celebrated the inaugural Mass of its 2024-2025 Academic Year on Monday, November 4, 2024, at 11:00 a.m.  
  
Presided over by His Excellency Antoine Nabil Al-Andary, representing the President of the Assembly of Catholic Patriarchs and Bishops in Lebanon (APECL), this inaugural Mass was concelebrated by Fr. Georges Hobeika, General Vicar of the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM), representing the Reverend Superior General Fr. Abbot Hady Mahfouz, and Fr. Elias Hanna, Dean of the School. The mass also welcomed superiors of seminaries, faculty, staff, and students of the School.  
  
In his homily, Bishop Andari addressed Pope Francis’ fourth Encyclical, "He Has Loved Us” (_Dilexit nos_), issued on October 24. In this letter, the Pope explores the tradition and reality of ecclesial thought on human and divine love of the heart of Jesus Christ. He calls believers to renew their devotion to the Heart of Jesus, so that we may not forget the tenderness of faith, the joy of service, and the warmth of mission, as the Heart of Jesus drives us toward love and sends us forth to serve our brothers and sisters.  
  
Following the Holy Mass, a reception was held in front of the chapel entrance.

## 
2022
Connected Apiculture Project: Collaboration between USEK and the IMT Engineering School 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
As part of a collaboration between the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), Institut Mines Télécom (IMT) - École des Mines d'Alès, and the French start-up ConnectHive, a French delegation of academic and industrial partners has recently visited USEK to discuss their connected apiculture project.  
  
This project, including engineering students and researchers from both universities, aims to enable beekeepers to follow in real time the activity of their apiaries, by providing them with new technologies in IoT and AI designed to improve honey production and reduce bee colony losses.  
  
For more information about this collaboration, please visit: <https://www.imt-mines-ales.fr/en/node/12111>

May 2, 2025
Gilbert Rahbani Sings Mohammed Abdel Wahab – A Tribute to a Musical Legend 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
On May 2, 2025, audiences gathered for an unforgettable evening as Gilbert Rahbani revived the timeless melodies of Mohammed Abdel Wahab in a heartfelt tribute to one of the greatest composers of Arabic music. Through a carefully curated selection of masterpieces, the concert honored a legacy that continues to inspire generations.

## 
September 25, 2025
Diplomacy Across Oceans - 80 Years of Lebanon-Latin America 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) was pleased to announce a special conference and exhibition, titled “Diplomacy Across Oceans – 80 Years of Lebanon-Latin America”, which explored the rich history of Lebanese emigration to Latin America during the 19th and 20th centuries.  
  
Hosted by the Latin American Studies and Culture Center in collaboration with the International Affairs Office, this event was held on Thursday, September 25, 2025, at 4:00 p.m., at the USEK Library. It showcased rare archives, photographs, newspapers, and publications documenting the presence and impact of Lebanese communities across Brazil, Argentina, Chile, and Mexico. These materials, part of USEK’s Latin American Collection, were available both digitally and in print, serving as a valuable resource for researchers and scholars in the fields of migration, diaspora, and cultural studies.  
  
A highlight of the conference was the commemoration of President Camille Chamoun’s 1954 diplomatic visit to Latin America, marked through archival materials and the participation of the ambassadors of Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, and Uruguay.  
  
The exhibition was open to the public from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.   
  
To explore the collection featured in this event, visit:   
<https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/latin-american-collection>

## 
October 2, 2025
Lecture: Middle Eastern Diaspora in South America 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized an informative lecture titled “Middle Eastern Diaspora in South America”, delivered by Dr. Arlene Clemesha, Professor of Contemporary Arab History at the University of São Paulo, Brazil.  
  
Hosted by the School of Law and Political Sciences, the event took place on Thursday, October 2, 2025, from 11:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., at the Etienne Sacre Auditorium.  
  
The lecture provided an academic exploration of the historical and cultural dynamics that shaped the Middle Eastern presence in South America, offering valuable perspectives on migration, identity, and transnational connections.

## 
October 1, 2025
Law in the Movies: Absence of Malice 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
As part of its “Law in the Movies” series, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) invites you to the screening of Absence of Malice (1981), starring Paul Newman and Sally Field.   
  
The film follows a reporter who publishes a story based on a prosecutor’s false leak about a shop owner suspected of murder. It explores the tension between the public’s right to know and the protection of personal privacy, while also raising important ethical and legal questions about journalism, confidentiality, and freedom of speech.  
  
Hosted by the School of Law and Political Sciences, the event will take place on Wednesday, October 1, 2025, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., in the Conference Hall.  
  
A discussion between students and instructors will follow the screening.

## 
May 2 & 3, 2025
100 Years of Arabic Music: Lebanon as a Model 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), in collaboration with the Arab Academy of Music, proudly presented “100 Years of Arabic Music: Lebanon as a Model,” a scientific conference held on May 2 and 3, 2025, in Auditorium A. The event celebrated a century of Arabic musical heritage and highlighted Lebanon’s influential role in shaping its evolution.  
  
Renowned scholars, historians, composers, and musicologists from across the Arab world—including Lebanon, Jordan, Tunisia, and Egypt—gathered to explore Arabic music’s legacy, its development over the decades, and its continued impact on global culture.  
  
The 2-day event offered an enlightening exploration of Arabic music’s past, present, and future, and was followed by captivating performances at the John Paul II Amphitheater by Gilbert Rahbani on May 2 and Dr. Ghada Chbeir on May 3.

## 
October 15, 2025
Inauguration Day: Presidential Investiture of Fr. Prof. Joseph Moukarzel 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
There are moments in the life of a university that embody both legacy and promise, moments when the past and the future converge in a shared spirit of service. With each new presidency, the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik renews its mission to lead with purpose, building bridges between heritage and innovation, between faith and knowledge, between Lebanon and the world.   
  
In this spirit, the University will hold its first-ever Inauguration Day marking the investiture of Fr. Prof. Joseph Moukarzel as the seventeenth President of USEK.   
  
The event will take place on Wednesday, October 15, 2025, at 7:00 p.m., in the John Paul II Amphitheater.

## 
April 15 & 18, 2024
HPV Vaccination Conference and Campaign 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) hosted an HPV Vaccination Conference and Campaign, organized by the School of Medicine and Medical Sciences, on Monday, April 15, 2024, at 12:00 p.m. at the Kaslik Campus, in Jean El Hawa Auditorium, and on Thursday, April 18, 2024, at 12:300 p.m. at the Dr. François S. Bassil Medical Building, Jbeil in Alex & Pierre Jalkh Auditorium.   
  
**Who is eligible?**   
Students, siblings, and personnel children aged 10 to 25 years (females and males).   
  
**What about the price?**   
Shots will be priced at 140 USD (instead of 200 USD) for each shot   
  
**How many shots does it take to be effective?**   
Under 14 ½ years of age: 2 shots   
Above 14 ½ years of age: 3 shots   
  
**The Speakers**   
Dr. Marie-Claude Fadous Khalife - Head of Pediatric department UHNDS, Vaccinology specialist   
Dr. Habib Barakat, Head of Gynecology Obstetric department UHNDS   
Dr. Marcel Massoud, Head of Oncology & Hematology department UHNDS

## 
October 22, 2025
Lecture: The European Union and its Role in Lebanon 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) is organizing a lecture on “the European Union and its Role in Lebanon”, featuring Ms. Alessandra Viezzer, Head of Cooperation at the EU Delegation in Lebanon.   
  
Hosted by the School of Law and Political Sciences (SLPS), this event will take place on Wednesday, October 22, 2025, at 10:30 a.m., in the Fr. Étienne Sacre Auditorium.   
  
In keeping with a series of similar lectures delivered by guest speakers from the EU Delegation in Lebanon, Ms. Viezzer will be exploring with our students EU diplomacy and mediation with neighboring countries, such as Lebanon, and avenues for collaboration under the SLPS’s course “EU: Origins and Evolution”, in addition to internship opportunities within the various departments of the delegation.

## 
From July 25 to 28, 2022
Lebanon Unsettled workshops 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK), in collaboration with the London School of Economics (LSE), organized a four-day in-person workshop: “Lebanon Unsettled” to examine the 2019 protests and their implications with Lebanon’s young generation and to “archive” this historical moment. The workshop provided an overview of the protest movement by leading scholars with a specific focus on the intersection between urban space and revolt. No prior knowledge of spatial methods and/or theories were needed.  
  
This event was hosted at USEK Campus from July 25 to 28, 2022, and a concluding roundtable was held in Beirut on Friday, July 29, 2022, with all participants (optional attendance).

## 
From July 1 to 12, 2024
USEK’s AI Summer Camp 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized an AI Summer Camp, titled: “High on AI: Aiming High with AI”.   
  
This event, hosted by the Faculty of Arts of Sciences, took place from July 1 to 12, 2024 at the USEK Campus.   
  
This two-week summer camp was designed for high school students in grades 10 and 11 who have a passion for technology and curiosity about Artificial Intelligence. Participants had the opportunity to engage in interactive workshops where they can create their own AI projects, learning from university professors and AI professionals. This was a unique opportunity for young minds to dive into the world of AI and gain valuable insights that can shape their future careers.

## 
September 25, 2025
Diplomacy Across Oceans - 80 Years of Lebanon-Latin America 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) was pleased to announce a special conference and exhibition, titled “Diplomacy Across Oceans – 80 Years of Lebanon-Latin America”, which explored the rich history of Lebanese emigration to Latin America during the 19th and 20th centuries.  
  
Hosted by the Latin American Studies and Culture Center in collaboration with the International Affairs Office, this event was held on Thursday, September 25, 2025, at 4:00 p.m., at the USEK Library. It showcased rare archives, photographs, newspapers, and publications documenting the presence and impact of Lebanese communities across Brazil, Argentina, Chile, and Mexico. These materials, part of USEK’s Latin American Collection, were available both digitally and in print, serving as a valuable resource for researchers and scholars in the fields of migration, diaspora, and cultural studies.  
  
A highlight of the conference was the commemoration of President Camille Chamoun’s 1954 diplomatic visit to Latin America, marked through archival materials and the participation of the ambassadors of Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, and Uruguay.  
  
The exhibition was open to the public from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.   
  
To explore the collection featured in this event, visit:   
<https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/latin-american-collection>

October 3, 2025
Pitch Perfect: UBS Hackathon 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized the “Pitch Perfect” hackathon, which took place on Friday, October 3, 2025, from 10:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m., at Building D, 4th Floor (D400).  
  
Hosted by the USEK Business School, the hackathon provided students with a dynamic platform to collaborate in teams, analyze case studies, and sharpen their skills in problem-solving, storytelling, and visual communication. The day culminated with each team presenting their pitch before a jury panel of business experts, where the top three teams were awarded valuable prizes.

## 
October 20 – November 21
Preparatory Session for the Controllers and Auditors 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The School of Law and Political Sciences at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) is organizing a Preparatory Session for the Controllers and Auditors Entrance Exam at the Court of Accounts.   
  
Led by experts in the field, this comprehensive session is tailored for recent graduates and students in law, business, or related fields. Participants will gain practical insights, targeted strategies, and essential knowledge to prepare effectively for the entrance exam.   
  
**Why enroll in this preparatory session?**
  * Understand the exam’s structure, its format, and key components 
  * Gain knowledge in public accounting and control 
  * Benefit from expert guidance and strategic preparation for exam success 

  
  
**Session Details**   
Date: October 20 – November 21   
Location: Court Room (Building B – GF)   
  
**Fees**
  * USEK active students: 200$ 
  * USEK alumni: 250$ 
  * External participants: 300$ 

  
**  
Registration and Payment**  
1. Go to the APPLY platform (apply.usek.edu.lb).   
2. Navigate to the Academic Applications section (apply.usek.edu.lb/academic-applications).   
3. Under the Law and Political Sciences section, locate the Controllers and Auditors Preparatory Session registration card and click on Apply Now.   
4. Log in using one of the following:   
- MS Office 365 account   
- Gmail account   
- USEK account (ID and Password)

## 
November 9, 2024
UCARE 2024 Medical Conference 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
U-CARE (Urology Cancer Academy for Research and Education) is an annual congress organized by the Urology Department at Notre Dame des Secours University Hospital, where this year’s edition took place on Saturday, November 9, 2024.  
  
Bringing together a multidisciplinary audience of urologists, oncologists, radiologists, pathologists, surgeons, nurses, fellows, and healthcare professionals involved in urology and oncology cancer care, this edition holds special significance, as it embodies the resilience of the medical community in light of Lebanon’s current challenges. Offering a hybrid format with both in-person attendance and virtual participation, this oncology and urology conference will address the latest updates in the field of prostate, renal, and bladder cancers, with emphasis on hormonal and immunotherapy approaches as well as practical functional urology.  
  
Distinguished local and international speakers will animate the discussions and present the advances in these fields, further emphasizing a multidisciplinary approach.

## 
From July 8 to 19, 2024 
USEK's Creative Writing Summer Camp 
[](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/news-and-media/news)
The Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) organized a Creative Writing Summer Camp, titled: “Unleash Your Creative Superpowers”.
  
This event, hosted by the Faculty of Arts and Sciences, took place from July 8 to 19, 2024 at the USEK Campus.   
  
This summer camp was dedicated to high school students in grades 10 and 11, who are passionate about the world of comic book storytelling and creative writing, giving them the opportunity to enhance their skills in character development, plot structure, dialogue writing and visual storytelling. The participants got the chance to unleash their creativity and strengthen their knowledge through workshops, expert mentorship and collaborative exercises.
