##  Testimonials 
**Georges Sarkis**  
_Bachelor's degree in Economic and Financial Analysis_  
  
I recently had the opportunity to take courses in Budgeting & Cost Control and Digital Marketing at USEK's Learning Center. The experience was outstanding and far exceeded my expectations. The Budgeting & Cost Control course offered in-depth insights into financial management, equipping me with essential skills to effectively plan and manage budgets. The real-life case studies and practical exercises were particularly beneficial, allowing me to apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios. The Digital Marketing course was equally impressive. It covered a wide range of modern marketing strategies and tools, providing me with a thorough understanding of current digital marketing trends. The hands-on projects and interactive sessions significantly enhanced my practical knowledge and expertise in the field. Overall, the faculty's expertise, the well-structured curriculum, and the supportive learning environment at USEK's Learning Center made this learning experience highly rewarding. I would wholeheartedly recommend these courses to anyone looking to advance their professional skills and knowledge.  
  
**  
Mariateresa Di Vietri**  
_Master’s degree in foreign Languages for International Cooperation_  
  
"Summer School at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik: An Unforgettable Experience"  
In the summer of 2019, I was fortunate to receive a scholarship from the University “L’Orientale” of Naples to attend the Summer School at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik. This two-week program was one of the best experiences of my life. I participated in language and cultural courses, including traditional dance lessons and oenology workshops. I had the opportunity to meet incredible people from Lebanon, as well as other international students from Brazil and the Netherlands. The staff at USEK organized cultural tours to cities like Beirut, Byblos, Baalbek, and Batroun, allowing me to explore Lebanon's rich history and heritage. I learned so much from this experience, and I am deeply grateful for the warm hospitality and care provided by the university. I highly recommend this program to all international students who want to experience Lebanon in a meaningful and immersive way.  
  
**Rana Ayoub**  
_Bachelor’s degree in Nutrition and Dietetics, American University of Madaba_  
  
"A Life-Changing Experience at USEK’s Summer School"  
In the summer of 2019, I participated in the Summer School at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, and it was, without a doubt, one of the best experiences of my life. The program was extremely well-organized, and the highlight was meeting new people from various cultures. I not only attended enriching cultural courses, but I also had the chance to meet with professors from the university to discuss my academic interests and ask questions related to my field of study. This interaction was incredibly valuable for my personal and professional growth. I wholeheartedly recommend this program to all students seeking a transformative experience, and I would not hesitate to participate again in the future.  
  
**Raya Yaqoub**  
_Student from the Netherlands_  
  
"A Dream Summer in Lebanon"  
Lebanon has always been one of my favorite countries, and when I found out about the Summer School at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, I knew it was the perfect opportunity. I had an amazing time meeting wonderful people and experiencing the beauty of Lebanon’s culture. I’ll always remember the mornings spent enjoying ‘manakeesh’ under the sun, the wine tour that deepened my appreciation for Lebanese winemaking, and the energetic dabke dance lessons. These experiences were unforgettable, and I would do it all over again without hesitation. The program offered a perfect blend of learning, adventure, and connection, and I am so grateful for the memories made.  
  
**Rawan Ayoub**  
_Bachelor’s degree, German Jordanian University_  
  
"A Memorable Cultural Journey at USEK"  
As a Lebanese student living abroad, I was eager to reconnect with my roots and deepen my understanding of Lebanese culture. The Summer School at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik provided me with that opportunity in 2019. It was an exceptional experience where I met amazing people from Brazil, the Netherlands, Italy, and beyond. Although Arabic is my native language, I opted to focus on cultural courses, including Lebanese traditional dance and oenology, which I thoroughly enjoyed. One of the highlights was visiting the Asher Center for Innovation and Entrepreneurship, an experience that inspired me greatly. The university also organized tours to some of Lebanon's most important cities, enriching my understanding of the country’s rich heritage. This program has been one of the most rewarding experiences of my life, and I encourage every international student to take part in it.  
  
**_Dalal Abbas_** _  
Beauty Specialist_  
  
My experience at USEK's Learning Center was both essential and incredibly fruitful. I have had the privilege of taking the Dermal Sciences Course with Dr. Lea Saab, whose expertise and teaching style made the journey truly enriching. This course provided me with valuable insights and practical tips for skincare, empowering me to achieve greater independence in my own workplace.  
For anyone passionate about skincare and seeking to elevate their knowledge and skills, I highly recommend this course and the exceptional learning opportunities at USEK's Learning Center!  
  
**Toni Touma**  
_Electrics and Electronics at Eddeh Technical School_  
  
I applied to the Jewelry Design and Fabrication course at UCLC, and it turned out to be an incredibly enjoyable and enriching experience. Every class was thoughtfully designed, combining creativity with practical skills that helped me deepen my appreciation for the art of jewelry-making. The course not only exceeded my expectations but also fueled my passion for this craft. I sincerely hope UCLC considers offering a level 2 for this course. I would eagerly participate and highly recommend it to anyone who loves jewelry and wants to explore their creative potential.  
  
**Nourchane Hamouchy**  
_Event Planner_  
  
I had the privilege of taking an Event Management course at USEK University during the pandemic, which was offered online due to COVID-19 restrictions. Despite the virtual format, the course exceeded my expectations and provided me with invaluable knowledge and practical skills in event planning and management. After completing the course, I felt confident enough to launch my own business, Nourchane Events. The insights and expertise I gained played a significant role in turning my passion into a thriving venture. I highly recommend USEK’s courses to anyone looking to expand their skill set and take their career aspirations to the next level. The experience was truly transformative for me!  
  
**Fatima Morsel**  
_Skin Therapist – Owner of Nefertiti Clinic_  
  
I want to express my heartfelt gratitude for the Dermal Sciences and Skin and the Sun courses, which have significantly enriched my field of work. The content was packed with valuable information, delivered in a practical and engaging manner. What truly stood out was the exceptional support and professionalism of the team, making the entire learning experience both enjoyable and rewarding. Thank you for offering such an enriching opportunity—I highly recommend these courses to anyone looking to enhance their skills and knowledge!

##  USEK Diplomacy Academy 
### About the Academy
At USEK, we recognize the crucial role diplomacy plays in shaping international relations and promoting peace, particularly in regions as complex as the Middle East. With a deep commitment to advancing diplomatic excellence, USEK has established the Diplomacy Academy, a dynamic hub for advanced training, strategic dialogue, and knowledge exchange.  
  
The USEK Diplomacy Academy offers certification programs, preparatory sessions for various diplomatic and international affairs exams, and specialized training courses designed to equip participants with essential expertise. These interactive sessions will be conducted by specialized experts in international affairs and diplomacy, also featuring guest lecturers who will address current global trends and other relevant issues that can enrich the learning experience.   
  

### Mission
In alignment with USEK’s educational mission and its commitment to academic excellence, USEK Diplomacy Academy aims to shape future diplomats and international affairs professionals through training in diplomacy, geopolitics, and global governance. By providing an interdisciplinary education, the Academy aims to equip its students with the knowledge and skills necessary for leadership in international diplomacy, conflict resolution, and strategic policymaking.  
  

### Vision
The USEK Diplomacy Academy seeks to be a leading center for diplomatic education and training in Lebanon and the region, recognized for its academic excellence and commitment to shaping the next generation of diplomats.

##  President 
[Back](https://www.usek.edu.lb/en/about-usek/governance)
###  ![](https://www.usek.edu.lb/Content/Images/Uploaded%20Images/20250906JosephMoukarzel.jpg)FATHER JOSEPH MOUKARZEL, PRESIDENT OF THE HOLY SPIRIT UNIVERSITY OF KASLIK (USEK)
Dear USEK Community,  
It is with deep gratitude and a profound sense of responsibility that I begin this new chapter as President of the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik. Rooted in the spiritual heritage of the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM) and animated by its Catholic identity and Lebanese values, USEK has long stood as a beacon of academic excellence, human dignity, and service to the common good. These guiding principles are more vital than ever as we face the challenges of our time — together.  
  
To our students,  
You are the heart of this University. Everything we do begins with you in mind. As you move forward in your journey, know that you are not alone; you are surrounded by a community who believes in you, nurtures your talents, and is committed to helping you grow into leaders who act with integrity, compassion, and vision — here in Lebanon and far beyond.  
  
To our faculty and staff,  
You are the soul of USEK. Your dedication, excellence, and quiet strength are the foundation of all that we achieve. I look forward to working with you to continue fostering a culture of research, creativity, collaboration, and inclusion — always anchored in the values that define us as a Catholic university and as a Lebanese institution of distinction.  
  
To our alumni,  
You carry the spirit of USEK into every corner of the world. You are our pride, our voice, and our living legacy. We count on your continued engagement as we strive to form the next generation — one that is grounded in the same values you once embraced at USEK.  
  
To our partners and friends,  
Your trust and support have played an essential role in USEK’s journey. As we move forward, we hope to deepen our collaboration with institutions, organizations, and individuals who share our vision of education as a force for good. Together, let us continue to build bridges — across cultures, disciplines, and generations — and forge partnerships that uplift learners, strengthen communities, and inspire change.  
  
My door and heart remain open to each and every one of you. Let us walk this path forward as one community, united in hope, committed to truth, and faithful to our mission as a Catholic university, guided always by our motto: “When the Spirit of truth comes, He will lead you to the whole truth.”  
  
Father Joseph Moukarzel

### Preventive measures against coronavirus (COVID-19) @ USEK Library
**1.** USEK Library is closed until further notice.  
**2.** Electronic Resources are accessible to all USEK community from off-campus.  
**3.** Document Delivery Service (article requests) is available to all USEK community.  
**4.** All borrowed books have been renewed until 31 May, 2020.  
**5.** For help and other reference services, use the library chat service, or send an email to reference@usek.edu.lb.  
  
⚠️ Online research consultation (Refworks, APA, etc.): meet with our reference librarian online via Microsoft Teams or Skype. Please book your appointment at least 24 hours in advance by contacting us on: reference@usek.edu.lb. ⚠️

#### Are you facing issues when trying to login to eLearning (or other USEK services)?
##### It's time to change your USEK Email password:
  * Open **Google Chrome** browser and go to <https://outlook.office365.com>
    * If you're using your mobile, you need to select "**Request Desktop Site** " browser option (by clicking on the three dots ..., bottom right). This may NOT work on Safari.
  * **Login** with your USEK Email and password.
  * Click on your name initials (_top right_) and go to "**View Account** "
  * Click on "**Change Password** " and follow the on-screen instructions 
    * Select a strong password: **10-12 characters** as a combination of _lowercase and uppercase letters, numbers, and symbols_ (at least one).
  * Well done.

#  Administrative Coordinator - ADMIEP202610 
Holy Spirit University of Kaslik · 3 weeks ago 
[ Apply Now ](https://jobs.usek.edu.lb/login?redirect-to=/usek-job-application/new?job_title=administrative-coordinator-admiep202610)
Department
Office of the Vice President for Institutional Effectiveness and Planning - USEK
Applications Received
174
### JOB SUMMARY
The **Administrative Coordinator** supports the **Office of the Vice President for Institutional Effectiveness and Planning** by managing daily operations, preparing reports and presentations, and organizing institutional policies and procedures.
They work closely with the VP and Assistant VP to ensure smooth coordination across **planning** , **accreditation** , and **institutional effectiveness** initiatives.
  

### RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS
  1. **Administrative and Logistical Support**
  2. Manages scheduling, agendas, and logistics for meetings, workshops, and events led by the OVP-IEP.
  3. Prepares presentations, reports, briefing materials, and meeting minutes.
  4. Supports the follow-up and tracking of office initiatives, deadlines, and deliverables.
  5. **Policy and Documentation Management**
  6. Collects, organizes, and maintains a repository of institutional policies, procedures, and related documents.
  7. Ensures systematic version control, archival, and accessibility of records.
  8. **Support for Reporting and Communication**
  9. Assists in preparing summary tables, visuals, and reports for leadership review.
  10. Provides support in developing presentations and institutional updates.
  11. Contributes to internal communications and outreach activities coordinated by the OVP-IEP.


  

### ﻿KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS
  

### EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND EXPERIENCE
  

Candidates must meet all employment requirements, including – but not limited to – education and certification requirements, reference checks, and criminal background checks.
  

Additional Details about this position will only be provided to Shortlisted Candidates.

Office of the Vice President for Institutional Effectiveness and Planning - USEK
Applications Received
9
### JOB SUMMARY
The **Director of Institutional Research and Data Analytics** leads efforts to use data and research to enhance **decision-making** and **institutional effectiveness**.
They provide insights supporting **academic excellence** , **student success** , and **strategic planning** , while overseeing **data systems** , **dashboards** , and **evaluation frameworks** , and promoting a **culture of evidence-based decision-making** across the university.
  

### RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS
  1. **Institutional Research Leadership**
  2. Directs the design and administration of institutional surveys, evaluation studies, and research projects.
  3. Generates actionable insights to monitor academic and administrative performance.
  4. Ensures research activities align with institutional priorities, accreditation requirements, and strategic initiatives.
  5. **Analytics and Decision Support**
  6. Provides advanced analytics, benchmarking, and predictive modeling to guide leadership decisions.
  7. Translates complex data into meaningful insights to support institutional strategy, resource allocation, and student success initiatives.
  8. Presents findings in clear and actionable formats for executive leadership and key stakeholders.
  9. **Dashboard and Data Infrastructure Management**
  10. Oversees the creation, maintenance, and governance of institutional dashboards, KPIs, and data visualization tools (such as Microsoft Power BI).
  11. Ensures that data reporting is timely, accurate, and aligned with institutional goals.
  12. **Data Integration and Quality Assurance**
  13. Manage ETL/ELT processes to extract, clean, and integrate data from core systems (SIS, LMS, HR, Finance).
  14. Maintains data integrity, security, and reliability within a unified institutional data environment.
  15. **Goal Tracking and Performance Monitoring**
  16. Develops systems to monitor progress on institutional goals, strategic initiatives, and accreditation standards.
  17. Provides regular reports and dashboards to leadership to support continuous improvement and accountability.
  18. **Collaboration and Capacity Building**
  19. Partners with academic and administrative units to enhance data literacy and research capacity.
  20. Supports evidence-based decision-making across the University through training, consultation, and collaboration.
  21. Promotes a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.

Admissions - USEK

### JOB SUMMARY
The Director of the Admissions Office is responsible for strategic enrollment management, including team management and initiatives related to the planning and implementation of current strategies and goals. The incumbent must align recruitment and admissions activities with the University’s strategic plan, mission, vision, and goals. In addition, they must work independently and be able to proactively lead the Admissions Office to achieve enrollment growth in a challenging demographic and competitive landscape.
  

### RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS
  1. **Recruitment and Enrollment Planning and Program Development**
  2. Designs, implements, and evaluates a comprehensive, data-driven strategic recruitment plan.
  3. Plans and supervises recruitment and application processing operations, including – but not limited to – lead generation, marketing/target analysis, prospect-enrollment pipeline development, application review and follow-up, high school/college outreach, on and off-campus recruitment events, and open-door events.
  4. Develops and manages a comprehensive recruitment plan and strategy that is designed to meet annual recruitment goals in collaboration with the Vice President for Enrollment Management; develops annual comprehensive recruitment strategies in cooperation with both administrative/academic units and the USEK administration to ensure optimal enrollment while maintaining and/or improving the University’s academic standing.
  5. Oversees the yearly assessment, revision, and implementation of admission policies through a holistic process that involves administration and faculty.
  6. **Administration,Data Gathering, Analysis, and Decision Support**
  7. Works with external offices to provide and collect data for planning and assessment.
  8. Works collaboratively with the Marketing and Communications Office to design effective print, email, text, and social media platforms for student recruitment.
  9. Works collaboratively with the Alumni Relations Office to implement effective recruitment strategies using alumni ambassadors.
  10. Researches and applies best practices and rapidly changing technology appropriately to further the University’s enrollment and recruitment goals.
  11. **Recruitment and Admissions Team Leadership and Management**
  12. Leads the Admissions Office, both in terms of strategic direction and complex daily operations using exceptional leadership and supervisory skills. This includes admissions and office policy development and implementation, professional development, and supervision to develop and support a strong admissions staff that is recruitment-centric, optimistic, empowered, responsive, innovative, results-oriented, and student-centered.
  13. Makesdata-informed enrollment projections by routinely running team meetings to shape strategic directions and make appropriate adjustments to an integrated marketing plan that identifies and defines historical University enrollment patterns and forecasts trends in new-student markets.
  14. Reassesses the effectiveness of recruitment activities and makes appropriate adjustments to continuously refine the team’s goals and strategies.


  

### KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS
  1. Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
  2. Outstanding interpersonal skills and ability to communicate and work effectively within a diverse community.
  3. Excellent computer skills and ability to operate software.
  4. Excellent management and leadership skills (technical, conceptual, and interpersonal skills).
  5. Excellent managerial skills (planning and administration, motivation, strategic action, multicultural competencies, among others).
  6. Analytical and problem-solving skills.
  7. Time management skills.
  8. Planning and forecasting.
  9. Creativity and innovation.
  10. High emotional intelligence.


  

### EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND EXPERIENCE
  1. Master’s degree in business or any related field.


  

Candidates must meet all employment requirements including, but not limited to, Education and Certification Requirements, Teaching Experience, Reference Checks and Criminal Background Checks.

The **Senior Coordinator for Integrated Planning** supports the **Office of the Vice President for Institutional Effectiveness and Planning** by coordinating the implementation of USEK’s institutional strategies across areas like strategy, finance, enrollment, technology, and academics.
They ensure unit plans align with institutional priorities, track progress, and use data and trends to guide planning.
The role also involves contributing to **risk assessment** , **continuous improvement** , and supporting **data-informed decision-making** for effective monitoring of strategic initiatives.

  1. **Planning Coordination and Strategic Support**

  3. Supports the maintenance of a centralized planning calendar, templates, and documentation to standardize planning processes.
  4. Facilitates communication and collaboration across academic and administrative units to support integrated planning efforts.
  5. **Monitoring, Evaluation, and Continuous Improvement**
  6. Assists in collecting and analyzing data related to strategic plan implementation and institutional performance.
  7. Supports evaluation processes to assess whether institutional strategies are achieving intended outcomes.
  8. Prepares reports and summaries for leadership on progress toward strategic goals and key initiatives.
  9. **Risk Monitoring Support**
  10. Assists in integrating risk considerations into institutional planning, including scenario planning and contingency preparation.
  11. Helps track key risk indicators (KRIs) and prepare summaries for leadership to support proactive decision-making.
  12. **Collaboration and Capacity Building**
  13. Works with stakeholders across the University to support planning initiatives and promote a culture of shared responsibility for outcomes.
  14. Assists in delivering training or guidance to units on planning processes, implementation tracking, and use of planning tools.


### EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND EXPERIENCE

##  Introduction 
**What is American Psychological Association (APA) style?**
  * **type/format of a source** (e.g. an article with two authors, a book with no date or an article with DOI etc.).


**What are in-text citations and references?**
Giving credit to a source is a must to avoid plagiarism. In APA style, there are **two ways to credit sources:**
  * **In-text citation:** In the body of a paper when a source is quoted, paraphrased, or summarized.
  * **References:** In an alphabetical order at the end of a paper.


In-text citation and references provide information about a source such as author and publication year that help a reader locate the source in its original form. 
##  APA 6th Edition Citation Style Manuals @ USEK Library 
  * [ ![Cover Art](https://syndetics.com/index.aspx?isbn=9781433805615/LC.GIF&client=holyspirituniv) Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association  by  American Psychological Association Staff  ](http://sierra.usek.edu.lb/record=b1197850) _The Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association is the style manual of choice for writers, editors, students, and educators in the social and behavioural sciences. It provides invaluable guidance on all aspects of the writing process, from the ethics of authorship to the word choice that best reduces bias in language. Well-known for its authoritative and easy-to-use reference and citation system, the Publication Manual also offers guidance on choosing the headings, tables, figures and tone that will result in strong, simple, and elegant scientific communication. The Sixth Edition offers new and expanded instruction on publication ethics, statistics, journal article reporting standards, electronic reference formats, and the construction of tables and figures. The Sixth Edition has been revised and updated to include new ethics guidance on such topics as determining authorship and terms of collaboration, duplicate publication, plagiarism and self-plagiarism, disguising of participants, validity of instrumentation, and making data available to others for verification; new journal article reporting standards to help readers report empirical research with clarity and precision; simplified APA heading style to make it more conducive to electronic publication; updated guidelines for reducing bias in language to reflect current practices and preferences, including a new section on presenting historical language that is inappropriate by present standards; new guidelines for reporting inferential statistics and a significantly revised table of statistical abbreviations new instruction on using supplemental files containing lengthy data sets and other media; significantly expanded content on the electronic presentation of data to help readers understand the purpose of each kind of display and choose the best match for communicating the results of the investigation, with new examples for a variety of data displays, including electrophysiological and biological data; consolidated information on all aspects of reference citations, with an expanded discussion of electronic sources emphasising the role of the digital object identifier (DOI) as a reliable way to locate information; and expanded discussion of the publication process, including the function and process of peer review; a discussion of ethical, legal, and policy requirements in publication; and guidelines on working with the publisher while the article is in press. Key to this edition of the Publication Manual is an updated and expanded Web presence. Visit the APA Style web site to Look up additional supplemental material keyed to the book Test your knowledge of APA Style with a free tutorial on style basics Learn about the changes in the sixth edition with a free tutorial reviewing key revisions Sign up for an on-line course to enrich and enhance your understanding of APA Style Read the APA Style blog and share your comments on writing and referencing Consult frequently asked questions to sharpen your understanding of APA Style Examine additional resources on such topics as ethics, statistics, and writing Familiarise yourself with submission standards for APA books and journals What''s New in the Sixth Edition? Book has been updated to acknowledge and incorporate advances in computer technology. New discussions of the creation, submission, and storage of supplemental data. New guidelines for referencing electronic sources. New and expanded reference examples for a variety of on-line sources. Redesigned APA Style website, expanded to provide tutorials, on-line courses, and other resources for learning APA style. Book has been reorganised and streamlined for ease of use Organised to describe the writing process from idea to publication, it begins with background information on ethical issues in publishing, then moves on to manuscript structure and content, then writing style and rules, then graphics and references, then guidance on working with the publisher. Sample paper section has been moved up and featured to better exemplify manuscript structure and content Like discussions have been moved to one place in the book, with discussions of function followed by instruction on form. Focus has been broadened to include readers in the behavioural and social sciences. Information specific to APA has been moved to the web, where it is more broadly accessible and can be updated frequently. New examples throughout the book have been drawn from publications in education, business, and nursing as well as psychology._

  * [ ![Cover Art](https://syndetics.com/index.aspx?isbn=9781433805608/LC.GIF&client=holyspirituniv) Concise Rules of APA Style  by  American Psychological Association Staff  ](http://sierra.usek.edu.lb/record=b1197847) _The Concise Rules of APA Style, Sixth Edition offers essential writing and formatting standards for students, teachers, researchers, and clinicians in the social and behavioural sciences. This easy-to-use pocket guide, compiled from the sixth edition of the Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association, provides complete guidance on the rules of style that are critical for clear communication. Readers will learn how to avoid the grammatical errors most commonly reported by journal editors; how to choose the appropriate format for statistics, figures, and tables; how to credit sources and avoid charges of plagiarism; and how to construct a reference list through a wide variety of examples and sources. In addition to guidance on grammar points that have challenged writers in the social sciences, the Concise Rules provides suggestions for reducing bias in language; reviews the mechanics of style for punctuation, spelling, capitalisation, abbreviation, italicisation, headings and quotations; examines the preferred use of numbers as well as standards for metrication and statistics; provides guidance on the construction and formatting of tables, figures and appendixes; and offers clear examples and models for citing sources and constructing error-free reference lists. Available in a light-weight, spiral-bound format, the Concise Rules will travel easily from home to school to office. It will be an invaluable reference tool for all social science scholars who are serious about communicating clearly and effectively. Key to this edition is an updated and expanded APA Style website, with many additional resources to help readers learn APA style, including free tutorials, on-line courses, frequently asked questions, sample papers, and the APA Style blog. The sixth edition of Concise Rules has been revised and updated to include simplified APA heading style to make it more conducive to electronic publication; updated guidelines for reducing bias in language to reflect current practices and preferences, including a new section on presenting historical language that is inappropriate by present standards; new guidelines for reporting inferential statistics and a significantly revised table of statistical abbreviations; a new discussion on the use of online supplemental materials, including lengthy data sets and other media, to enrich the published article; significantly expanded content on the electronic presentation of data to help readers understand the purpose of each kind of display and choose the best match for communicating the results of the investigation, with new examples for a variety of data displays, including electrophysiological and biological data; an expanded discussion of electronic sources, emphasizing the role of the digital object identifier (DOI) as a reliable way to locate information; and a wealth of new reference examples, with a focus on new electronic formats. New and experienced readers alike will find the sixth edition a complete resource for writing with clarity and precision.How does the Concise Rules differ from the Publication Manual of the American Psychological Association? The Publication Manual remains the best source for broad background information about scientific publishing. In addition to writing style rules, it provides detailed guidance on publication ethics, journal article reporting standards, and the process of journal publication. The Concise Rules, by comparison, targets only those rules writers need for choosing the best words and format for their articles. It offers a comprehensive list of essential writing standards in a convenient, easily retrievable format._

### JOB SUMMARY
A Senior Graphic Designer is responsible for creating strong visual concepts, visual communications, while conveying the messages in ways that are effective and aesthetically pleasing.
  

### RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS
  1. **Analyze Design****Requirements****:**
  2. Carefully review design briefs and comprehend the project needs.
  3. Lead the conceptualization of visuals based on these requirements.
  4. **Design Creation & Development**:
  5. Craft initial design drafts and present ideas for review and feedback.
  6. Produce advanced illustrations, logos, and various designs, either digitally or by hand.
  7. Select appropriate colors, layouts, and compositions for each project.
  8. **Collaboration & Finalization:**
  9. Work closely with copywriters and the designers to refine and finalize designs.
  10. Test design performance across different mediums.
  11. Adjust designs based on feedback.
  12. Ensure all completed designs are visually compelling and align with brand guidelines.


  

### KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS
  1. Excellent design software skills (Adobe Creative Suite)
  2. In-depth understanding of both print and digital design requirements.
  3. Expertise in typography and visual composition.
  4. Keen awareness of current design trends and their application in a commercial context.
  5. Exceptional creative and innovative design skills.
  6. Acute attention to detail and aesthetics.
  7. Proficient in managing time and meeting deadlines.
  8. Flexible and adaptable to changing project scopes and teams.
  9. Strong multitasking ability.
  10. Excellent team collaboration skills, with experience working as part of a design team.
  11. Superior communication skills for effective client interactions and understanding project needs.
  12. Effective negotiation and interpersonal skills


  

### EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND EXPERIENCE
  1. BA degree in graphic design.
  2. 5 years of experience in a similar field.

##  How to place digital signature in your PDF Document 
1. Open your PDF file.
2. Click on **Fill & Sign** in the Tools pane on the right, then choose **Place Signature.**
![alt="fill & sign option"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/fill.png)
3. A popup will open giving you several options; click **Use a certificate** and**click Next**
**N. B.:** If you already have scanned your original signature, you can select **“Use an image”** , browse the scanned copy and place it in the area where you would like your signature to appear.
![alt="Use certificate option in place signature tab within fill and sign in PDF"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/Place_signature_pop_up.png)
4. A new message appears; click on **Drag New Signature Rectangle** , and then drag out the area where you would like your signature to appear. 
![alt"drag new signature rectangle message"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/Drag_new_signature_rectangle.png)
5. A popup will open; choose **A new digital ID I want to create now** then click **Next.**
**![alt="Create new digtial ID option"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/add_digital_ID.png)**
6. You will receive a new message: choose **Windows Certificate Store** and then click **Next.**
**![alt="windows certificate store message"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/windows_certificate_store.png)**
7. A form for identity information, will be opened to be filled out; fill it out and click Finish.
![alt="Identity informaiton form"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/identity_information_form.png)
8. The signature will be created, you can review it, change its standard appearance, and click **Sign** to digitally sign your document.
![alt="Sign document preview"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/sign_document_preview.png)
9. The Digital signature will be placed in the area you dragged out before.
![alt="screenshot on how appears the digital signature"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/test.png)
10. Your digital ID is stored in the Windows Certificate Store, so you can reuse it at any time. Or you can create a new ID as follows:
![alt="Stored signature"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/stored_signature.png)

# Access USEK Library Special Collections and Archives: Home
  * [ Home ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/access-special-collections/home)
  * [ How to place your Digital Signature in PDF ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/access-special-collections/digital-signature-pdf)


USEK library Special Collections and Archives units are committed to providing open and equitable access to the Library’s historical records, to numerous digital collections, and to other valuable resources (rare books, manuscripts, newspapers, images etc.)
To protect and preserve USEK Library collections, Special Collections and Archival materials do not circulate, but are stored in our vaults, or available in digital forms. 
### PLAN YOUR VISIT
To access materials from the Special Collections or Archives please download, fill out, digitally sign the below form "**Special Collections and Archives Request"** to**psd@usek.edu.lb****.**
If you are a non-USEK user, please check our [visitors policy.](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/visitors)
  * [ ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/ld.php?content_id=56985073)


Please note that at least 3 business days’ notice is required for processing requests. 
After you submit your request, a staff member will e-mail you to confirm your appointment. Please do not visit the library until you have received this confirmation.
Physical collection access can only be accommodated during the Special Collections Reading Room opening hours:
**Monday-Friday: 8 a.m.-1p.m. & 2p.m.-4 p.m.**
### **RULES FOR USING USEK SPECIAL COLLECTIONS AND ARCHIVES**
1. Divisional staff will determine which materials can be made available for use and when surrogates must be used instead of originals. 
2. Only items necessary for research such as papers, pencils, laptops without cases, are permitted in the Special Collections Reading Room.
3. Cameras and mobile phones are not allowed. 
4. Personal items are subject to examination upon entering and leaving the Special Collections Reading Room.
5. For [reproduction](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/services/reproduction-service) or publishing, the below **Notice of intent to Publish Special Collections & Archival Materials from USEK Library **should be filled and signed for approval**.**
  * [ ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/ld.php?content_id=75795257)


6. Reproduction of Rare Books, manuscripts, newspapers, and archives housed at USEK Library should be accompanied by a credit line. Credit lines for film, television, and video may be run at the end of the program or presentation. 
**Credit Format:** Name or title of the item, Name of collection, Name of Center or Special Collections, USEK Library, Holy Spirit University of Kaslik, Lebanon. 
7. One gratis copy of any publication resulting from extensive research in USEK Library materials should be offered to the Library. 
8. In all cases, the USEK University Library only owns the physical item and therefore does not assume any responsibility for literary property, copyright, or any other legal issues involved in the publication and reproduction of items in its collections. In the case of both textual and visual materials (including photographs and works of art), it is the responsibility of the user to secure permission from the appropriate copyright holder.
### **DIGTIAL SIGNATURE**
### Since USEK is a paperless community, we adopt Digital Signature. Please check the next tab to know how to place your Digital Signature in the PDF Document.

This guide provides access to primary sources and materials available at USEK Library. It serves as a starting point to find resources for searching the life of Kamal S. Salibi, publications about and by him, media, quotes etc..
  * [ Home ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/Kamal-Salibi/home)

**Please note that USEK Library houses the Archives of Kamal S. Salibi.**
##  Biography 
Kamal Salibi was born in Beirut on 2 May 1929 to a protestant family of 5 boys and one girl. The family was originally from Bhamdun, a mountain town on the main road from Beirut to Damascus.
Salibi early education was completed at the famous Quaker School in Brummana (today Brumanna High School) and then at International College. He completed his education at the American University of Beirut, where he obtained a BA in history in 1949.
In 1950, Salibi traveled to London to pursue a PHD in Middle Eastern History at the University of London. After London, he returned to Beirut and joined AUB as bibliographer of the Arab Studies Program and then he was hired as professor in the Department of History and Archaeology.
In the early 1990s, Salibi decamped to Amman, where he had another carrier as director of the Royal Institute of Inter-Faith Studies. The last ten years of his life were spent in Lebanon. 
Salibi was a lifetime bachelor, who devoted his life to books.
He died in Beirut on 1 September 2011.

##  Biography 
Born in 1919, Camille Aboussouan was a humanist writer, diplomat, lawyer, journalist, editorialist, and founding director of _Les Cahiers de l’Est_ (1945). He also founded Lebanon’s Pen Club (1948) and was the secretary general of the Lebanese National Commission for UNESCO (1953-1972) and the curator of the Nicolas Sursock Museum (1957-1978).
In addition to his membership of several cultural associations in Lebanon and in France, Aboussouan served as Lebanon’s permanent delegate to the UNESCO between 1983 and 1987. 
Camille Aboussouan né en 1919, diplomate, écrivain humaniste, avocat, journaliste, éditorialiste, créateur et directeur de la revue Les cahiers de l’Est (1945), fondateur de Pen Club du Liban (1948), secrétaire général de la commission nationale libanaise pour l’Unesco (1953-1972), conservateur du Musée Nicolas Sursock (1957-1978). Ambassadeur délégué permanent du Liban auprès de l’Unesco (1983-1987), membre de nombreuses associations culturelles au Liban et en France.

##  Biography 
مؤرّخ وأستاذ جامعيّ وُلِدَ في النوبة بفلسطين. التحق أبو حسين بالجامعة الأميركيّة في بيروت منذ العام 1971 كطالب واستمرّ في التدريس بعد ذلك منذ العام 1982، حين نال درجة الدكتوراه من الجامعة نفسها بعد أن درس على يد الأستاذ الراحل كمال صليبي وكان أحد طلّابه اللامعين. عمل على تاريخ لبنان وتركّزت خبرته على التاريخ السياسيّ والاجتماعيّ لسوريا العثمانيّة، مع التشديد بشكل خاصّ على تاريخ المناطق التي أصبحت تشكّل دولة لبنان الحديث.
كذلك، كان أبو حسين أستاذًا زائرًا في عدد من الجامعات الأميركيّة والعربيّة، وهو مرجع عالميّ في التاريخ العثمانيّ. منحته الجمعيّة التاريخيّة التركيّة سنة 2013 العضويّة الفخريّة لمساهماته في حقل الدراسات العثمانيّة.
تعمّق بأرشيف الإمبراطوريّة العثمانيّة وكشف عددًا من المحطّات الأساسيّة في تاريخ لبنان. توفّي في بيروت سنة 2022، وله مؤلّفات وأبحاث عدّة بالإنكليزيّة والعربيّة والتركيّة في التاريخ اللبنانيّ والعربيّ والعثمانيّ.
A historian and university professor born in the Palestinian village of Nuba, Abu Husayn enrolled as a student at the American University of Beirut (AUB) in 1971, also teaching there as of 1982. During that year, he earned his PhD from AUB, as he studied the history of Lebanon as a star student under the supervision of the late [Lebanese historian] Kamal Salibi. His area of focus was the sociopolitical history of Ottoman Syria, with special emphasis on the history of the regions that went on to form the modern state of Lebanon. 
A visiting professor in several U.S. and Arab universities, he is regarded as a world-renowned expert in Ottoman history. The Turkish Historical Society granted him honorary membership in 2013 in recognition of his contributions to the field of Ottoman studies. 
His in-depth study of the Ottoman Empire archives shed light on several key stages in the history of Lebanon. With his death in Beirut in 2022, he leaves behind a wealth of books and research in English, Arabic, and Turkish on Lebanese, Arab, and Ottoman history. 
Historien et professeur d’université originaire du village de Nouba en Palestine, Abu Husayn intègre l’Université américaine de Beyrouth (AUB) en 1971 et y enseigne à partir de 1982. Cette année-là, il obtient son doctorat à l’AUB, où il étudie l’histoire du Liban en tant qu’étudiant vedette sous la supervision du défunt [historien libanais] Kamal Salibi. Son domaine d’intérêt est l’histoire sociopolitique de la Syrie ottomane, avec un accent particulier sur l’histoire des régions qui ont par la suite formé l’État moderne du Liban. 
Professeur invité dans plusieurs universités américaines et arabes, il est considéré comme une sommité mondiale de l’histoire ottomane. La _Turkish Historical Society_ lui a accordé en 2013 le titre de membre honoraire en reconnaissance de ses contributions dans le domaine des études ottomanes. 
Son travail approfondi sur les archives de l’Empire ottoman a permis de mettre en lumière plusieurs étapes clés de l’histoire du Liban. Décédé à Beyrouth en 2022, il laisse derrière lui une multitude de livres et de recherches en anglais, en arabe et en turc portant sur l’histoire libanaise, arabe et ottomane.

**Please note that USEK Library houses the Archives of Abbot Boulos Naaman.**
##  Biography 
Born in Chartoun (district of Aley) in 1932, he studied philosophy and theology at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) between 1951 and 1957. After completing a Baccalaureate in Theology in Rome in 1959, he earned a Doctorate in History from the Pontifical Gregorian University in 1966. In addition to his positions as dean of the Faculty of Letters and director of the Institute of History at USEK between 1972 and 1980, he taught history from 1970 to 2000. 
A former superior general of the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM) between 1980 and 1986, he has authored numerous books, articles, and lectures on Lebanese and Church history, particularly the history of the Maronite Church, in Arabic, French, and English.
وُلِدَ في شرتون – عاليه سنة 1932. درس الفلسفة واللاهوت في جامعة الروح القدس – الكسليك من سنة 1951 إلى سنة 1957. نال إجازة في اللاهوت من روما سنة 1959 ودكتوراه في التاريخ من الجامعة الغريغوريّة في روما سنة 1966. شغل منصب عميد كلّيّة الآداب ومدير معهد التاريخ في جامعة الروح القدس – الكسليك من سنة 1972 إلى سنة 1980، وأستاذ مادّة التاريخ من سنة 1970 إلى سنة 2000.
كذلك، كان رئيسًا عامًّا للرهبانيّة اللبنانيّة المارونيّة من سنة 1980 حتى سنة 1986. له مؤلّفات ومقالات ومحاضرات عدّة في التاريخ اللبنانيّ والكنسيّ، وخاصّة تاريخ الكنيسة المارونيّة، في اللغات العربيّة والفرنسيّة والإنكليزيّة.
Né à Chartoun (district d’Aley) en 1932, il a étudié la philosophie et la théologie à l’Université Saint-Esprit de Kaslik (USEK) entre 1951 et 1957. Après un baccalauréat en théologie à Rome en 1959, il obtient un doctorat en histoire de l’Université Pontificale Grégorienne en 1966. Doyen de la Faculté des Lettres et de directeur de l’Institut d’Histoire de l’USEK entre 1972 et 1980, il a également enseigné l’histoire de 1970 à 2000. 
Ancien supérieur général de l’Ordre Libanais Maronite (OLM) de 1980 à 1986, il est l’auteur de nombreux livres, articles et conférences sur l’histoire du Liban et de l’Église, notamment l’histoire de l’Église maronite, en arabe, français et anglais.

##  Biography 
Albert Hourani was born in Manchester, England, on 31 March 1915, the son of Fadlo and Sumaya Hourani, immigrants from Marjayun -South Lebanon. He attended Magdalen College, Oxford in 1933, where he read philosophy, politics, and economics. He graduated in 1936 and went to the Middle East where he taught politics for two years at the American University of Beirut. With the outbreak of World War II, he joined the Royal Institute of International Affairs where he worked with and came under the influence of Arnold Toynbee and Hamilton Gibb. He served as an analyst at the Office of the British Minister of State resident in Cairo from 1943-1945 and worked as principal researcher and writer at the Arab Office, where he helped with the presentation of the Arab case to the Anglo-American Committee of Inquiry which visited Palestine in 1946. After that, he devoted the rest of his life to an academic career. In 1948, he was offered a fellowship at Magdalen College and, three years later, he took up the post of first University lecturer in the modern history of the Near East and later became director of St. Antony’s College Middle East Centre. He was a frequent visitor to universities in the United States and the Middle East, and he received recognition and numerous awards.
Albert Hourani’s influence as a scholar and a teacher continues to be felt throughout our field. In 1946 he published Syria and Lebanon and in 1947 Minorities in the Arab World. In 1962, he published his classic, Arabic Thought in the Liberal Age 1789-1939, which went through two editions and numerous reprints. In 1991, he capped his remarkable career with the publication of The History of the Arab Peoples, which was instantly recognized for its remarkably rich portrayal of the history and culture of the Arab Peoples. Between 1946 and 1993, he published eight books and edited seven others; he also published over 150 articles and over 100 book reviews. Among his articles, “Ottoman Reform and the Politics of the Notables,” originally published in 1968 and reprinted in 1981, has provided a concept—that of the politics of the “notables”—which has inspired generations of historians to study the society and politics of the modern Middle East from within.
Much of Albert Hourani's work reflected his deep appreciation for the intellectual traditions of the Middle East and the West. He was a remarkably enlightened interpreter of the historical processes which inform social life of different civilizations and had a keen understanding of the ways in which ideas are exchanged and filtered through different cultural prisms and historical experiences. His genius was an integral part of the personal and professional ethic that informed all his work and relationships. More than any other single individual, he established modern Middle East studies on a solid academic basis.
Albert Hourani died in Oxford on 17th January 1993. He lives with us through his scholarly work, through the institutions he helped create, through his students, but above all, through the standards of personal and professional conduct associated with his name. It is, therefore, with tremendous pride and joy that we established an award in Albert Hourani’s name. In doing so we recognize that his name and legacy will continue to expand the frontiers of Middle Eastern studies, that he will continue to enrich the intellectual and historical traditions of the worlds and peoples he loved, and that he will continue to guide and inspire the work of future generations of scholars. They could receive no greater honor, or challenge.
**Reference**

This encyclopedia provides authoritative and up-to-date information about theatre and performance from ancient Greek theatre to the latest developments in London, Paris, New York, and around the globe. In addition to performances in playhouses, it covers dance, opera, radio, film, television, and popular performance, including carnivals, circus, and public executions. Entries range from short definitions of terms to lengthy considerations of genres and movements, such as feminism and psychoanalytic criticism. Entries on cities and regions place performance in its local social and political context. Written in accessible language, this encyclopedia brings together an international cast of over 300 specialist contributors.

#### Search Tips
  * Adding quotes can help narrow the results, especially for multiple word search terms, words with hyphens, or dates   
_"Digital ReLab"_ or _"e-mail"_
  * Make sure the format of the date entered is consistent with the file's metadata   
_"1/1/2016"_ is not the same as _"01/01/2016"_ when using quotes 
  * Use a asterisk (*) as a wildcard to broaden the search results   
_air*_ finds airplane and airship

_jpg +bob +sue -beach_ to find all jpg images with bob and sue but not at the beach.

# USEK Library Blog
## Map of Beirut (Beyrouth), 1922
by Carlos Younes on April 19th, 2021 in [Beirut](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Map-of-Beirut-1922?tag_id=200344), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Map-of-Beirut-1922?tag_id=144979) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Map-of-Beirut-1922#comments)  

![alt="map of beirut 1922"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Map_Beyrouth_1922.jpg)
The map of Beirut was drawn by the cadastral office of the French Army of the Levant in February 1922, at a scale of 1/10,000.
Highlighted in red are residences, institutions and populated areas at the time, in addition to bridges and street names, the tramway line, the hippodrome, and agricultural lands the majority of which were planted with vineyards, berries and cactus.
We also see on the map some landmarks that no longer exist, namely:
**Place des Canons:** Currently known as the Martyrs’ Square, it was called at the time as the Cannons’ Square, in reference to the cannons that were installed therein to protect Beirut against naval invasions.
During World War I, Jamal Pasha executed death sentences in the square for an elite of Lebanese and Syrian intellectuals, and since then it was known as the Martyrs’ Square. In 1937, May 6 was declared as the Martyrs’ Day in honor of their memory and to pay tribute to their pure souls.
**The Petit Serail:** It was called the _Petit Serail_ (literally the ‘small serail’) to distinguish it from the Grand Serail; it was built on the northern side of the Cannons’ Square (now opposite the _Le Gray_ Hotel), and it was inaugurated in 1884 as the seat of the governor of Beirut, then the seat of the French rulers, and finally the seat of the Presidency of the Republic.
The most powerful image in the memory of the Lebanese is the one that represents the demonstrators on the morning of November 22, 1943, climbing the roof of the Serail to raise the new Lebanese flag before the return of President Bechara El-Khoury along with the men of independence to the _Petit Serail_ after being arrested in the citadel of Rashaya.
In order to expand the Martyrs' Square, the Grand Serail was demolished in 1950.

# USEK Library Blog
## فارس خيرالله اسطفان
by Carlos Younes on April 13th, 2022 | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/95602#comments)  

في زمن الألام والقيامة نستذكر صديق المكتبة العامة في جامعة الروح القدس – الكسليك، إبن بلدة غوسطا المرحوم فارس خيرالله اسطفان الذي غادرنا الى بيت الأب السماوي في 6 نيسان 2022.
في مثل هذا اليوم من العام 2020 وهب المرحوم فارس اسطفان أرشيف جريدة الهدى النيويوركية الى المكتبة العامة في جامعة الروح القدس – الكسليك، ليكون هذا الأرشيف بمتناول الباحثين والطلاب في دراساتهم البحثية.
مع الاشارة الى أن جريدة الهدى هي من أعرق الصحف المهجرية الناطقة باللغة العربية، وقد لعبت دوراً هامأ في دنيا الإغتراب، وكانت الصوت الحر للبنان واللبنانيين في المهجر خاصة في زمن الحرب العالمية الأولى والمجاعة.
بعد ان انتقال ملكيتها في أوائل السبعينات الى فارس اسطفان تحول دار " الهدى" الى ملتقى التف حواليه كل من أحب وخاف على الوطن الجريح، خاصة خلال الحرب الأهلية التي عصفت بلبنان واللبنانيين، فظلت الصوت اللبناني الصارخ للمغتربين والمنتشرين الى جانب جريدة Lebanese American Journal التي تصدر باللغة الأنكليزية.
مع غياب فارس اسطفان في غوسطا غابت صورة لبنان بشجاعته ووطنيته وكرمه ونبله، وغاب فارس الاغتراب والموقف والشهامة والأخلاق، لكن ذكراه ستبقى خالدة من خلال الدراسات والأبحاث التي ستستند الى أرشيفه المحفوط بعناية في مكتبة جامعة الروح القدس - الكسليك.

# USEK Library Blog
## The Maronite Evangeliary, 1673
by Essine Gemayel on March 18th, 2021 in [Evangeliary](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/maronite-evangeliary-1673?tag_id=201291), [Manuscripts](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/maronite-evangeliary-1673?tag_id=200093), [Maronite](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/maronite-evangeliary-1673?tag_id=200349) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/maronite-evangeliary-1673#comments)  

![alt="photos from the maronite gospel"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/collage_with_cross-reused.png)
Did you know that the USEK Library holds thousands of [significant manuscripts, incunables and rare books](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/special-collections)? Its [Conservation and Restoration Center](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/crc)[ ](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/english/crc)oversees the preservation of these priceless heritage collections.
Today, we are featuring one of the most remarkable manuscripts of the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM): 
**_, 1673_**
**_[Qira’at min Al-ānjīl Al -Araba‘a, 1673_ _]_**
The Maronite Evangeliary, written in Aleppo (Syria) contains a Syriac-Garshuni Gospel of the 17th century (1673, 354 ff, 33 x 23 x 10 cm), including a text in two columns (23 lines per column). The Gospels are divided according to the days and feasts of the Maronite liturgical year.
This manuscript was copied and illuminated by the hand of Deacon Rizk – son of Pierre from the Marc family, the student of Bishop Gibrael (f.351v) – following the request of Bishop Gibrael Al Blouzani for the Monastery of Our Lady of Tamich, Lebanon. 
Three miniatures representing the evangelists St. Mark, St. Luke and St. John illuminate this manuscript, and several portals mounted with a cross embellish the beginning of each Gospel.
Throughout the pages, we find several details, filled with decorative Syriac letters, creating sometimes the shape of a cross. 
This manuscript still retains its original full-leather binding.
For more details about the restoration of this manuscript, visit the following page: [https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/crc/step-by-step](https://www.usek.edu.lb/library/crc/step-by-step)
**Call Number :** **USEK-OLM 983**

# USEK Library Blog
## "Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.

# USEK Library Blog
## The Book of the Psalms of David, King and Prophet, 1610
by Joseph Moukarzel on May 22nd, 2021 in [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610?tag_id=144979), [Maronite](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610?tag_id=200349), [Ottoman Empire](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610?tag_id=200100), [Psalms](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610?tag_id=201294), [Special Collections](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610?tag_id=200094) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/The-Book-of-the-Psalms-of-David-King-and-Prophet-1610#comments)  

![alt="Book of Psalms"](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/281549/images/May_post6.png)
**The Book of the Psalms of David, King and Prophet, 1610**
_**[Ktobo d-mazmouré d-David malko wa-nbiyo]**_
The  _Book of Psalms_ was printed in the monastery of Saint Anthony of Qozhaya in 1610. Since it is the first book ever printed in the Eastern part of the Ottoman Empire, it is considered as one of the most distinguished works in the history of typography.
In 1485, the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid II issued a decree banning all forms of printing in the Empire, and this prohibition was reinforced by Sultan Selim I in 1515. The supposed purpose was to safeguard the contents of Islamic religious books from being modified in the process of printing. However, some researchers believe that the real motivation was to control the work of calligraphers and painters, and to ensure that Istanbul benefited financially. This ban remained in force until the establishment of the first Ottoman printing press in Istanbul in 1727 which printed only in Arabic and Turkish.
The Christian minorities living in the eastern part of the Ottoman Empire were unaware of the printing process during the majority of the 16th century. The first published work seen by the Maronites was a book on Christian catechism in Garshuni, printed in Rome in 1580. In this same year, it was brought to Mount Lebanon by the papal legate Giovanni Battista Eliano, who distributed it to the members of the Synod of Qanoubine. Eliano also distributed another book he translated himself from Latin into Arabic (printed in Garshuni, 1580). It was entitled  _Creed of the Catholic Faith_ , approved by the Council of Trent, and known as the  _Creed of Pope Pius IV_.
However, this development of typography was not paralleled in the Middle East. Although Stefano Evodio Assemani recorded in the catalogue of the Bilblioteca Medicea Laurenziana (Florence - Italy), that the  _Book of Psalms_ was printed in the Qozhaya monastery in 1585, this statement remains questionable, since there is no physical evidence of the existence of this edition in any library. Furthermore, the papal legate Girolamo Dandini noted, during his apostolical visit to the Maronites in 1596, that there were no printing presses in the region. Therefore, it can be concluded that the first book in the eastern part of the Ottoman Empire was this Syriac-Garshuni  _Book of Psalms,_ printed at Qozhaya monastery in 1610.
Researchers tend to believe, without any reliable sources, that Sarkis, ater named Archbishop of Damascus, purchased printing tools from a city in Italy and carried them back to Mount Lebanon after the election of Patriarch Makhlouf (circa 1609). It is important to mention that since printing presses at that time were made of wood, and required great dexterity and expertise, the printing of the  _Book of Psalms_ was not completed before November 10th, 1610, as is written in the colophon at the end of the book. However, the fact that this book was the only one printed at that time raises many questions such as: why other books were not printed, what happened to the printing press or even if the printing press was dismantled. The relevant historical sources do not delve into this topic at all, and most of them actually ignore the existence of this printing press. For these reasons, we wonder whether the  _Book of Psalms_ was only printed in a limited number of copies before the printing press was dismantled.
The  _Book of Psalms_ is made up of 268 pages and uses Syriac letters for pagination (except for the first eight pages which were not paginated). The psalm verses are not numbered but divided into groups of five, with a number placed in the margin to mark each of these groups.
We still do not know exactly how many copies were printed and distributed. All we can confirm is that a German traveler bought one copy in Tripoli in 1611. Currently we have tracked six copies in various public and private libraries: National Library of France, the Saint Geneviève Library in Paris, the Staatsbibliothek in Nürnberg (Germany), the Herzog August Bibliothek, in Wolfenbüttel (Germany), the Saint Joseph University Library in Beirut and lastly the Holy Spirit University Library of Kaslik (Lebanon).

# USEK Library Blog
## The USEK Library Partners with the British Library to Digitize Endangered Historical Newspapers in the Middle East (1895-1950)
by Elham Abdallah on March 13th, 2023 in [Archives](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=200095), [British Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225150), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225154), [Digitization](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225155), [EAP1434](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225149), [Endangered Archives Programme](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225151), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225152), [History](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=144974), [Identity Crisis](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225153), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=144979), [Metadata](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225156), [Middle Eastern Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=202255), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

# USEK Library Blog
## Partnership between USEK Library and Moise Khayrallah Center: Arabic OCR
by Elham Abdallah on April 4th, 2022 in [Diaspora](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR?tag_id=213563), [Latin America](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR?tag_id=213562), [Lebanese Immigrants](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR?tag_id=213564), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR?tag_id=144979) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/ARABIC_OCR_LIBRARY1__002_.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce its cooperation with Moise Khayrallah Center in USA aimed at implementing the Arabic OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology to the digital periodicals from the Latin American collection housed at the USEK Library. These periodicals were written in Arabic and published in Latin America by Lebanese immigrants, dating back to the 19th century, era of the great immigration wave, onwards.
This partnership is part of the arabicarchives.org project initiated by Khayrallah Center, which collects the early Arab immigrants’ archives that have left remarkable legacy in North and South America. These records were not accessible because they were dispersed and stored in disparate locations, and hence not digitally searchable. Consequently, the Center has created a completely searchable database of these publications by developing Arabic OCR technology to render the digitized images of these history pages into searchable text. 
The objectives of this collaboration are to contribute to scholarly research, explore a heritage that spans years and tells the stories of Lebanese/Arab pioneers, and expand non-English content on the web. 
Accordingly, our digital periodicals from the Latin American collection will be fully searchable, allowing users to easily search their content by keyword. 
_“We at USEK Library, entrusted with this legacy, are proud to join this remarkable initiative, to bring our treasures and efforts in support of the expertise of Khayrallah Center to achieve this worthy goal”_ , said Fr. Joseph Moukarzel, USEK Library Director.
_“Joining this partnership allows us to share our collection with scholars, researchers and public worldwide, a step forward in keeping with our commitment to discoverability and to the growth of our renowned collections”_ , added Fr. Moukarzel.
_“_ _The Khayrallah Center is delighted and privileged to collaborate with USEK Library, one of the premiere archives in the world for Lebanese history. This partnership will add a treasure trove of periodicals to our Arabic database and give researchers and the general public unprecedented access to a wealth of historical literature about Lebanese migration to South America. We regard this as the first step in a very important partnership between NC State University and USEK."_ stated Dr. Akram Khater, Director of Moise Khayrallah Center.
To know more about the Latin American collection at the USEK Library, click here: 
<https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/latin-american-collection>

# USEK Library Blog
## Letter from the heirs of Emir Fares Chehab : Titanic victim
by Carlos Younes on April 14th, 2021 in [Emir Fares Chehab](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab?tag_id=201996), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab?tag_id=144979), [Titanic Sank](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab?tag_id=201994), [Titanic Victim](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab?tag_id=201995) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/titanic.png)
**Storied @ USEK Library**
On the 109th anniversary of the sinking of the Titanic, there are still many conflicting opinions about the exact number of Lebanese victims who drowned on that tragic day in April 1912.
Some say that the official number of Lebanese victims is 85, while others claim that the number is considerably higher and can be up to 125, or maybe even more. This discrepancy in numbers is because the nationality of the victims is missing, and many names were incorrectly registered. 
The Lebanese who sailed on the “unsinkable ship” are mostly third-class passengers, who were attempting to flee persecution and poverty in their home country, and dream of a better tomorrow in the country of freedom. They were originally from: Bint Jbeil, Tebnine, Sereel, Kfarmechki, Beirut, Kfaraabida, Zgharta, Kfardlaqos, Tripoli, ‘Ibrin, Hardine (the village that lost 11 of its residents), Kfarzghab, Fghal, Choueir, Al-Hakur, Toula, Bkassine, Hadath, Zahle, Tahoum, and Al-Faqha .
During our search in the Ottoman archives in Istanbul, and among the documents related to the Titanic, we found a letter signed by the heirs of Prince Fares Chehab, one of the ship’s victims from the village of Hadath. The heirs include his wife Hind Chehab, his mother Marwa Chehab, and his sister Helen Chehab; they addressed the letter to the Emergency Committee on June 11, 1912, through the Turkish Consul in London, to claim compensation following the death of their devisor on the Titanic.
It is said about Prince Fares Chehab that while the ship was sinking, he quietly grabbed his _oud_ and played a song "Be strong, young fellowmen. It is a shame to die without _dabke_ and songs”.
في الذكرى التاسعة بعد المئة لغرق سفينة التايتانيك، لا تزال الآراء متضاربة حول العدد الفعلي للضحايا اللبنانيين الذين قضوا غرقًا في ذلك اليوم المشؤوم من شهر نيسان 1912.
يذكر البعض أنَّ العدد الرسمي للضحايا اللبنانيين هو 85 شخصًا، فيما يذكر البعض الآخر إنَّ الرقم أعلى وقد يصل إلى 125 شخصًا وربما أكثر. ويعود هذا التفاوت في الأرقام إلى عدم ذكر جنسيات الضحايا والأخطاء المرتكبة خلال إجراءات التسجيل لكثير من الأسماء.
كانت غالبيّة اللبنانيين الذين أبحروا في السفينة التي "لا تغرق ولا تحرق" من ركاب الدرجة الثالثة، هربًا من الاضطهاد والفقر في بلدهم الأم وحلماً بغدٍ أفضل في بلد الحرية. وهم من بلدات: بنت جبيل، تبنين، سرعل، كفرمشكي، بيروت، كفرعبيدا، زغرتا، كفردلاقوس، طرابلس، عبرين، حردين (القرية التي خسرت 11 من أبنائها)، كفرصغاب، فغال، الشوير، الحاكور، تولا، بكاسين، الحدث، زحلة، تحوم، والفاكهة.
خلال بحثنا في الأرشيف العثماني في اسطنبول، ومن ضمن الوثائق المتعلقة بسفينة التايتانك، عثرنا على رسالة موقّعة من ورثة الأمير فارس شهاب، أحد ضحايا السفينة من قرية الحدث، وهم زوجته هند شهاب، ووالدته مروه شهاب، وشقيقته هيلين شهاب، موجهة إلى لجنة الطوارئ بتاريخ 11 حزيران 1912، من خلال القنصل التركي في لندن، طالبين التعويض عليهم جراء وفاة مورثهم في باخرة التايتانيك.
ويُروى عن الأمير فارس شهاب أنه أثناء غرق السفينة، أخذ عوده بكل رباطة جأش وعزف عليه أغنية "شدّوا الهمة يا شباب، عيب نموت بدون دبكة وأغاني".
