### Posts with the subject: _Titanic Sank_
## [Letter from the heirs of Emir Fares Chehab : Titanic victim](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab)
by Carlos Younes on April 14th, 2021 in [Emir Fares Chehab](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201996), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Titanic Sank](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201994), [Titanic Victim](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201995) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/titanic.png)
**Storied @ USEK Library**
On the 109th anniversary of the sinking of the Titanic, there are still many conflicting opinions about the exact number of Lebanese victims who drowned on that tragic day in April 1912.
Some say that the official number of Lebanese victims is 85, while others claim that the number is considerably higher and can be up to 125, or maybe even more. This discrepancy in numbers is because the nationality of the victims is missing, and many names were incorrectly registered. 
The Lebanese who sailed on the “unsinkable ship” are mostly third-class passengers, who were attempting to flee persecution and poverty in their home country, and dream of a better tomorrow in the country of freedom. They were originally from: Bint Jbeil, Tebnine, Sereel, Kfarmechki, Beirut, Kfaraabida, Zgharta, Kfardlaqos, Tripoli, ‘Ibrin, Hardine (the village that lost 11 of its residents), Kfarzghab, Fghal, Choueir, Al-Hakur, Toula, Bkassine, Hadath, Zahle, Tahoum, and Al-Faqha .
During our search in the Ottoman archives in Istanbul, and among the documents related to the Titanic, we found a letter signed by the heirs of Prince Fares Chehab, one of the ship’s victims from the village of Hadath. The heirs include his wife Hind Chehab, his mother Marwa Chehab, and his sister Helen Chehab; they addressed the letter to the Emergency Committee on June 11, 1912, through the Turkish Consul in London, to claim compensation following the death of their devisor on the Titanic.
It is said about Prince Fares Chehab that while the ship was sinking, he quietly grabbed his _oud_ and played a song "Be strong, young fellowmen. It is a shame to die without _dabke_ and songs”.
في الذكرى التاسعة بعد المئة لغرق سفينة التايتانيك، لا تزال الآراء متضاربة حول العدد الفعلي للضحايا اللبنانيين الذين قضوا غرقًا في ذلك اليوم المشؤوم من شهر نيسان 1912.
يذكر البعض أنَّ العدد الرسمي للضحايا اللبنانيين هو 85 شخصًا، فيما يذكر البعض الآخر إنَّ الرقم أعلى وقد يصل إلى 125 شخصًا وربما أكثر. ويعود هذا التفاوت في الأرقام إلى عدم ذكر جنسيات الضحايا والأخطاء المرتكبة خلال إجراءات التسجيل لكثير من الأسماء.
كانت غالبيّة اللبنانيين الذين أبحروا في السفينة التي "لا تغرق ولا تحرق" من ركاب الدرجة الثالثة، هربًا من الاضطهاد والفقر في بلدهم الأم وحلماً بغدٍ أفضل في بلد الحرية. وهم من بلدات: بنت جبيل، تبنين، سرعل، كفرمشكي، بيروت، كفرعبيدا، زغرتا، كفردلاقوس، طرابلس، عبرين، حردين (القرية التي خسرت 11 من أبنائها)، كفرصغاب، فغال، الشوير، الحاكور، تولا، بكاسين، الحدث، زحلة، تحوم، والفاكهة.
خلال بحثنا في الأرشيف العثماني في اسطنبول، ومن ضمن الوثائق المتعلقة بسفينة التايتانك، عثرنا على رسالة موقّعة من ورثة الأمير فارس شهاب، أحد ضحايا السفينة من قرية الحدث، وهم زوجته هند شهاب، ووالدته مروه شهاب، وشقيقته هيلين شهاب، موجهة إلى لجنة الطوارئ بتاريخ 11 حزيران 1912، من خلال القنصل التركي في لندن، طالبين التعويض عليهم جراء وفاة مورثهم في باخرة التايتانيك.
ويُروى عن الأمير فارس شهاب أنه أثناء غرق السفينة، أخذ عوده بكل رباطة جأش وعزف عليه أغنية "شدّوا الهمة يا شباب، عيب نموت بدون دبكة وأغاني".

## [Partnership between USEK Library and Moise Khayrallah Center: Arabic OCR](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR)
by Elham Abdallah on April 4th, 2022 in [Diaspora](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213563), [Latin America](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213562), [Lebanese Immigrants](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213564), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/ARABIC_OCR_LIBRARY1__002_.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce its cooperation with Moise Khayrallah Center in USA aimed at implementing the Arabic OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology to the digital periodicals from the Latin American collection housed at the USEK Library. These periodicals were written in Arabic and published in Latin America by Lebanese immigrants, dating back to the 19th century, era of the great immigration wave, onwards.
This partnership is part of the arabicarchives.org project initiated by Khayrallah Center, which collects the early Arab immigrants’ archives that have left remarkable legacy in North and South America. These records were not accessible because they were dispersed and stored in disparate locations, and hence not digitally searchable. Consequently, the Center has created a completely searchable database of these publications by developing Arabic OCR technology to render the digitized images of these history pages into searchable text. 
The objectives of this collaboration are to contribute to scholarly research, explore a heritage that spans years and tells the stories of Lebanese/Arab pioneers, and expand non-English content on the web. 
Accordingly, our digital periodicals from the Latin American collection will be fully searchable, allowing users to easily search their content by keyword. 
_“We at USEK Library, entrusted with this legacy, are proud to join this remarkable initiative, to bring our treasures and efforts in support of the expertise of Khayrallah Center to achieve this worthy goal”_ , said Fr. Joseph Moukarzel, USEK Library Director.
_“Joining this partnership allows us to share our collection with scholars, researchers and public worldwide, a step forward in keeping with our commitment to discoverability and to the growth of our renowned collections”_ , added Fr. Moukarzel.
_“_ _The Khayrallah Center is delighted and privileged to collaborate with USEK Library, one of the premiere archives in the world for Lebanese history. This partnership will add a treasure trove of periodicals to our Arabic database and give researchers and the general public unprecedented access to a wealth of historical literature about Lebanese migration to South America. We regard this as the first step in a very important partnership between NC State University and USEK."_ stated Dr. Akram Khater, Director of Moise Khayrallah Center.

### Posts with the subject: _Endangered Archives Programme_
## [The USEK Library Partners with the British Library to Digitize Endangered Historical Newspapers in the Middle East (1895-1950)](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library)
by Elham Abdallah on March 13th, 2023 in [Archives](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200095), [British Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225150), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Digitization](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225155), [EAP1434](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225149), [Endangered Archives Programme](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225151), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [History](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144974), [Identity Crisis](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225153), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Metadata](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225156), [Middle Eastern Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=202255), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

# USEK Library Blog
### Posts with the subject: _Emir Fares Chehab_
## [Letter from the heirs of Emir Fares Chehab : Titanic victim](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab)
by Carlos Younes on April 14th, 2021 in [Emir Fares Chehab](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201996), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Titanic Sank](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201994), [Titanic Victim](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=201995) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/emir-fares-chehab#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/titanic.png)
**Storied @ USEK Library**
On the 109th anniversary of the sinking of the Titanic, there are still many conflicting opinions about the exact number of Lebanese victims who drowned on that tragic day in April 1912.
Some say that the official number of Lebanese victims is 85, while others claim that the number is considerably higher and can be up to 125, or maybe even more. This discrepancy in numbers is because the nationality of the victims is missing, and many names were incorrectly registered. 
The Lebanese who sailed on the “unsinkable ship” are mostly third-class passengers, who were attempting to flee persecution and poverty in their home country, and dream of a better tomorrow in the country of freedom. They were originally from: Bint Jbeil, Tebnine, Sereel, Kfarmechki, Beirut, Kfaraabida, Zgharta, Kfardlaqos, Tripoli, ‘Ibrin, Hardine (the village that lost 11 of its residents), Kfarzghab, Fghal, Choueir, Al-Hakur, Toula, Bkassine, Hadath, Zahle, Tahoum, and Al-Faqha .
During our search in the Ottoman archives in Istanbul, and among the documents related to the Titanic, we found a letter signed by the heirs of Prince Fares Chehab, one of the ship’s victims from the village of Hadath. The heirs include his wife Hind Chehab, his mother Marwa Chehab, and his sister Helen Chehab; they addressed the letter to the Emergency Committee on June 11, 1912, through the Turkish Consul in London, to claim compensation following the death of their devisor on the Titanic.
It is said about Prince Fares Chehab that while the ship was sinking, he quietly grabbed his _oud_ and played a song "Be strong, young fellowmen. It is a shame to die without _dabke_ and songs”.
في الذكرى التاسعة بعد المئة لغرق سفينة التايتانيك، لا تزال الآراء متضاربة حول العدد الفعلي للضحايا اللبنانيين الذين قضوا غرقًا في ذلك اليوم المشؤوم من شهر نيسان 1912.
يذكر البعض أنَّ العدد الرسمي للضحايا اللبنانيين هو 85 شخصًا، فيما يذكر البعض الآخر إنَّ الرقم أعلى وقد يصل إلى 125 شخصًا وربما أكثر. ويعود هذا التفاوت في الأرقام إلى عدم ذكر جنسيات الضحايا والأخطاء المرتكبة خلال إجراءات التسجيل لكثير من الأسماء.
كانت غالبيّة اللبنانيين الذين أبحروا في السفينة التي "لا تغرق ولا تحرق" من ركاب الدرجة الثالثة، هربًا من الاضطهاد والفقر في بلدهم الأم وحلماً بغدٍ أفضل في بلد الحرية. وهم من بلدات: بنت جبيل، تبنين، سرعل، كفرمشكي، بيروت، كفرعبيدا، زغرتا، كفردلاقوس، طرابلس، عبرين، حردين (القرية التي خسرت 11 من أبنائها)، كفرصغاب، فغال، الشوير، الحاكور، تولا، بكاسين، الحدث، زحلة، تحوم، والفاكهة.
خلال بحثنا في الأرشيف العثماني في اسطنبول، ومن ضمن الوثائق المتعلقة بسفينة التايتانك، عثرنا على رسالة موقّعة من ورثة الأمير فارس شهاب، أحد ضحايا السفينة من قرية الحدث، وهم زوجته هند شهاب، ووالدته مروه شهاب، وشقيقته هيلين شهاب، موجهة إلى لجنة الطوارئ بتاريخ 11 حزيران 1912، من خلال القنصل التركي في لندن، طالبين التعويض عليهم جراء وفاة مورثهم في باخرة التايتانيك.
ويُروى عن الأمير فارس شهاب أنه أثناء غرق السفينة، أخذ عوده بكل رباطة جأش وعزف عليه أغنية "شدّوا الهمة يا شباب، عيب نموت بدون دبكة وأغاني".

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

## ["Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers)
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.

# USEK Library Blog
### Posts with the subject: _British Library_
## [The USEK Library Partners with the British Library to Digitize Endangered Historical Newspapers in the Middle East (1895-1950)](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library)
by Elham Abdallah on March 13th, 2023 in [Archives](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200095), [British Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225150), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Digitization](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225155), [EAP1434](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225149), [Endangered Archives Programme](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225151), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [History](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144974), [Identity Crisis](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225153), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Metadata](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225156), [Middle Eastern Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=202255), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

## Welcome to AGORA
The AGORA programme, set up by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN (FAO) together with major publishers, enables developing countries to gain access to an outstanding digital library collection in the fields of food, agriculture, environmental science and related social sciences. AGORA provides a collection of up to 15,500 key journals and up to 48,000 books in more than 115 countries. AGORA is designed to enhance the scholarship of the many thousands of students, faculty and researchers in agriculture and life sciences in the developing world. AGORA is one of the five programmes that make up Research4Life: AGORA, HINARI, OARE, ARDI and GOALI. 
Research4Life content is grouped into the following collections: 
  * [**Hinari**](https://agora.research4life.org/content/hinari) is one of the world's largest collections of **biomedical and health** literature.
  * ****AGORA**** is an outstanding digital library collection in the fields of ****food and agriculture****.
  * [****ARDI****](https://ardi.research4life.org/)****scientific and technical**** information.
  * [**GOALI**](https://agora.research4life.org/content/goali)**law and social sciences** , including politics, economics, philosophy, history and more.
  * [**OARE**](https://agora.research4life.org/content/oare)**environment** , including ecology, geography, energy and more.

# USEK Library Blog
### Posts with the subject: _Historical Newspapers_
## ["Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers)
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.
* * *
## [The USEK Library Partners with the British Library to Digitize Endangered Historical Newspapers in the Middle East (1895-1950)](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library)
by Elham Abdallah on March 13th, 2023 in [Archives](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200095), [British Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225150), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Digitization](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225155), [EAP1434](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225149), [Endangered Archives Programme](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225151), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [History](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144974), [Identity Crisis](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225153), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Metadata](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225156), [Middle Eastern Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=202255), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

## [Partnership between USEK Library and Moise Khayrallah Center: Arabic OCR](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR)
by Elham Abdallah on April 4th, 2022 in [Diaspora](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213563), [Latin America](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213562), [Lebanese Immigrants](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213564), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/ARABIC_OCR_LIBRARY1__002_.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce its cooperation with Moise Khayrallah Center in USA aimed at implementing the Arabic OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology to the digital periodicals from the Latin American collection housed at the USEK Library. These periodicals were written in Arabic and published in Latin America by Lebanese immigrants, dating back to the 19th century, era of the great immigration wave, onwards.
This partnership is part of the arabicarchives.org project initiated by Khayrallah Center, which collects the early Arab immigrants’ archives that have left remarkable legacy in North and South America. These records were not accessible because they were dispersed and stored in disparate locations, and hence not digitally searchable. Consequently, the Center has created a completely searchable database of these publications by developing Arabic OCR technology to render the digitized images of these history pages into searchable text. 
The objectives of this collaboration are to contribute to scholarly research, explore a heritage that spans years and tells the stories of Lebanese/Arab pioneers, and expand non-English content on the web. 
Accordingly, our digital periodicals from the Latin American collection will be fully searchable, allowing users to easily search their content by keyword. 
_“We at USEK Library, entrusted with this legacy, are proud to join this remarkable initiative, to bring our treasures and efforts in support of the expertise of Khayrallah Center to achieve this worthy goal”_ , said Fr. Joseph Moukarzel, USEK Library Director.
_“Joining this partnership allows us to share our collection with scholars, researchers and public worldwide, a step forward in keeping with our commitment to discoverability and to the growth of our renowned collections”_ , added Fr. Moukarzel.
_“_ _The Khayrallah Center is delighted and privileged to collaborate with USEK Library, one of the premiere archives in the world for Lebanese history. This partnership will add a treasure trove of periodicals to our Arabic database and give researchers and the general public unprecedented access to a wealth of historical literature about Lebanese migration to South America. We regard this as the first step in a very important partnership between NC State University and USEK."_ stated Dr. Akram Khater, Director of Moise Khayrallah Center.
To know more about the Latin American collection at the USEK Library, click here: 
<https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/latin-american-collection>

### Posts with the subject: _Lebanese Immigrants_
## [Partnership between USEK Library and Moise Khayrallah Center: Arabic OCR](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR)
by Elham Abdallah on April 4th, 2022 in [Diaspora](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213563), [Latin America](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213562), [Lebanese Immigrants](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=213564), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Arabic-OCR#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/ARABIC_OCR_LIBRARY1__002_.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce its cooperation with Moise Khayrallah Center in USA aimed at implementing the Arabic OCR (Optical Character Recognition) technology to the digital periodicals from the Latin American collection housed at the USEK Library. These periodicals were written in Arabic and published in Latin America by Lebanese immigrants, dating back to the 19th century, era of the great immigration wave, onwards.
This partnership is part of the arabicarchives.org project initiated by Khayrallah Center, which collects the early Arab immigrants’ archives that have left remarkable legacy in North and South America. These records were not accessible because they were dispersed and stored in disparate locations, and hence not digitally searchable. Consequently, the Center has created a completely searchable database of these publications by developing Arabic OCR technology to render the digitized images of these history pages into searchable text. 
The objectives of this collaboration are to contribute to scholarly research, explore a heritage that spans years and tells the stories of Lebanese/Arab pioneers, and expand non-English content on the web. 
Accordingly, our digital periodicals from the Latin American collection will be fully searchable, allowing users to easily search their content by keyword. 
_“We at USEK Library, entrusted with this legacy, are proud to join this remarkable initiative, to bring our treasures and efforts in support of the expertise of Khayrallah Center to achieve this worthy goal”_ , said Fr. Joseph Moukarzel, USEK Library Director.
_“Joining this partnership allows us to share our collection with scholars, researchers and public worldwide, a step forward in keeping with our commitment to discoverability and to the growth of our renowned collections”_ , added Fr. Moukarzel.
_“_ _The Khayrallah Center is delighted and privileged to collaborate with USEK Library, one of the premiere archives in the world for Lebanese history. This partnership will add a treasure trove of periodicals to our Arabic database and give researchers and the general public unprecedented access to a wealth of historical literature about Lebanese migration to South America. We regard this as the first step in a very important partnership between NC State University and USEK."_ stated Dr. Akram Khater, Director of Moise Khayrallah Center.
To know more about the Latin American collection at the USEK Library, click here: 
<https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/latin-american-collection>

### Posts with the subject: _Cultural Heritage Preservation_
## ["Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers)
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.
* * *
## [The USEK Library Partners with the British Library to Digitize Endangered Historical Newspapers in the Middle East (1895-1950)](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library)
by Elham Abdallah on March 13th, 2023 in [Archives](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200095), [British Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225150), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Digitization](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225155), [EAP1434](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225149), [Endangered Archives Programme](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225151), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [History](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144974), [Identity Crisis](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225153), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Metadata](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225156), [Middle Eastern Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=202255), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

## [The USEK Library Partners with the British Library to Digitize Endangered Historical Newspapers in the Middle East (1895-1950)](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library)
by Elham Abdallah on March 13th, 2023 in [Archives](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=200095), [British Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225150), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Digitization](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225155), [EAP1434](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225149), [Endangered Archives Programme](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225151), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [History](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144974), [Identity Crisis](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225153), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Metadata](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225156), [Middle Eastern Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=202255), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/EAP1434-USEK-Library#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/EAP_1434_VISUAL.jpg)
The USEK Library is delighted to announce receiving a Major Grant from the Endangered Archives Programme funded by the British Library and supported by Arcadia.
**An ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon: Arab or What? Digitizing early newspapers in the Middle East, 1895-1950 (EAP1434).**
This project aims at preserving 24 848 Newspaper pages dating back to 1895 and showcasing the identity crisis of what’s called nowadays “Lebanon”: division amongst Lebanese in agreement with/against several nationalist’s movements, their views/activism towards independence in relation to religious affiliations. They reveal the diverse viewpoints of everyday life in Lebanon and surrounding Arab countries: geopolitical, social, educational, political economy... highlighting the dynamics of localities from social/anthropological perspectives. 
This fragile collection was rescued and relocated to USEK library. It was spotted in poor and harsh handling, consequently, needing urgent curation to secure the voice of the past as a path towards leading the tomorrow.  
The project entails digitizing and indexing the collection content, spreading awareness on protecting cultural heritage, as well as putting the material at the disposal of researchers and scholars worldwide.
Ms. Elham Abdallah, Assistant University Librarian at USEK library and the project lead acknowledged the support of the British library and stated: “ _this is a unique opportunity to safeguard the voice of the past and shed light on the ongoing identity crisis in Lebanon. The collection, which was jeopardized by auto-deterioration with time, deserves to be curated and disseminated globally. USEK Library is thrilled to be a part of this project. It is a testament to our commitment to preserving the past and making it accessible to all”._
Abdallah also acknowledged the professionalism of the Digitization and Metadata team and thanked them for bringing this exceptional project to fruition.
For more information about The Endangered Archives Programme at the British Library, click here: [_https://eap.bl.uk/_](https://eap.bl.uk/)

## ["Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers)
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.

## ["Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers)
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.

# Father Boulos Daher 1915-1990: Home
This guide provides access to primary sources and materials available at USEK Library. It serves as a starting point to find resources for searching the life Father Boulos Daher, publications about and by him, media, quotes etc..
  * [ Home ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/boulos-daher/home)
  * [ Books by Daher ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/boulos-daher/Books)
  * [ Articles by Daher ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/boulos-daher/articles)
  * [ Books on Daher ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/boulos-daher/Books-daher)


##  Biography 
Born on July 14, 1915 in the town of Ehmej, Father Boulos Daher was a member of the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM). Following a BA in Theology from the _Université de Strasbourg_ in France, he earned a PhD in Philosophy from the _Université de Paris_ in addition to a degree in Arabic, Hebrew, and Syriac from the _Institut Catholique_ of Paris. Ordained to the priesthood on May 30, 1948, he was appointed to teach philosophy at the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK) where he held the position of Dean of the Faculty of Letters. 
He was the managing editor of the magazine _Charbel_ and the superior of the Saint Maron Monastery in Annaya for thirteen years. His most notable achievements include the construction of the Saint Charbel Church in Annaya. He died in 1990. 
راهب لبناني ماروني. ولد في 14 تموز سنة 1915 في بلدة إهمج. نال ليسانس في اللاهوت من جامعة ستراسبورغ في فرنسا. حاز على دكتوراه في الفلسفة من جامعة باريس وعلى دبلوم في اللغة العربية والعبرانية والسريانية من المعهد الكاثوليكي في باريس. منح رتبة الكهنوت في 30 أيار 1948. عين استاذ للفلسفة في جامعة الروح القدس – الكسليك وعميدا لكلية الاداب. مدير تحرير مجلة "شربل". تولى رئاسة دير مار مارون في عنايا لمدة ثلاث عشرة سنة. من أهم إنجازاته بناء كنيسة مار شريل في عنايا. توفي سنة 1990

# USEK Library Blog
### Posts with the subject: _Al-Tayyar_
## ["Al-Telegraph" and "Al-Tayyar" Newspapers: Deed of Gift from lawyer Fawzi Toufic Al-Matni and his Siblings](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers)
by Carlos Younes on September 14th, 2023 in [Al-Tayyar](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232624), [Al-Telegraph](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232622), [Cultural Heritage Preservation](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225154), [Deed of Gift](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232621), [Historical Newspapers](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225152), [Lebanon](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=144979), [Phoenix Center for Lebanese Studies](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=232623), [USEK Library](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog?tag_id=225148) | [0 Comments](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/blog/Al-Telegraph-and-Al-Tayyar-Newspapers#comments)  

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/278579/images/Post_14-09-23-01_01.jpg)
**“Al-Telegraph”** was initially a weekly magazine founded in Beirut in 1930 by journalist Tawfiq Al-Matni, under the name **“Beirut Telegraph”.** It is a weekly illustrated fictional magazine whose slogan is the **“** People’s Magazine**”** ,
On February 12, 1945, it shifted from a weekly magazine into a daily political newspaper, published every afternoon and on Monday mornings.
“Al-Telegraph” was renowned for raising the voice of the opposition, hence the voice of the workers, the peasants, the aggrieved and the oppressed, the voice of the voiceless.
Many well-known writers and politicians took turns writing in “Al Telegraph” newspaper, including Saeb Salam, Hamid Franjieh, Kamal Jumblatt, Hussein Al-Awaini, Ahmed Al-Asaad, etc. 
“Al-Telegraph” fought many battles in defense of freedoms and played a key political role in the history of Lebanese political life. It was engaged in fierce battles against the mandate extension of President Beshara Al-Khoury and later against that of President Camille Chamoun. It also fought battles against corruption in state administrations and against the interference of foreign countries in domestic politics.
In April 1950, Tawfiq Al-Matni issued a political newspaper under the name of **“Al-Tayyar”** ; in October 1960 the two newspapers were merged into one under the name **“Al-Tayyar wal Telegraph”** , under the slogan "the newspaper of the people, to defend the people, in the hands of the people”.
On the dawn of May 8, 1958, journalist Nassib Al-Matni, brother of Tawfiq Al-Matni, owner of the Telegraph newspaper, was assassinated. He was the first victim of the press after independence. His blood sparked the revolution as demonstrations and strikes spread across the country. Hundreds of people were killed or wounded.
“Al-Telegraph” and “Al-Tayyar” newspapers were donated to the USEK Library by **lawyer Fawzi Tawfiq al-Matni, and his siblings,****Dr. Ghassan, Jihan and Ghada Toufic Al-Matni** , with the aim of digitizing them to be available to researchers and students throughout their studies and research.

# nui.aria.page.search
### AATA
is a free research database containing abstracts of literature related to the preservation and conservation of material cultural heritage. It has been managed and published by the Getty since 1983. AATA contains over 170,000 records and adds approximately 4,000 new records each year through regular updates. The database also includes selected subject-specific bibliographies produced as part of the Getty Conservation Institute’s own conservation and scientific research projects or as part of specific collaborative projects in which the Institute is involved.
Links [What's inside?](https://www.getty.edu/databases-tools-and-technologies/aata/) [What are the main publications abstracted?](https://media.getty.edu/Text/51619e79-75d8-544d-ad84-2c0663b54a77.pdf) [Where can I find more library materials on conservation?](https://libguides.getty.edu/friendly.php?s=conservation) [What’s the history of AATA?](https://blogs.getty.edu/iris/the-database-conservators-built/) [How can I become a volunteer abstractor?](https://www.getty.edu/databases-tools-and-technologies/aata/volunteer-abstractors/)
Featured Subject Term
[Microscopes](https://aata.getty.edu/primo-explore/search?query=sub,contains,microscopes&tab=aata&search_scope=AATA&vid=AATA&facet=topic,include,microscopes&offset=0) consist of a lens or a combination of lenses and have a long history as essential optical instruments and equipment, contributing to advancements in scientific research and conservation.
![Antique microscope and case](https://aata.getty.edu/primo-explore/custom/AATA/img/term.jpg)
Compound Microscope and Case (ca. 1751), collection J. Paul Getty Museum. Term and image submitted by Annie Choy, former AATA Graduate Intern.
Recent Additions
The fall update includes abstracts on earthen architecture, concrete pavements and floors, the retouching of cultural heritage, historical wooden structures, stone, and from the North American Textile Conservation Conference.

##  What is EBSCO eBook Academic Collection? 
[EBSCO eBook Academic Collection](http://ezproxy.usek.edu.lb/login?url=http://search.ebscohost.com/login.aspx?authtype=ip,uid&profile=ehost&defaultdb=e000xww) contains:
  * A large selection of multidisciplinary e-books representing a broad range of academic subjects; more than 170,000 multidisciplinary e-books.
  * Titles from leading university presses and academic publishers.


##  EBSCO eBooks Requirements 
In order to download EBSCO eBooks, you must have Adobe Digital Editions installed on your computer. You will also need to use Adobe Digital Editions to transfer an eBook to a supported portable eReader device.
Adobe Digital Editions is a free download available at this link: <http://www.adobe.com/products/digital-editions/download.html>
**Note:**
Some EBSCO eBooks do not have DRM (Digital Rights Management) restrictions. These eBooks do not require you to sign into My EBSCO _host_ to download them. In addition, no special software such as Adobe Digital Editions is necessary to download and read them.
DRM-Free EBSCO eBooks can be opened with Adobe® Acrobat or any software that supports PDF or EPUB files and there are no restrictions on printing, saving, or copying.

# Father Antonios Chebli 1894-1964: Home
This guide provides access to primary sources and materials available at USEK Library. It serves as a starting point to find resources for searching the life of Father Antonios Chebli, publications about and by him, media, quotes etc..
  * [ Home ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/father-antonios-chebli/home)
  * [ Books by Chebli ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/father-antonios-chebli/Books)
  * [ Articles by Chebli ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/father-antonios-chebli/articles)
  * [ Books and articles on Chebli ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/father-antonios-chebli/Books-articles-chebli)


##  Biography 
Born in the Lebanese town of Mayfouq in 1894, Father Antonios Chebli was a writer and a composer. Having joined the Lebanese Maronite Order, he was ordained to the priesthood at the Saints Cyprian and Justina Monastery in Kfifane in 1919. Besides serving as a preacher and spiritual guide and undertaking various spiritual duties in many dioceses, he was dedicated to the collection of the monastic and Lebanese heritages until his death in 1964. 
كاتب ومؤلف. ولد في ميفوق (لبنان) عام 1894. راهب لبناني ماروني، سيم كاهناً في دير مار قبريانوس-كفيفان عام 1919. مارس الوعظ والإرشاد والخدم الروحية في عدد من الأبرشيات. إهتم بجمع التراث الرهباني واللبناني. توفي سنة 1964
**Reference**
شبلي، انطونيوس. _فهارس الآثار المطوية_. الكسليك: جامعة الروح القدس-الكسليك، 2005

# Father Ignatius El Khoury, OLM, 1899-1961: Home
This guide provides access to primary sources and materials available at USEK Library. It serves as a starting point to find resources for searching the life of Father Ignatius El Khoury, publications about and by him, media, quotes etc..
  * [ Home ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/father-ignatius-khoury/home)

  * [ External Links ](https://libguides.usek.edu.lb/father-ignatius-khoury/external-links)


##  Biography 
A historian and member of the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM), Father Ignatios Al-Khoury was born in the town of Kfarshakhna – District of Zgharta in 1899. Following his early studies in his hometown’s open-air school, he joined the OLM in 1914 and continued his studies in the order’s schools. At the OLM’s behest, he pursued his higher education at the Jesuits’ _Université Saint-Joseph_ in Beirut and was ordained to the priesthood in 1928. 
Having been appointed as director of the Al-Qala’a School in Akkar wherein he taught Arabic and French, he became an instructor at the Patriarchal College in Beirut and at the Brothers of the Christian Schools’ institution in Ras Beirut in 1913. In 1938, he became the counselor of the Brothers of the Christian Schools at their major institute in Beirut, wherein he dedicated himself to research and writing. 
مؤرخ وراهب ماروني من الرهبانية اللبنانية المارونية. ولد في قرية كفرشخنا – قضاء زغرتا. بدأ دروسه الاولى في مدرسة تحت السنديانة. سنة 1914 دخل الرهبانية اللبنانية ودرس في مدارسها. ادخلته الرهبنة الى الكلية اليسوعية في بيروت فأكمل دروسه العالية. سيم كاهنا سنة 1928  
عين مديرا لمدرسة القلعة في عكار ومدرسا فيها العربية والفرنسية. سنة 1913 استاذا في الكلية البطريركية في بيروت وفي مدرسة الفرير في راس بيروت. سنة 1938 مرشدا لاخوة المدارس المسيحية في معهدهم الكبير في بيروت حيث انصرف للبحث والتأليف

##  Biography 
A Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM) member born in Tannourine Al-Fawqa in 1905, Father Maroun Karam studied at the open-air school of the Saint Anthony Monastery in Houb. Having pronounced his monastic vows in 1922, he was ordained to the priesthood in 1932 at the Our Lady of the Succour Monastery in Jbeil. He taught Arabic, French, and music in OLM schools and took a particular interest in historical research and writing about the OLM’s history. He stayed in various monasteries of the order and died at the Our Lady of the Succour Monastery in Jbeil in 1992.

##  Note 
**Please note that USEK Library houses the Archives of Father Louis Hage.**
##  Biography 
Father Louis Hage (1938-2010) is recognised as a leading figure in sacred music in Lebanon and worldwide. He played a crucial role in the International Society of Sacred Music (_Consociatio Internationalis Musicae Sacrae_ – CIMS). He made significant contributions to the preservation of both oral and manuscript Maronite music, as well as the revitalisation of Syriac and Arabic sacred music. Fr. Hage authored numerous books and studies on the topic and also organised many conferences and seminars to educate, promote, and safeguard this crucial cultural heritage.
Father Louis Hage was born on May 1st, 1938, in Bteddine El-Leqch, in the district of Jezzine, South Lebanon, He began his primary education in his village in 1944, and from 1947 onwards he studied at the Monastery of Our Lady of Machmoucheh, which belongs to the Lebanese Maronite Order (OLM).
In 1962, he finished his two years of philosophical studies at the College of the Holy Spirit in Kaslik, while at the same time studying philology at the _École Supérieure des Lettres_ in Beirut. At the same time, at the College of Kaslik, he was a teacher of music and of Latin. Moving to Rome, he pursued his theological studies at St. Anselm University where in 1966 he earned a Bachelor Degree in Theology. He was ordained a priest in Rome by Bishop Peter Sfeir on December 2nd, 1965.
While in Rome, he pursued music studies at the Pontifical Institute of Sacred Music and also studied the Gregorian chant at the St. Jerome Monastery of the Solesmes Congregation of the Order of Saint Benedict.
Between 1967 and 1970, Fr. Hage pursued a doctorate in Musicology at the University of Paris-Sorbonne, under the supervision of Professor Solange Corbin. In 1971, he earned a diploma from the _École Pratique des Hautes Etudes_ in Paris. In 1980, he received the _Doctorat d'État_ in Musicology from the Ministry of National Education in Lebanon, and, in 1990, he was awarded an honorary Doctorate in Arts from Stonehill College in Massachusetts, USA.
After studying at the Sorbonne, he travelled across Europe, America, Mexico, and Brazil studying ethnomusicology. Upon his return to Lebanon in 1970, Fr. Hage became a professor at the Faculty of Theology and the Institute of Liturgy at USEK.
His passion for preserving and studying the Syro-Maronite chant was consistent with the artistic ambience in Lebanon during the 1950s and 1960s. This period saw a thriving artistic movement, with concerts, festivals and theatre, and the involvement of national and international artists and composers in religious, folkloric, popular, and classical music. This environment helped to promote music studies in Lebanon, meeting academic and methodological standards.
On October 31st, 1970, he founded the Institute of Musicology, which later became an independent Faculty in 1996, which is considered pioneering in Lebanon. He remained the director of the Institute of Musicology and the School of Music until 1986. and then served as the dean of the Faculty of Music from 1999 until his passing in 2010. During these years, various musical events, concerts, and orchestral performances took place, organised in collaboration with Lebanese and foreign institutions, such as _Jeunesses Musicales du Liban_ (JML), the International Federation of Catholic Universities (FIUC), the _Agence de Coopération Culturelle et Technique_ (ACCT), which later became the _Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie_ , and UNESCO. He also organised competitions to encourage musical talent and showcased successful performers of both Western and Eastern instruments. Furthermore, he supervised numerous academic research projects and theses for Lebanese, Arab, and Western students
Fr. Hage assumed leadership of the Kaslik Choir in 1970, 20 years after its establishment, and transformed it into a mixed, diverse choir.
In 1986, He was elected president of USEK, serving until 1992.
Between 1992 and 1995, he served as the abbot of St. Anthony's Monastery in Montreal, Canada. While there, he established the Eastern Cultural Centre, which served as a hub for documentation and research, providing resources on Lebanon, the Arabic language, and music. In recognition of his efforts, he was honoured with the Medal of the 125th Anniversary of the Confederation of Canada on April 13th, 1993, and the ‘Grand Prix’ from the French Academy for his contributions to the French language on December 2nd, 1993.
Fr. Hage served as the president of the _Consociatio Internationalis Musicae Sacrae_ (CIMS) three times, in 1996, 2000, and 2005 until his passing in 2010.
Fr. Hage was a prolific author, writing around 100 scholarly works, including books, articles and speeches on various subjects, particularly Syriac and Maronite music.
Father Louis Hage died on July 1st, 2010, at the age of 72. A formal memorial service was held for him at the Pope John Paul II Amphitheatre on the USEK campus. He was posthumously honoured by the President of the Lebanese Republic, General Michel Suleiman, with the National Order of the Cedar at the rank of officer in recognition of his contributions to Lebanon.
**References**
Achkar, C. (2008). _Père Louis Hage, enfant de Dieu et frère des hommes : homme de prière, homme de musique, homme d’action_. Beyrouth: Auteur.
Maatouk, T. (2020). Vers une prosopographie du Père Louis Hage (1938-2010), musicologue francophone du chant syro-maronite. _Revue des traditions musicales des mondes arabe et méditerranéen,_ 14 ,71-84.

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/163744/images/banner_youakim8.png)
##  Biography 
Born Youwakim Moubarak in the North Lebanon town of Kfarsghab in 1924, he took up the religious name of Youssef Estephan. Having studied Arabic, French, and Syriac at his hometown school, he continued his secondary and higher education at the _Université Saint-Joseph_ in Beirut. Following a PhD in Theology (1958) and another PhD (_Doctorat d’État_) in Literature (1972) in Paris, he became a university instructor in Paris, Leuven (Belgium), and Balamand (Lebanon). A disciple of Louis Massignon, he became his close assistant in his intellectual and spiritual endeavors and oversaw the publication of his works. 
Besides authoring many books in French, he translated a few books from Arabic into French and published or helped publish several serials and periodicals. In addition to his involvement in higher education, he served as a vicar at the Saint-Séverin parish in Paris and took an interest in its mission within the city’s Quartier Latin neighborhood, as well as in its cultural activities and publications. 
Father Youwakim Moubarak participated in several regional and international seminars and conferences on scientific matters pertaining to the Christian-Muslim dialogue, Jerusalem, and Palestine. He died in France on May 24, 1995. 
ولد يواكيم (في الكهنوت يوسف اسطفان) مبارك في بلدة كفرصغاب – شمالي لبنان 1924. درس العربية والفرنسية والسريانية في مدرسة الضيعة. تابع تحصيله العلمي الثانوي والعالي في كلية القديس يوسف – بيروت. في باريس نال شهادة دكتوراه في اللاهوت 1958 ودكتوراه دولة في الاداب 1972   
استاذ جامعي في باريس ولوفان (بلجيكا) والبلمند (لبنان). تتلمذ على يد معلمه لويس ماسينيون، ثم اصبح معاونه المقرّب في نطاق نشاطاته الفكرية والروحية، واشرف على نشر اعماله  
صاحب مؤلفات متعددة باللغة الفرنسية. ترجم بعض الكتب من العربية الى الفرنسية. اصدر واسهم في اصدار عدّة مجموعات ونشرات دورية. الى جانب اعماله الجامعية، خدم كاهنا مساعدا، في رعية سان سيفران بباريس واهتمّ برسالتها في الحيّ اللاتيني وبنشاطها الثقافي وبمنشوراتها. شارك في ندوات ومؤتمرات اقليمية ودولية، كلها تبحث في الشؤون العلمية المتعلقة بالحوار الاسلامي وبقضايا القدس وفلسطين. توفي يواكيم مبارك في فرنسا في 24 ايار 1995

![](https://libapps.s3.amazonaws.com/accounts/148280/images/terre_3.png)
##  Biography 
Born in Bejjeh – District of Jbeil on January 19, 1928, Michel Hayek went to the Jesuits’ _Université Saint-Joseph_ in Beirut, before continuing his higher education at the _Institut Catholique_ of Paris. 
Following his ordination to the priesthood on May 17, 1954 at the Saint-Joseph-des-Carmes Church in Paris, he went on to earn a PhD in Theology, Liturgy, Letters and Sociopolitical Sciences and taught at the _Institut Catholique_ of Paris from 1957 to 1993, as well as at the Lebanese University in Beirut and the Holy Spirit University of Kaslik (USEK). 
Father Hayek took part in the Second Vatican Council (1961-1965) as a theological advisor. As of 1972, he headed, in Lebanon’s name, several delegations to conferences abroad, such as the Lebanese delegation to the Islamic Conference in Algeria. 
Between 1965 and 2004, he delivered sermons at the Saint George Maronite Cathedral in Beirut during Lent and in 1983, he was appointed director of the international Catholic review _Communio_ , published in Arabic under the title _Al-Liqa’_. 
He died on Thursday, September 1, 2005. 
Father Michel Hayek was a true man of the Church, probably one of its most talented, educated, and cultured minds. In addition to his many talents, he was a polyglot known for his broad culture and prolificity. As a writer who tackled history, philosophy, theology, liturgy, literature, poetry, and anthropology among others, he left behind a rich collection of books, articles, studies, research, and poetry, some of which were published while others remain unpublished. 
ولد ميشال حايك في بلدة بجّه - قضاء جبيل في 19 كانون الثاني 1928. التحق بجامعة القديس يوسف للآباء اليسوعيين- بيروت، وبعدها بالمعهد الكاثوليكي – باريس، حيث حصّل دروسه الجامعية.
في 17 ايّار عام 1954، سيم كاهنا، في كنيسة مار يوسف للأباء الكرمليين في باريس حيث نال الدكتوراه في اللاهوت والليتورجيا، والآداب والعلوم الاجتماعية-السياسية، علّم في المعهد الكاثوليكي – باريس منذ سنة 1957 وحتى سنة 1993. كما علّم في الجامعة اللبنانية – بيروت، وفي جامعة الروح القدس-الكسليك.
شارك في المجتمع الفاتيكاني الثاني (1961-1965) بصفة مستشار لاهوتي. ومنذ سنة 1972 ترأس، بأسم لبنان، بعثات عديدة الى مؤتمرات في الخارج، منها البعثة اللبنانية الى المؤتمر الإسلامي في الجزائر وغيرها.
بين عامي 1965 و2004 ألقى ميشال حايك العظات من على منبر كاتدرائية القدّيس جرجس المارونية في بيروت، وذلك بمناسبة الصوم الكبير. وفي عام 1983 عيّن مديرا للمجلّة الكاثوليكية العالمية الصّادرة باللغة العربية تحت اسم اللقاء. Communio
توفّي ميشال حايك يوم الخميس الاوّل من ايلول 2005.
إنه رجل كنيسة بامتياز، لا بل كان من اكثر رجالاتها نبوغا وعلما وثقافة. متعدد المواهب، واسع الثقافة غزير الإنتاج. ويتقن الى هذا، العديد من اللّغات. كتب في التاريخ والفلسفة واللاهوت والليتورجيا والادب والشعر والانتروبولوجيا وغيرها. ترك مجموعة كبيرة من الكتب والمقالات والدراسات والأبحاث والأشعار، بعضها منشور وبعضها الآخر لم ينشر.
